### Completed related lifecycle correction

Independent review and executable regression found that `LayersLayerCore.Delete`
and `FinalizeLockedDelete` ignore a rejected owned-damage release and destroy
the descriptor, orphaning the allocation. `layers-portable-current-860.trx`
is 514 passed / one failed, solely
`DeleteAfterCompletedRefreshNeverOrphansRejectedOwnedDamageRelease`.
The fix transfers a rejected free to an allocation-free root-owned queue by
repurposing that same opaque block as a RetiredDamageRegion. Direct, locked
and prepared callback deletion preflight queue capacity and ownership before
commit; callback preparation is rechecked after Hooks. The descriptor is not
destroyed before handoff. Reset validates the entire bounded chain, retries
frees, and preserves the root until empty; Expunge refuses owned queue state.
Invalid flags, foreign/unregistered records and cycles fail before draining.
Arbitrary memory corruption after the final preflight is not claimed
recoverable; the defensive finalizer leaves the envelope allocated rather
than destroying its last descriptor. Ordinary rejected frees are covered.

The private root is now version 2, 48 bytes (previously v1/44), with its new
queue at offset 44. Old roots are rejected, not interpreted as the new layout.
Public SDK structures and private damage allocation size stay unchanged.

test path to exercise the graphics raster bridge; they are not, by themselves,
proof of parity against a stock Kickstart 3.1 ROM.

The [BeginUpdate autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/layers.library/BeginUpdate.html)
states that the layer is locked against layer-library changes during the
active update. The [EndUpdate autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/layers.library/EndUpdate.html)
states that EndUpdate restores normal ClipRects and unlocks it; FALSE retains
DamageList and TRUE clears it. The [Graphics Regions guide](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Graphics_Regions)
confirms ClipRegions are independent of DamageList and demonstrates changing
one between paused update pairs.

RastPort. The reader still consumes only the BitMap pointer and required bitmap
header fields; individual memory reads retain their own validity checks.

matrices), and two production-allocator lifecycle cases. Both matrices execute

Strict interior `ClearRectRegion` holes now preserve all FOUR nodes. The old
three-node implementation and test expectation deleted middle-right pixels.

`[0,0..2,3]`, `[0,4..0,5]`, `[2,4..2,5]`, `[0,6..2,10]`.

Reversed-source vertical Ts are also complete. The old Region is the narrow
stem and the input Rectangle the wider bar; the existing two-node transaction

adjacency checks use a strictly bounded endpoint and restore it on success
and gap routes, including retained-X equality at -32768/+32767.
The shared envelope preflight checks relative width/height before allocating;

Wait for the actual build session to finish before testing. The raw fallback
RTS may be copied locally by the branch linker, so its exported PC is not
the only valid decline address; verify the saved D0 frame, caller stack,
allocation log, and unchanged Region bytes as well.

## Execution rules

Every goal records:

- status (`pending`, `in progress`, `pass`, or `blocked` with evidence);
- exact V40 LVOs and structures in scope;
- portable-core work and host/native adapter work;
- timing/custom-chip obligations;
- focused tests, differential fixtures, and the ROM-overlay decision;
- an objective exit gate.

For each migrated LVO, complete the portable semantic method first, then the CopperStart register adapter, then tests, and only then add the LVO to the ROM-safe overlay allow-list. Unsupported ROM vectors retain their original bytes. No goal may broaden the overlay by implication.

### G15/G18 — screen-resource retirement follows successful teardown

Status: pass for the bounded close ownership rule (2026-08-28).

`CloseScreen` now invokes optional graphics-resource retirement only after
the actual Screen close reports success. A declined close retains the committed
View/ViewPort resource handoff for its owner to retry, and per-Screen tracking
prevents a successful foreign close from retiring a different Screen's
resources. Failed `OpenScreen` and `OpenScreenTagList` requests keep their
existing explicit rollback finalization before staged teardown. The complete
Intuition lifecycle family covers both rules.

Exit gate: `CopperStartIntuitionLifecycleTests` passes 35/35, including
OpenScreen and OpenScreenTagList resource commit/retirement and preparation
decline, declined- and foreign-close retention, and the open rollback cases.

### G03 — Text metrics

The text-vector register boundary follows the Kickstart field widths:
`Text`, `TextLength`, and `TextExtent` consume signed WORD counts, while
`TextFit` consumes UWORD `strLen`/width/height fields and signed WORD
`strDirection`. Negative signed counts remain unclaimed before guest-string
access; unrelated high-word residue is ignored. The portable core may retain
widened host counts for bounded internal arithmetic.

`TextFit` consumes the signed WORD `strDirection` field in D1; high-word
residue is ignored and the low-word direction is validated against the
documented forward/reverse values.

`TextLength` retains its separate classic result ABI: the portable core keeps
wider checked accumulation, while the register gateway publishes the signed
WORD result in D0.

Status: in progress (`TextLength`, `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent` now have portable semantics plus CopperStart gateway routing; the font gateway now selects the decoded TextFont from the RastPort rather than probing the RastPort address itself, fixed-cell and proportional metrics use the nominal cell advance when `CharSpace` is absent and the final TextFont glyph for out-of-range bytes, decoded metrics now apply signed per-character `TxSpacing` including the final character while preserving leading negative kerning, movement cells are included in `TextExtent`/`TextFit` horizontal bounds, explicit `TextExtent` constraints correctly take precedence over alternate width/height arguments, reverse `TextFit` is covered at both the pure and register boundaries using the documented end-anchored string pointer, `TextFit` now returns an empty extent when signed `TxSpacing` stalls or reverses the effective inter-glyph path, non-empty decoded metric calls reject null guest strings, and zero-length register `TextExtent`/`TextFit` calls accept a null A0 without dereference; all metric vectors preflight the complete 12-byte guest `TextExtent` result, `FontExtent` now scans the declared `LoChar..HiChar` range, derives width from complete `CharSpace + CharKern` movement with the normal/`FPF_REVPATH` directional clamp, includes per-glyph kerning in the returned bounding rectangle, and fails closed on movement overflow; decoded fonts now derive a negative default fixed-cell advance when `FPF_REVPATH` is set and `CharSpace` is absent; metric accumulation now fails closed before publishing when glyph advances or signed spacing exceed the 32-bit result contract; `SetFont` preflights the complete guest font/cache span before mutation; text-attribute matching is routed through the public `WeighTAMatch` vector and broader metric edge-case parity remains pending).

Implement `TextLength`, text extents, text fitting, font extents, and text-attribute matching. Test proportional fonts, fixed fonts, clipping-independent measurement, negative/zero lengths, and 16-bit coordinate limits.

G03 bounded constraint correction: `TextFit` now preserves the Kickstart rule
that an explicit `TextExtent` must include the current origin (`MinX <= 0 <=
MaxX`) before its rendered envelope and explicit width/height fields are
considered. A positive-kerning glyph wholly inside a positive-side rectangle
therefore returns an empty fit. The focused regression covers that rejection
while the alternate width/height path and all other bounds checks remain
unchanged ([TextFit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).

G03 prefix-envelope closeout: `TextFit` now rolls back the speculative
horizontal bounds of the first rejected glyph before publishing the accepted
prefix. A wide proportional second glyph can stop a two-character fit without
inflating the one-character `TextExtent` returned with the fit count.

G03 alternate-dimension range closeout (superseded by the 2026-08-18
alternate-constraint selection closeout below): when no explicit `TextExtent`
was supplied, the portable `TextFit` core rejected ULONG width/height values
above the documented `0..32767` range instead of silently narrowing them; the
register adapter preserved D0 for native/provider fallback. The current
implementation applies that range only to the alternate form; an explicit
extent ignores D2/D3.
([TextFit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).

G03 guest-word publication closeout: metric results now validate the complete
`TextExtent` envelope before writing it. UWORD width/height values may retain
their documented high-bit/REVPATH representation, while signed Rectangle
coordinates must fit `WORD`; an accumulated envelope outside those guest
fields leaves the destination untouched and remains available to the
native/provider path.

G03 shared-result rollback closeout (2026-08-29): `TextFit` and `FontExtent`
now share the late-WORD-failure regression with `TextExtent`. A failure while

G03 zero-length TextFit correction: the alternate `0..32767` dimension guard
is applied only when `strLen` is nonzero. A zero-length request publishes the
documented empty extent without dereferencing a string or treating unused

The same empty-request boundary skips an unreadable `constrainingExtent`; the
validated output structure remains the only guest result required for the

The text-vector register boundary follows the documented WORD/UWORD fields:

signed counts remain unclaimed before guest-string access, while high-word

### G06 — Pixels and lines

Status: in progress (portable planar pixels now reject missing declared bitplanes, preflight every selected plane before a multi-plane write, and roll back earlier plane bytes when a later selected-plane publication fails; `WritePixel` reports the documented `-1` outside-RastPort result instead of inheriting clipped drawing semantics, a zero write mask is a successful no-op across the shared planar primitives, Bresenham lines, rectangles, masks, PolyDraw, pen/mode/MaxPen attributes, classic line-pattern preshift/major-axis phase handling, documented line `INVERSVID` pattern inversion, `Move` fresh-segment `FRST_DOT` and native `linpatcnt=15` publication, connected-line endpoint consumption, explicit `ONE_DOT` one-sample-per-horizontal-raster enforcement, and first gateway migration implemented; `Draw` now snapshots its complete patterned raster traversal and RastPort line state, restoring both when a later pixel or state write fails, and clips off-raster samples while preserving the requested endpoint/line phase; `PolyDraw` preflight now models the implicit fresh `Move` and the same major-axis phase transition before probing every line destination; void Move/Draw/PolyDraw register calls now clear D0 after the portable operation; layered Draw now reaches an explicit layer-raster provider boundary, and the pure/core `Draw` and `PolyDraw` entries now decline layered RastPorts unless an explicit provider visibility predicate is present; the validated Layers projection now supplies its explicit visibility predicate to the supported line/rectangle/clear/scroll operations; line admission now limits the provider visibility predicate to in-bitmap logical cells and reuses the connected COMPLEMENT undo's prior visibility result; non-layered `DrawEllipse` now retains its documented no-clipping boundary while preserving complete per-plane preflight and rollback; remaining line clipping, layer damage, and draw-mode edge cases pending).

Implement pixel read/write, `Move`, `Draw`, `PolyDraw`, line patterns, line masks, draw modes, and clipping across planar bitmaps.

`SetRast` preflights the complete bitmap, snapshots selected plane storage, and restores the full raster if a later plane write fails before unconditionally writing the requested pen independent of active DrawMode; `ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, and `EraseRect` now preflight their complete clipped fill rectangles before publishing any rows, with `ClearScreen` probing both its text-line prefix and remaining rows before either span is published; `ScrollRaster` now preflights the clipped destination after its source snapshot and before publishing moved/cleared pixels; `EraseRect` now temporarily selects `BgPen` and routes the non-layered fill through `RectFill`, restoring `FgPen`, minterms, and line phase transactionally; `ScrollRasterBF` now applies the same `BgPen` backfill to vacated pixels while retaining its distinct full-displacement clear boundary; clipped scrolling snapshots source coordinates in the original logical rectangle before applying the delta, so off-raster bounds do not rebase the source image; the clear vectors, integer midpoint `DrawEllipse`, and snapshot-based non-layered scrolling have portable semantics and gateway tests; the void rectangle/ellipse/clear/scroll gateway family now clears D0 after dispatch; ### G08 — Areas, ellipses, and flood fill

The auxiliary descriptor boundary is now atomic: `InitArea` snapshots the complete `AreaInfo` envelope before publishing collector pointers, and `InitTmpRas` snapshots its descriptor before publishing the buffer and byte count. A rejected later field write restores the original guest bytes and leaves the vector available to a native/provider implementation. `InitTmpRas` validates only its descriptor envelope; its caller-owned backing span is consumed and checked by AreaEnd/Flood/Text. The register adapter now preserves that ownership rule for malformed/truncated `InitArea` and `InitTmpRas` calls instead of claiming successful no-ops.

Status: in progress (`DrawEllipse` now collects and preflights every clipped destination point before publishing its midpoint outline, and provider-backed ellipses skip off-raster outline points before visibility admission while non-layered calls retain their all-or-nothing no-clipping boundary; non-layered `Flood` now has portable semantics and register coverage; `InitArea`, `AreaMove`, and `AreaDraw` now record guarded classic 5-byte-per-vector state, `InitArea` publishes `AreaInfo` pointers after descriptor/arithmetic preflight without dereferencing caller-owned coordinate/flag storage, `AreaEllipse` records the documented two-vector center/radius item, `InitTmpRas` now publishes a validated guest temporary-raster descriptor, and non-layered `AreaEnd` now decodes/fills polygons and recorded ellipses with integer scanline semantics before resetting the collector; `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, and `AreaEllipse` preflight both coordinate and flag-table storage before mutating the guest collector, and their vector bytes plus pointer/count/first-point metadata now roll back atomically when a late guest write is rejected; `AreaEnd` now preflights the shape bounds and complete area-pattern envelope before any fill or outline write, and its collector reset has the same atomic metadata boundary; `Flood` now preflights the complete planar destination and area-pattern envelope before its connected-region traversal, and attached `TmpRas` storage is now cleared and consumed as the guest areafill mask or Flood visited bitmap; when the real graphics core sees an unset descriptor, both AreaEnd and Flood allocate temporary guest Chip rasters through the allocator, roll them back if their spans cannot be probed, and release them on all operation outcomes, while explicitly attached rasters remain caller-owned and strict; `AreaEnd` and seed-color `Flood` now consume the same RastPort area-pattern/JAM rules as `BltPattern`, and explicitly attached temporary rasters are rejected when undersized; AreaEnd now sizes an attached temporary raster from the largest decoded shape's 16-pixel-aligned bounding rectangle and clears/applies each local mask before the next shape, while Flood retains full-raster capacity; PolyDraw now preflights its complete guest point stream and every line destination before changing the RastPort or drawing a partial chain; area construction/fill and ellipse register calls now preserve their void D0 ABI; layered area/flood/ellipse vectors now explicitly fall back to the layer provider; layer damage, clipping, and complete profile/failure parity remain).

Implement area vectors, area filling, circles/ellipses, flood fill, temporary-raster exhaustion, and documented failure behavior.

G08 regression note: `AreaEnd` now has focused failure coverage proving that a late `AreaInfo` reset-field rejection rolls back the already-filled destination and preserves the recorded collector for retry.

Recent bounded G09 closeout: allocator-returned bitmap headers, contiguous
interleaved blocks, separate plane spans, and `AllocRaster`/`FreeRaster` ranges
now reject 32-bit guest-envelope wrap before any clear, pointer publication, or

G15 DBufInfo duplicate-allocation closeout (2026-08-29): `AllocDBufInfo`
restores its complete public envelope before releasing a duplicate address

G15 native DBufInfo envelope closeout (2026-08-29): the mapped 68k
`AllocDBufInfo` body now rejects ViewPort and RasInfo bases whose required

G15 RasInfo cardinality closeout: `MakeVPort` now requires a terminating
one-node RasInfo chain for single-playfield ViewPorts and exactly one

G16 RasInfo merge closeout: `MrgCop` now applies the same exact cardinality
validator to every linked ViewPort before invoking the copper merge backend.
A readable third DUALPF node returns the merge failure status with existing

G16 mapped-status parity closeout: the extra-`RasInfo` `MrgCop` guard now has
the same direct-host and mapped ROM-overlay proof. Both entry paths preserve

G17 display-chain cardinality closeout: `LoadView` now applies the same exact

G15 native extended-node overlay closeout: mapped `GfxNew` now publishes a

G15/G26/G27 `NextDisplayInfo` public-key closeout: the portable iterator now
returns the public ModeID key, including zero for the default lores record,

the zero-key first result, handle mapping, and complete PAL/NTSC enumeration;

G15/G18 mapped-enumeration closeout: the register gateway now has a complete
direct-versus-mapped continuation proof from `INVALID_ID` through all 66 native
OCS/ECS records and the final `INVALID_ID` terminator. The same fixture checks
that the private default-mode compatibility handle advances to the second

G15/G16 empty-teardown closeout: `FreeVPortCopLists` now treats a validated
ViewPort whose public `DspIns`, `SprIns`, `ClrIns`, and `UCopIns` links are

D0 clearing, and cycle preservation.

### G16 — Copper construction and merge

The temporary `ViewPortExtra` path marks `VPXF_FREE_ME`, rolls back on a failed status-aware build, is reclaimed only while still associated during `FreeVPortCopLists`, and is also reclaimed when a caller-owned association displaces it; `FreeVPortCopLists` honors the guest free-me marker for registry-owned ViewPortExtra nodes.)

Implement `MakeVPort`, `MrgCop`, copper-list allocation/freeing, CINIT/CMOVE/CWAIT/CEND/CBump semantics, and profile-specific PAL/NTSC/OCS/ECS rules.

G16 copper-source envelope closeout: the host `LoadView` resolver now checks

G16 native user-copper alignment closeout: `UCopperListInit` now requires an
even guest `UCopList` envelope, and every allocator-returned `CopList` and

The CopperStart standard-planar projection now validates every displayed bitplane row envelope after applying the RasInfo source offset. A nonzero but unmapped plane no longer produces a hardware copper list; `MakeVPort` reports `MVP_NO_DISPLAY` and leaves the existing DspIns/CPR links untouched. This guard is deliberately limited to OCS/ECS-compatible planar projection; CyberGraphX remains the owner of RTG scanout validation.

Synthetic `OpenScreen` defaults now select the active profile's standard height when `NewScreen.Height` is zero (`256` PAL, `200` NTSC), and double that default for Interlace before applying the profile-specific maximum. This removes the last PAL-default height leak from the standard host screen path.

Standard `OpenScreenTagList` now follows the same synthetic screen handoff and applies bounded `SA_Width`, `SA_Height`, `SA_Depth`, native PAL/NTSC or zero-monitor-part default `SA_DisplayID`, signed `SA_Left`/`SA_Top`, `SA_Title`, `SA_DClip` fallback geometry, profile-aware `SA_Overscan` defaults, legacy/default `DetailPen`/`BlockPen`, `SA_Pens`, explicit `SA_DetailPen`/`SA_BlockPen`, initial `SA_Colors` ColorSpec records, `SA_Colors32` interleaved RGB triplets reduced to OCS/ECS RGB4, and the classic `SA_ShowTitle`/`SA_Behind`/`SA_Quiet`/`SA_AutoScroll` flags over the legacy `NewScreen`/`ExtNewScreen` request. The owned Screen publishes the classic `CUSTOMSCREEN` type nibble, the `SA_ErrorCode` success word is initialized for accepted standard opens, the standard Intuition `ShowTitle` vector toggles the published `Screen.SHOWTITLE` bit, `GetScreenData` copies bounded prefixes for owned custom and standard-screen queries while projecting the requested Workbench/Public screen type, and `QueryOverscan` publishes profile-aware native PAL/NTSC rectangles; foreign screens and non-native display IDs remain available to native/provider ownership. The guest `Screen.DefaultTitle` and current `Screen.Title` pointers are published for legacy/tagged opens and `SetWindowTitles`; `STDSCREENWIDTH`/`STDSCREENHEIGHT` are treated as profile defaults. RTG display IDs and custom bitmaps remain unclaimed by this OCS/ECS path so the CyberGraphX/native scanout boundary retains ownership. Focused host coverage verifies Hires geometry/depth, PAL/NTSC/default-monitor mode selection, display-clip and overscan fallback, title-pointer lifecycle, pen precedence, both palette tag formats, screen flags, bounded screen-data copies, and QueryOverscan through the tag-list ABI (420 focused tests).

Lifecycle ownership closeout: malformed or non-standard `SA_BitMap` requests

The public-screen `SA_PubName`/`SA_PubSig`/`SA_PubTask` family follows the same

The tag-list adapter also rejects a non-null but unreadable legacy

the exact present-chain RasInfo rule before allocating replacement CPR/raw

G17 native LoadView envelope closeout: the smallest native assembling-view

G06/G07/G27 ScrollRaster boundary closeout: the mapped native jump-table path

ownership.

can select a monitor by name even when its supplied display ID carries a

G18 monitor-list closeout: each portable PAL/NTSC `MonitorSpec` now
initializes its embedded `DisplayInfoDataBase` as an empty Exec list (head to

instead of leaving the public list envelope all-zero. This preserves the

Native display-database handoff closeout: `GfxBase.DisplayInfoDataBase` is an
`APTR` pointer to the private native database object, unlike the embedded
`MonitorSpec.DisplayInfoDataBase` list. After the full native `GfxBase`
envelope is validated, the bridge transactionally allocates a private,
self-describing sidecar containing the native ModeID table and publishes the
APTR last. Existing Kickstart/provider pointers are preserved; allocation or
guest-write failure frees the sidecar and leaves the field unchanged. Overlay
disposal clears and frees only a sidecar still owned by the bridge. This closes
the bounded G18/G26 pointer/linkage slice without claiming undocumented ROM
database internals or CyberGraphX records.

The same native monitor publication now validates `GfxBase.MonitorList`'s
Exec `lh_Type` and `lh_Pad` bytes before linking. Non-zero metadata declines
without changing list links or retaining the provisional `MonitorSpec`;

G18 chipset ownership closeout: `BestModeIDA` now treats an explicit

G27 native-overlay lifecycle extension: the reversible manifest now also
covers scheduler/display-owned `WaitTOF`, `VBeamPos`, `WaitBOVP`,
`ScrollVPort`, `ChangeVPBitMap`, `AllocDBufInfo`, and `FreeDBufInfo`. Each has
an independent direct-vs-mapped proof, and every unbound or malformed decline
tail-chains through the captured original `JMP.L`; the graphics scaffold now
passes 564 tests. This extends the boundary without claiming copper merge,
layer clipping, RTG, or full native semantic parity.

G19/G26/G27 bitmap allocation overlay closeout: standard planar `AllocBitMap`
and `FreeBitMap` now have an independent direct-vs-mapped proof covering
clearable plane storage, compact guest geometry publication, allocator release,
D0, and cycles. A mapped allocation decline for a malformed friend or failed
allocation preserves the original native `JMP.L`; a second/foreign free is
likewise transparent, so RTG/CyberGraphX and foreign graphics instances retain
ownership.

G16/G26/G27 copper-overlay extension: `MakeVPort` and `MrgCop` now have
direct-vs-mapped parity through the status-aware CopperStart callbacks,
including guest status and cycle preservation. RTG-owned copper construction
tail-chains through the captured native vector, leaving CyberGraphX/provider
ownership intact; full copper instruction/timing parity remains open.

The copper teardown seam now follows the same proof boundary: `FreeVPortCopLists`
and `FreeCprList` are admitted for validated guest envelopes, with direct-vs-
mapped parity for viewport-link clearing, resource-owner callbacks, D0, and
cycles. RTG-owned viewport teardown and malformed `cprlist` envelopes decline
through the captured original `JMP.L`, so CyberGraphX/native ownership is not
swallowed by the overlay; allocator/hardware deallocation and complete copper
timing parity remain open.

The user-copper seam now extends that proof to `UCopperListInit`, `CMove`,
`CWait`, `CBump`, and registry-owned `FreeCopList`. The mapped jump table
matches direct CopperStart dispatch for allocator publication, six-byte
pseudo-instruction contents, pointer/count advancement, guest-link clearing,
allocator release, D0, and cycles. When the allocator is unavailable or the
registry/envelope is malformed, each admitted vector tail-chains to its
captured Kickstart target; `CEND` remains the macro-equivalent `CWait`/`CBump`
sequence, and hardware copper merge/timing semantics remain open.

The lifecycle capability seam now also admits `CalcIVG` and `SetChipRev`.
Validated standard View/ViewPort queries reach their explicit display/chipset
providers through both direct and mapped dispatch with matching scan-line or
capability results and unchanged cycles. RTG-owned CalcIVG calls and unbound
chip-revision requests tail-chain to the captured native vectors with D0 and
cycles preserved; profile-specific chipset timing and complete copper
publication remain open.

The display-query seam now admits `FindDisplayInfo`, `NextDisplayInfo`, and
`ModeNotAvailable` for the native OCS/ECS monitor families. Valid mode handles
and enumeration sentinels compare identically through direct and mapped
dispatch; `ModeNotAvailable` still reports `DI_AVAIL_NO_CHIPS` for recognized
but unsupported feature keys. Unknown monitor families remain unclaimed and
tail-chain to the captured native vector, preserving RTG/CyberGraphX ownership.

The monitor lifecycle seam now admits native PAL/NTSC `OpenMonitor` and
`CloseMonitor`. Successful opens publish the shared guest `MonitorSpec` and
increment its open count through direct and mapped dispatch; closes release it
only on the final reference. Unknown display IDs, foreign names, invalid
specifications, and allocator failures decline with D0/cycles intact and
tail-chain to the captured Kickstart/provider vector.

The mode-selection seam now admits validated native `BestModeIDA` and
`CoerceMode`. Direct and mapped calls return the same PAL/NTSC ModeID for
documented tag lists and standard-planar ViewPort geometry. Cyclic or
unreadable tag lists, malformed viewport chains, unsupported feature keys, and
RTG-owned ViewPorts decline before changing D0/cycles, leaving mode selection
to Kickstart or CyberGraphX.

The viewport-mode query now has the same proof boundary. Standard-planar
ViewPorts resolve their profile-aware native ModeID through direct and mapped
dispatch without changing cycles; an RTG-owned ViewPort remains transparent
and tail-chains to its captured provider vector with D0/cycles untouched.

The font-match unit now admits `WeighTAMatch` at its CopperSharp68k-compatible
`-804` slot. Valid guest `TextAttr` pairs return the same signed 15-bit match
weight through direct and mapped dispatch without touching guest memory or
cycles; tagged-DPI and malformed-chain behavior remains bounded by the shared
font backend.

The font-query seam now also admits `AskFont`. A validated RastPort/TextFont
pair copies the complete 8-byte guest `TextAttr` result through direct and
mapped dispatch, with transactional rollback on a late destination-byte
failure. Unreadable RastPort, TextFont, or output envelopes decline before
claiming the call and tail-chain through the captured original `JMP.L`, so
font-provider ownership is not swallowed by the overlay.

`SetFont` extends the same seam to RastPort cache publication. A decoded guest
`TextFont` and complete `RastPort` font/cache span produce identical font,
style, height, width, baseline, and spacing fields through direct and mapped
dispatch; truncated cache storage declines before mutation and tail-chains to
the captured native vector.

The native font-list seam now also admits `AddFont` and `RemFont`. These
vectors require the shared guest `TextFonts` backend, mutate the discovered
native `GfxBase` list after overlay rebinding, and leave the host compatibility
list untouched. An overlay created without that explicit backend declines both
vectors and tail-chains to the captured Kickstart/provider implementation.

`ExtendFont` and `StripFont` use the same explicit list boundary. The mapped
vectors are claimed only when the rebound guest list is present and validates
its bounded predecessor/successor chain; `ExtendFont` clones the caller's
bounded tag stream before allocating and publishing an owned
`TextFontExtension`, while `StripFont` detaches and frees only extensions
allocated by that backend. A missing or malformed list tail-chains before any
allocation or teardown, keeping native extension ownership intact.

The Region unit now follows the same ownership rule. `NewRegion` publishes a
guest Region allocated by the current graphics instance; mapped boolean and
teardown vectors may reclaim rectangle nodes only when their destination (and,
for region-to-region operations, source) belongs to that instance. Foreign or
native Regions tail-chain before any allocator call, while direct host calls
retain the existing guest-memory boolean layout and transactional rollback.

`AllocRaster`/`FreeRaster` now publish and consume instance-owned chip-memory
spans through the mapped table. The core records the requested width/height
alongside each allocation, so a repeated, mismatched, or foreign free remains
unclaimed and leaves the allocator untouched.

Pure ColorMap allocation and RGB4/RGB32 table operations now use the same
mapped ownership seam. `GetColorMap` creates an instance registry entry;
`FreeColorMap`, `GetRGB4`, `SetRGB4CM`, `SetRGB32CM`, and `GetRGB32` decline
foreign/native maps before touching their tables, while valid calls preserve
the guest high/low color words and cycle state.

The palette-sharing overlay extends that seam to `AttachPalExtra`,
`ObtainPen`, `ObtainBestPenA`, `ReleasePen`, and `FindColor`. Mapped calls may
allocate and mutate only an instance-owned ColorMap, while foreign maps and
malformed palette attachments tail-chain with D0/cycles intact. The guest
PaletteExtra free/shared lists, reference counts, nearest-color selection, and
viewport palette publication remain the same portable state exercised by the
direct register tests.

`OpenFont` now enumerates the selected guest list with bounded predecessor,
successor, cycle, and tail checks, so resident native fonts participate in the
same `WeighTAMatch` ordering as host-added nodes. The paired `CloseFont` path
tracks only fonts opened through this boundary and releases their accessor
word without removing untracked native residents; malformed attributes or
lists remain unclaimed.

The matcher now revalidates each resident candidate's common strike envelope
before scoring it, not only when this backend publishes a node through
`AddFont`. A structurally valid native list can therefore contain a node whose
`tf_CharData`/`tf_Modulo` was damaged by another owner without allowing
`OpenFont` to select it and leave a later `Text` dereference to fail; the
accessor word stays unchanged and a retry remains available to the resident
provider.

`GetDisplayInfoData` now joins that seam for recognized native handles and
`DTAG_DISP`/`DTAG_DIMS`/`DTAG_MNTR`/`DTAG_NAME` requests. Direct and mapped
dispatch compare the clipped guest chunk bytes, returned length, and cycles;
unknown tags and empty caller buffers retain their valid zero-length result.
Malformed non-empty recognized chunks decline before claiming the call, so the
captured Kickstart/provider vector retains ownership instead of observing a
partial or fabricated display record.

### Recent bounded closeout: native text-metric overlay

`TextExtent`, `FontExtent`, and fixed-cell `TextFit` are now admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos` after an independent host/native differential fixture proved the bounded guest-font metric path through both direct CopperStart dispatch and the mapped native jump table. The fixture compares the 12-byte guest extent result after each operation and D0/cycles; proportional text, rendering, and native font ownership remain separate parity gates.

`AskSoftStyle` and `SetSoftStyle` are now admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos` after the same direct-vs-mapped fixture proved intrinsic-style masking, byte-sized `AlgoStyle` publication, and D0/cycle parity. Algorithmic glyph rendering and extended provider-defined style bits remain separate gates.

`SetRPAttrsA` and `GetRPAttrsA` are now admitted for the pure pen/mode/mask/outline/MaxPen subset plus Font, SoftStyle, and DrawBounds tags after the direct-vs-mapped fixture proved bounded TagItem traversal, guest RastPort updates/queries, validated font/cache publication, non-layered bitmap bounds, MaxPen mask narrowing/publication, all-bits-set SoftStyle query results, and D0/cycle parity. Layered or malformed DrawBounds state still declines to the native/layers provider.

Native-overlay DrawBounds admission closeout: the reversible overlay now
validates a nonzero, word-aligned, non-wrapping Rectangle destination before
claiming a `GetRPAttrsA` tag list. An odd or 32-bit-wrapping destination remains
with the captured native vector without entering the compatibility adapter;
focused pure and mapped regressions preserve the original Rectangle bytes,
D0, cycles, and program counter.

Recent bounded closeouts: the real portable `Flood` core now allocates an unset-TmpRas visited bitmap through `IGraphicsAllocatorBackend`, probes the guest span before use, and frees the Chip scratch on both success and allocation/probe failure; allocator-backed `AreaEnd` now acquires, clears, consumes, and releases a guest Chip areafill-mask raster with rollback on an unprobeable span; and `InitRastPort` now publishes the guest-compatible standard font plus cached text metrics when the register adapter has a validated `DefaultFont` provider. Explicit guest temporary-raster descriptors remain strict and caller-owned.

Recent bounded closeouts: malformed guest `TextFont` headers are rejected unless both strike storage and modulo are readable, even when `tf_CharLoc` is non-null, and decoded glyph spans are rejected when they cross the declared modulo row; the Text/SetFont register boundary now preserves D0 and leaves malformed guest streams or truncated RastPort cache spans for native/font-provider fallback; layered Text/Draw now have an explicit `IGraphicsLayerRasterBackend` claim path with an end-to-end test for both provider success and declined-call preservation; patterned `Flood` treats AreaPt suppression as a destination-write decision while still traversing through those cells, preserving connected-region semantics; an attached `TmpRas` is now cleared and used as Flood's guest visited bitmap, while unset descriptors retain the bounded host fallback; multicolor area patterns now apply `INVERSVID` across every declared source plane before JAM2/COMPLEMENT selection; `AreaEnd` now fails closed instead of resetting its collector when the RastPort flags word is unreadable; non-layered `DrawEllipse` and `AreaEnd` now reject outlines/fills that would leave the bitmap instead of silently clipping them; allocator-backed `AreaEnd` now acquires a temporary guest Chip raster when `TmpRas` is unset, rolls back an unprobeable span, clears it before filling, and releases it on every result; the portable drawing gateway now preserves void-vector failure ownership for malformed `Move`, `Draw`, `PolyDraw`, area construction, `RectFill`, ellipse, scroll, clear, erase, and `SetRast` plans instead of claiming successful no-ops; timed `ChangeVPBitMap` now preserves malformed DBufInfo/bitmap validation status and leaves the guest association and cycle unchanged for provider fallback; non-null DBufInfo swaps now also require ownership by the current graphics-library instance, and a mapped-but-foreign envelope remains unclaimed with its D0, cycle, and RasInfo association unchanged; timed `ScrollVPort` and `WaitBOVP` now do the same for malformed viewport chains, and the host `GraphicsServices` fallback now leaves declined `WaitBOVP`/`ScrollVPort` calls' D0 and cycle state untouched instead of fabricating a compatibility object; all declined layered graphics vectors now retain that same end-to-end provider boundary instead of falling through to the synthetic host-object callback; the native overlay differential fixture now compares the approved safe subset through direct host dispatch and the mapped native jump table; V36 pixel-array gateways now validate an explicitly supplied temporary RastPort's layer-free one-row padded BitMap envelope, matching depth, aligned plane pointers, and complete temporary row storage before any planar write; `ChangeVPBitMap` now fails through the portable adapter for RTG-owned replacement or attached bitmaps, `FreeBitMap`/`GetBitMapAttr` likewise decline RTG addresses and foreign bitmap frees now fall through the registry boundary, `LoadView` declines a view whose linked viewport is already attached to an RTG bitmap, the shared non-layered RastPort gate now declines registered RTG ports across drawing/text/area/clear/scroll vectors, ROM-overlay `InitVPort` now preserves guarded host projection parity, the ROM overlay now forwards RTG `GetBitMapAttr` misses to its provider callback, untimed display waits now fall back to the scheduler-aware viewport-bottom callback, ownership-sensitive `FreeColorMap`, `FreeSprite`, `DisposeRegion`, `QBlit`, and `QBSBlit` now leave foreign, stale, or malformed objects unclaimed, so CyberGraphX/native providers retain a clean boundary; the layout-backed V39 `VideoControl` state family now has register coverage for chroma/bitplane keys, user-copper clipping, batch/list fields, border sprites, sprite resolutions, base words, chroma plane, full-palette mode, and allocation-owned chroma-pen state, with malformed out-of-range private values declined without publishing sidecar state; fixed-metric fallback `TextLength`/`AdvanceText` now interpret `TxSpacing` as signed guest state, preserve negative condensed/reverse-path advances, and distinguish a valid -1-pixel result from the failure sentinel; the GraphicsServices provider fallback now preserves the classic `GetBitMapAttr` selector-in-D0 ABI, with a regression covering the RTG/CyberGraphX boundary; `InitView` and `InitVPort` now also decline malformed/truncated guest envelopes at the register boundary, preserving D0/cycles and suppressing host ViewPort projection on invalid pointers; structure initialization now snapshots and restores the original guest bytes when an initializer write fails after preflight, preventing partially cleared View/ViewPort/RastPort/RasInfo envelopes.

### Recent bounded closeout

`FreeVPortCopLists` now snapshots the complete guest `ViewPort` envelope before clearing `DspIns`, `SprIns`, `ClrIns`, and `UCopIns`. If any guarded link write fails, the original guest bytes are restored and no native/resource teardown callback is invoked; the register adapter leaves D0 and cycles untouched so the native/provider path can handle the declined call.

### Recent bounded closeout: InitView origin

`InitView` now clears the guest `View` atomically and publishes the standard OCS/ECS origin (`DyOffset=$002C`, `DxOffset=$0081`) from shared layout constants. CopperStart's compatibility projection composes those View offsets with each ViewPort's relative offsets when emitting DIWSTRT/DIWSTOP, and a post-default write failure restores the original envelope. Focused pure, register, host, and copper-origin tests cover the new behavior.

### Recent bounded closeout: descriptor initialization atomicity

`InitBitMap`, `InitArea`, and `InitTmpRas` now snapshot their writable guest
descriptor envelopes after descriptor-range preflight. `InitBitMap` touches
only its eight-byte geometry/header prefix and never probes caller-owned
`Planes[]`; `InitArea` and `InitTmpRas` publish their caller-owned backing
pointer/count pairs without dereferencing those spans, while their geometry,
area, flood, text, and bitmap consumers retain operation-specific
capacity/readability checks. If a geometry, collector-pointer, buffer-pointer,
byte-count, or reused-plane write fails, the original bytes are restored and
the portable vector remains available for the native/provider fallback.
Regression tests inject failures at later writes to prove no partial guest
state is exposed.

The `SetOutlinePen` register gateway now applies the same ownership rule as the other RastPort setters: a malformed or failed guest update leaves D0 and cycles untouched for native/provider takeover, while a successful call publishes the documented previous outline pen.

`AskSoftStyle` now validates its guest font envelope before claiming the register vector without treating its valid all-ones result as failure. `TextLength` now carries an explicit success bit through both decoded-font and fixed-metric paths, so malformed guest streams decline cleanly while a valid signed width of `-1` remains observable.

The metric gateway now also preserves failure ownership for `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent`: a rejected text stream, font, or 12-byte result envelope leaves D0/cycles untouched, while valid zero-width/zero-fit results still claim normally.

The same metric boundary now rejects wrapped high guest addresses before any portable read: fixed-metric `TextLength` probes its cached width/spacing fields, and decoded `TextExtent`/`TextFit`/`FontExtent` calls preflight their font and complete result/constraint envelopes.

The synthetic `OpenScreenTagList` walker now rejects a tag-list address whose next eight-byte item would cross the 32-bit guest boundary, keeping malformed screen construction from wrapping into an unrelated low-memory tag stream.

The register `Text` gateway now uses the same guarded RastPort-font envelope as the metric/style vectors, so a high RastPort address cannot wrap its `tf` pointer read into low guest memory before the portable renderer claims the call.

The shared `TryReadBitmap` envelope now guards the complete public RastPort span, its `BitMap` pointer, and the bitmap header fields against 32-bit guest-address wrap.  The related bitmap-layout and allocated-bitmap readers use the same checked field/plane addresses for bitmap attributes, allocation friends, display validation, teardown, and bitmap utilities.  Pixel reads/writes, drawing primitives, patterned fills, flood/area paths, and planar blits all consume these helpers, so malformed high pointers now remain available to the native/provider path instead of aliasing low guest memory.  Focused pure coverage exercises truncated RastPorts, wrapped bitmap headers, and teardown wrap points.


The auxiliary initializer vectors now also preserve failure ownership at the register boundary: valid void calls clear D0 after a successful portable operation, while malformed or failed `InitRastPort`, `InitBitMap`, `InitArea`, and `InitTmpRas` calls leave D0/cycles untouched for native Kickstart or another provider. A selected compatibility-font initialization is no longer retried as a no-font success after a late guest write failure.

### Recent bounded closeout: linked ViewPort copper projection

The host `MrgCop` compatibility path now preflights the complete linked `ViewPort.Next` chain with a bounded cycle guard before allocating any new copper lists. Every linked viewport receives rebuilt `DspIns` state, while the first viewport's CPR wrapper remains active in the View; the same helper refreshes the full chain during display rethink/palette rebuilds. Cyclic or malformed chains leave the existing View CPR links untouched, and a later projection failure rolls back the complete guest chain transaction. The host register path reports `MCOP_NOP`, `MCOP_OK`, or `MCOP_NO_MEM` from the actual rebuild result; display rethink leaves the prior hardware publication in place when a non-empty chain cannot be rebuilt. Focused AmigaBoot memory tests cover multi-viewport projection, status propagation, rollback, display-list refresh, and cycle preservation. Full copper instruction merge and profile timing remain backend/native parity gates.

The host `LoadView` path now reports copper-source resolution through a status-aware display callback. Non-empty views commit `ActiView` and `_currentViewAddress` only after a CPR source is resolved and queued; a failed projection leaves the prior guest publication and active hardware stream intact. `LoadView(NULL)` supersedes an older queued list with a blanking request at the next frame boundary, and the host queue advances past any finalized presentation horizon before scheduling custom-register writes. Empty assembly views and CyberGraphX-owned front viewports retain their explicit paths, with focused AmigaBoot regressions covering failed resolution and queued-blank cancellation.

### Recent bounded closeout: ViewPort mode projection

The host compatibility copper builder now maps `ViewPort.Modes` feature flags to BPLCON0 controls for HAM (`HAM`), dual-playfield (`DPF`), and ECS superhires (`SHRES`) while preserving direct Hires/Interlace bits. Distinct dual-playfield `RasInfo` nodes now contribute bounded alternating plane pointers for each legal asymmetric depth distribution (1+1 through 3+3), publish the combined depth, and emit the two classic palette banks; shared-bitmap compatibility inputs retain their original total-depth representation. Focused AmigaBoot regressions cover HAM, shared-bitmap dual-playfield, distinct equal/asymmetric plane publication, dual-playfield palette-bank mapping, and Hires+SuperHires output values; full chipset-profile timing and copper merge parity remain open.

The synthetic Intuition screen handoff now preserves single-playfield HAM, Extra-Halfbrite, SuperHires, and Interlace mode bits, permits the SuperHires raster width and profile-aware interlace height, and publishes six guest bitplanes for HAM/EHB even when NewScreen leaves depth at zero. It also creates a shared-bitmap second `RasInfo` node for synthetic dual-playfield screens, so the existing graphics copper projection sees the complete two-node contract; distinct-playfield bitmap allocation remains a graphics-owned path. Focused OpenScreen regressions verify the HAM/EHB mode/depth fields, interlace geometry/BPLCON0 lace control, and the dual-playfield RasInfo chain plus BPLCON0/BPLCON2 output.

The synthetic Intuition `CloseScreen` path now claims only its own screen, blanks an active synthetic view through the same `LoadView(NULL)` frame boundary, frees compatibility copper wrappers, clears the viewport's published `DspIns` and the synthetic View's LOF/SHF CPR links, and drops reset-scoped backing handles so a later `OpenScreen` can publish fresh geometry. Foreign screen pointers remain available to native Intuition or another provider. Focused host coverage verifies the boolean result, `GfxBase->ActiView` clearing, guest-link teardown, and a second open with different dimensions.

The focused graphics/OpenScreen/MakeVPort regression filter now passes 420 tests after these lifecycle gates; the broader `AmigaBootMemoryTests` class remains at its known nine unrelated baseline failures (memory-list metadata, MorphOS exec compatibility, and RTG/CyberGraphX cases).

The same builder now translates the canonical `PlayfieldBitAssignment` flag to BPLCON2 PF2-first priority and emits an explicit zero for ordinary viewports. Focused mode coverage verifies both the PF2-first value and reset behavior when the next rebuild is not dual-playfield.

RasInfo `RxOffset` now projects both parts of hardware scrolling: coarse word offsets are applied to each playfield's bitplane pointers and residual pixel offsets are emitted as PF1/PF2 BPLCON1 delays, including a floor-division path for negative guest offsets. Distinct dual-playfield tests cover different fine delays for the two RasInfo nodes.

The same projection now emits independent BPL1MOD/BPL2MOD values for distinct dual-playfield bitmaps with different `BytesPerRow` values; a focused regression covers the two stride calculations.

Distinct dual-playfield construction now also clamps the visible height against the second bitmap's `Rows - RyOffset` envelope, with focused coverage for unequal playfield heights.

### Recent bounded closeout: user copper projection

`MakeVPort` now preflights a bounded `ViewPort.UCopIns` → `UCopList` → `CopList` chain and translates validated MOVE/WAIT pseudo-instructions into the compatibility raw copper list. Unsupported opcodes, count/pointer inconsistencies, cycles, unreadable guest ranges, and fixed-list capacity overflow fail closed and release the newly allocated raw list before the existing View/CPR links are replaced. Focused host regressions cover successful MOVE/WAIT projection plus malformed-chain and over-capacity rejection; exact Kickstart WAIT timing and full multi-list merge ordering remain native/display parity gates.

### Recent bounded closeout: ColorMap copper palette

`MakeVPort` now reads a valid guest `ViewPort.ColorMap` and `ColorTable` when emitting compatibility COLOR moves, preserving the RGB4 high-nibble words consumed by OCS/ECS hardware. Synthetic palettes retain explicit precedence, and malformed/foreign map storage falls back without claiming ownership. A focused AmigaBoot regression covers two-color guest palette projection; native AGA/RGB32 timing and palette ownership remain open.

Active standard-planar `SetRGB4`/`LoadRGB4` callbacks now request a bounded copper rebuild after the portable ColorMap commit; inactive chains and RTG scanout remain untouched. The host regression also covers an allocator-owned ColorMap update through the active View lifecycle.

`BestModeIDA` now treats a `TAG_MORE` item with a null continuation as the documented end of the tag list, matching the shared Exec tag-chain contract while retaining bounded cycle and malformed-pointer rejection.

`GetDisplayInfoData` now snapshots the complete clipped data chunk before publishing it and restores the original bytes if a later guest write fails, so monitor/display records cannot be partially exposed to a View or screen consumer.

`GetRGB32` now snapshots its complete requested output table before publishing expanded RGB values and restores it after a late entry failure, keeping ColorMap reads atomic for standard-planar screen consumers.

`LoadRGB4` and `LoadRGB32` now preflight the complete guest source table and every referenced ColorMap entry before publishing.  ColorMap high/low words are committed as one staged update with rollback on a late write failure; only a successful commit reaches the display palette callback.  `LoadRGB32` retains the Kickstart interleaved RGB triplet record format and terminator contract ([LoadRGB32 autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node02FB.html)).

`SetRGB4CM` and `SetRGB32CM` now use the same two-word transaction for direct ColorMap updates, restoring the prior high/low pair when a low-word guest write fails.  The viewport setters inherit this protection before they publish their host palette callback.

The host register adapter keeps `GetRGB4`'s ULONG RGB4 result in D0 and leaves the `0xFFFFFFFF` invalid-entry sentinel unclaimed.  A direct register regression now guards that result/cycle boundary alongside the mapped ColorMap overlay, so a future native 68k dispatch cannot accidentally replace the palette value with unrelated RastPort state.  The focused `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests` suite now passes 597 tests after this boundary was added.

`VideoControl` now fully precollects its bounded TAG chain, including `TAG_MORE`/`TAG_SKIP` continuations, before applying ColorMap or sidecar state.  A malformed later continuation therefore cannot leave an earlier tag published; a null `TAG_MORE` continuation is accepted as a clean end-of-list.

Classic VideoControl GET items are rewritten in-place to their SET/CLR form with
the queried value in `ti_Data`; the V40 `VC_*_Query` destinations are
range-preflighted as a group before setter tags run, so a truncated late query
cannot expose earlier state changes.

Region boolean publication and `ClearRegion` now snapshot the complete 12-byte guest `Region` header.  Allocation or late header-write failures restore the previous bounds and rectangle head before newly allocated nodes are released, preserving the old linked region for native/provider fallback.

G13 relative-layout closeout: published `RegionRectangle` bounds now use the
classic Region-relative coordinates from `graphics/regions.h`. The portable
boolean engine translates those nodes to absolute coordinates for its
coordinate-compression pass and re-encodes the result relative to the new
`Region.Bounds`; focused pure, register, and mapped-overlay coverage verifies
that geometry is unchanged while the guest node bytes match the native layout
([AROS OrRectRegion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/orrectregion.c), [AROS AndRectRegion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/andrectregion.c)).

`AndRectRegion` now clips and relinks the existing node list without allocating
replacement rectangles.  A focused allocator-exhaustion regression confirms
that the valid intersection still claims and publishes, while the shared
snapshot restores both header and node bytes if a later guest write fails.

The rectangle vectors now distinguish malformed storage from native
`IS_RECT_EVIL` input: Or/Xor/Clear return a successful no-op for inverted
bounds, while And clears the destination. Pure coverage exercises all four
branches and preserves the native/provider fallback for unreadable pointers
([AROS ClearRectRegion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/clearrectregion.c), [AROS XorRectRegion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/xorrectregion.c)).

The register adapter now keeps `AndRectRegion`'s native void ABI separate from
the portable helper status: successful calls clear D0, with a focused gateway
regression covering the zero result.

The mapped region lifecycle fixture now exercises `AndRectRegion` as well as
`OrRectRegion` and teardown, comparing the guest-relative node bytes, cycles,
and void D0 result through the native jump-table seam.

`ChangeVPBitMap` now restores the previous `RasInfo.BitMap` pointer if a guarded long write fails after publishing a prefix, so a failed screen-buffer swap cannot expose a half-written guest association.

RastPort pen/mode setters, `SetABPenDrMd`, `SetOutlinePen`, and `Move` now snapshot their prior fields and restore them when a later pattern, flags, or coordinate write fails.  The text/drawing state boundary therefore remains all-or-nothing for guarded guest-memory failures.

`SetBitmapPixel` now snapshots every selected planar byte before publishing a pixel and restores earlier planes if a later byte write fails.  `WritePixel` therefore cannot expose a partial depth-two-or-greater colour update at the portable memory boundary; the focused failure-injection regression uses the public status-bearing vector.

`Draw` now extends that transaction across the entire patterned line: it snapshots every touched selected-plane byte and the original `Flags`, pattern phase, and cursor fields, restoring them if a later pixel or RastPort-state write fails.  The focused failure-injection regression covers a later-plane failure after an earlier pixel has already published.

`Text` now applies the same transaction boundary across the complete rendered string: it snapshots every touched selected-plane byte and restores those bytes plus the original `CurrentX` when a later glyph, style pass, or final cursor write fails.  A focused failure-injection regression covers a later-plane failure after an earlier glyph pixel has published.

`PolyDraw` now extends the line transaction across the complete point chain: it snapshots all touched selected-plane bytes and the original cursor, pattern phase, and flags, restoring them if a later connected `Draw` fails.  The focused regression injects a later-plane failure after the first line has published.

`SetFont` now snapshots the existing guest font pointer and cached metric/style words, restoring the complete RastPort font state if a later cache write fails.  The focused regression fails the second byte of the final spacing word after the new pointer and earlier cache fields have been written.

`TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent` now snapshot the complete 12-byte `TextExtent` result before writing and restore it after any late word failure.  A focused `TextExtent` regression fails the second byte of the height word and verifies that no partial metric result is exposed.

Zero-length `TextExtent` now publishes the documented font-height envelope with `Width=0`, `MinX=0`, and `MaxX=-1`; algorithmic bold and italic styles cannot invent horizontal pixels for an empty string.  The pure and register gateway tests cover the empty result, including the null-A0 register call.

`SetRast` now snapshots every selected plane's complete row envelope and restores the full raster if a later pixel write fails.  The focused public-vector regression injects a later-plane failure after an earlier pixel has published.

`BltPattern`/`RectFill` now snapshot the clipped selected-plane byte region before patterned writes and restore it on a later pixel failure.  The focused `RectFill` regression exercises a later-plane fault after the first pixel has published.

`ClearScreen` now snapshots the selected plane storage across both its text-prefix and remaining-row fills, restoring the complete raster if the lower span fails after the prefix has published.  The focused regression injects that later-span failure.

`ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` now snapshot the clipped destination byte region after source capture and restore it if a later moved or vacated pixel write fails.  A focused overlap-scroll regression injects a later-plane failure and verifies the original destination remains intact.

`Flood` now snapshots the selected planar destination before its connected-region walk and restores the complete raster if a later seed-region write or temporary-raster operation fails.  A focused failure-injection regression covers a later-plane fault after an earlier flood pixel has published; successful calls retain the existing caller-owned or allocator-owned temporary-raster lifetime rules.

`DrawEllipse` now snapshots its bounded outline envelope after midpoint collection and restores it if a later planar write fails.  `AreaEnd` applies the same operation-level transaction across fill, optional outline, and collector reset, restoring the decoded shape bounds while leaving the recorded area available for retry on failure.

`BltClear` now snapshots its complete byte/row span and restores it on a late byte-write failure.  `BltBitMap` snapshots the clipped participating destination planes after source/destination capture and restores them if a later minterm write fails, preserving overlap-safe source semantics and the status-bearing failure boundary.

`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` now snapshots its clipped participating destination planes after source, destination, and mask capture, restoring them when a later masked minterm write fails.  `BltTemplate` applies the same transaction around its clipped template destination after complete template/plane preflight.  Focused regressions cover later-plane failures in both paths.

The V36 pixel-array family now snapshots logical output-array bytes for `ReadPixelArray8` and clipped participating planar storage for `WritePixelArray8`/`WriteChunkyPixels`, restoring the original destination when a later array or plane write fails.  Focused regressions cover both guest-array and multi-plane raster rollback.

`BitMapScale` now snapshots the clipped destination planes and the prior derived extent words before publishing its scaled result, restoring both if a later pixel or extent write fails.  The focused regression injects a late plane fault after an earlier scaled pixel and verifies the original geometry and raster remain available to a retry.

User-copper `CMove` and `CWait` now snapshot their six-byte pseudo-instruction before publishing opcode/register/value words, restoring it if a later word write fails.  This keeps intermediate copper construction atomic at the guest boundary while `CBump`/allocation and hardware merge remain explicit backend responsibilities.

`CBump` now snapshots the current `CopList` before advancing `CopPtr` and `Count`, restoring both fields if the second publication fails.  Full-block rollover snapshots both the current block and owner `UCopList` links, restoring them and freeing the speculative successor if either link write fails; existing-block owner relinks receive the same guard.  Focused regressions cover late count and late owner-link failures.

`FreeCopList` now snapshots the caller-owned `UCopList` before clearing `FirstCopList` and `CopList`, restoring both links and retaining the registry/allocation when the second clear fails.  `UCopperListInit` snapshots the caller envelope before allocation and publication, restoring it and freeing the internal block on a late clear/link failure so the same owner can retry.

The guest `GfxBase.TextFonts` list now snapshots its header, participating font links/flags, and neighboring node links around `AddFont`/`RemFont`.  A late Exec-style link or removed-flag write restores the complete list mutation, leaving the font registration retryable; focused regressions cover both insertion and one-node removal failures.

The same guest font-list backend now snapshots the `TextFonts`/`DefaultFont` image envelope during initialization and `SetDefaultFont`, restoring it on a late long-word failure before the host/native image is exposed.

`GraphicsMemoryFontBackend.TryAdd` now publishes a zeroed accessor word before asking the guest list backend to insert the node, restoring the prior accessor count if insertion declines.  This keeps the host registration sidecar and guest `TextFonts` list coherent across the cross-layer handoff.

`AllocDBufInfo` now snapshots the allocator-owned public DBufInfo envelope before clearing it and publishing the two Exec message lengths.  A late message-word failure restores the original guest bytes before freeing the allocation, keeping the screen/view double-buffer boundary retryable.

`AskFont` now snapshots the complete guest `TextAttr` result envelope after preflight and restores it if a later name/size/style/flag write fails.  Font attribute queries therefore retain the same all-or-nothing guest ABI as the text metric vectors.

Owned `TextFontExtension` publication now snapshots the original `tf_Extension` pointer and `tf_Style`.  `ExtendFont` restores both if the final style publication fails, and `StripFont` restores both while retaining ownership when either detach field fails, so both operations remain retryable without leaking or detaching foreign extensions.

`CloseFont` now restores the original `tf_Accessors` word when its decrement write fails after a partial byte publication, preserving removed/open registration state for a retry.

`AllocBitMap` now snapshots the newly allocated public `BitMap` envelope and restores it before releasing the object on every later header, plane-allocation, plane-link, or displayable-flag failure.  Standard planar bitmap allocation therefore cannot leak a partial geometry or plane-pointer record to a native/provider retry.

`MoveSprite` now snapshots the public `SimpleSprite` envelope and attached POS/CTL words before publishing coordinates and regenerated hardware words; `ChangeSprite` restores the original image pointer after a late long-write failure.  The optional display backend is called only after the guest state commits, and focused regressions cover both late-write paths.

`ChangeExtSpriteA` now snapshots and restores the complete public `ExtSprite` envelope when any of its seven field publications fails late, keeping image, geometry, sprite number, width, and flags coherent for retry.

`AddVSprite` and `RemVSprite` now snapshot all four reciprocal GELS links and restore the original topology if a late link-byte write fails.  Focused regressions cover both insertion and removal failure paths.

`InitGels` now snapshots both sentinel `VSprite` envelopes, the caller-owned `GelsInfo`, and the optional collision-vector word before clearing or publishing defaults; a late failure restores the complete GELS owner state.

`SortGList` now snapshots every reciprocal link it rewrites and restores the previous stable ordering if any late link publication fails.

`InitMasks` now snapshots the complete border and collision-mask spans before publishing computed words, restoring both destinations on a late failure.

`SetCollision` now snapshots the selected collision routine entry and restores the previous long word when a late write fails.

`AddBob` now publishes Bob flags, VSprite flags, and the VSprite owner pointer transactionally, restoring all three fields on a late failure before list insertion.

`RemIBob` now snapshots reciprocal VSprite links and Bob owner fields before unlinking, restoring them if the final Bob-state publication fails after background restoration.

`GetGBuffers` now snapshots every public Bob/VSprite buffer pointer before clearing or publishing allocator-owned storage, restoring the complete pointer envelope before freeing storage after any late clear, pointer, or DBufPacket write failure. `InitGMasks` likewise restores every Bob owner link it published if a later mask write fails. `FreeGBuffers` now snapshots owned pointers before teardown and keeps the registry/storage live when a late clear fails, so a retry cannot observe stale pointers to freed memory.

`AddAnimOb` now snapshots the AnimOb chain and active-component timer/owner fields before publication, restoring both envelopes when a late link, timer, or Bob insertion fails.

`Animate` now preflights and snapshots the complete AnimOb position/velocity/clock word set before advancing it, restoring the old state if any late word publication fails.

`Animate` component publication now snapshots the active timer, VSprite coordinates, and Bob flags, restoring all four guest fields when a late coordinate or flag write fails; sequence switching remains an explicitly separate transaction gate.

Sequence switching now snapshots both AnimComp reciprocal links and the old Bob/VSprite envelope before removal, restoring the active frame if AnimOb head publication or replacement-Bob insertion fails; raster background restoration remains the explicit committed side effect.

The host register adapter now propagates portable `LoadView` validation failure as an unclaimed call, preserving D0/cycles and the previously published view for native Kickstart or another display provider; valid calls retain the documented void ABI.

Palette void vectors (`SetRGB4CM`, `SetRGB32CM`, `GetRGB32`, `LoadRGB4`, `LoadRGB32`, `SetRGB4`, and `SetRGB32`) now propagate portable ColorMap/viewport validation failure as an unclaimed call instead of fabricating success; valid calls retain their documented D0/cycle behavior.

The focused graphics/architecture/corpus subset now passes 423 tests; the targeted host MakeVPort/MrgCop plus active-palette and LoadView lifecycle set passes 26 tests, including the user-copper and ColorMap projections plus malformed/capacity guards. The broader plan remains open for the explicitly listed native/display/provider parity gates.

The latest text-metric/style-envelope, ViewPortExtra lifecycle, and native RastPort tag-boundary regressions raise that focused subset to 423 passing tests; native overlay eligibility and the broader display/provider gates remain unchanged.

The current CopperStart lifecycle follow-up adds non-head `MakeVPort` chain preservation, `MrgCop` status/rollback, and failed-rethink publication regressions; replacement `MakeVPort` CPR wrappers are now allocated before retiring the prior wrapper, with raw-list cleanup and `MVP_NO_DISPLAY` on program-memory exhaustion. The compatibility `MrgCop` path now returns wrapper addresses to its transactional registry and appends later per-viewport streams to the first active raw list with bounded vertical waits; an over-capacity merge returns `MCOP_NO_MEM` and rolls back every speculative wrapper/raw allocation. The targeted host lifecycle set remains green. The broader `AmigaBootMemoryTests` class still carries nine unrelated baseline failures outside this change.

Host `GraphicsServices` no longer invokes its legacy Text/SetFont compatibility helpers after the portable adapter declines. Valid decoded-font and layer-provider calls still claim through their explicit paths; malformed guest font/RastPort state remains available to native Kickstart or another provider.

The same ownership guard now covers the legacy `LoadView` callback: after a portable decline, `GraphicsServices` forwards only a view whose linked viewport is positively identified as CyberGraphX/RTG-owned. A malformed standard view remains unclaimed with D0, cycles, and the prior display publication unchanged, while an RTG view still reaches the provider callback.

The legacy `LoadRGB4`/`SetRGB4` callbacks use the same narrow viewport classifier. Malformed standard palette state now remains available to native Kickstart or another provider instead of receiving a synthetic D0-clear success; an explicitly RTG-owned viewport retains its provider handoff.

`GraphicsServices` applies that split to `ChangeVPBitMap` as well: malformed standard viewport/bitmap/DBufInfo state is left untouched for native ownership, while an RTG replacement or currently attached RTG bitmap is forwarded to the provider callback.

Layered/RTG `BltBitMap`, `ClipBlit`, and `BltBitMapRastPort` declines now use the same explicit provider classification. Invalid standard endpoints remain unclaimed, while layer or RTG ownership reaches the corresponding host callback with the classic D0/cycle state preserved.

The same boundary now covers `CloseFont`: a malformed or foreign guest `TextFont` declined by the portable lifecycle registry is no longer converted into a synthetic D0-clear success by the host compatibility switch, so native Kickstart or a font provider retains ownership of the call.

`GetBitMapAttr` now has an explicit portable validation result at the register boundary. Unknown selectors on a readable standard bitmap still return zero, while an unreadable or foreign envelope is left unclaimed; only an RTG-owned bitmap is forwarded to the provider callback, including through the narrow ROM-overlay seam.

The pure RastPort getters (`GetAPen`, `GetBPen`, `GetDrMd`, and `GetOutlinePen`) now preserve the same result distinction: a readable byte returns its classic value, while an unreadable RastPort leaves D0/cycles unchanged for native/provider ownership.

Host view, viewport, and RastPort ownership classifiers now reject address arithmetic that would wrap at the 32-bit guest boundary. A high malformed pointer cannot alias low memory into a synthetic RTG/layer claim, with a focused regression covering the provider handoff path.

The CopperStart display adapter now exposes a status-aware `VBeamPos` boundary. A configured scheduler beam callback still returns the cycle-sampled position, while an unbound host leaves D0 and cycles untouched so a native Kickstart or provider implementation can claim the vector.

View publication now uses the same explicit ownership boundary: the portable core validates the guest View first, then the CopperStart display adapter claims `LoadView` only when its host callback is present. A host with no display publication backend leaves the void vector's D0/cycle state untouched, while the production scheduler-backed AmigaBoot path retains the documented publication behavior.

The frame wait follows the same rule. `WaitTOF` is claimed only when the scheduler wait callback is present; an unbound host leaves the guest cycle and D0 untouched for native/provider ownership, while the AmigaBoot path continues to advance the canonical frame cycle.

The production AmigaBoot frame callback now derives that boundary from the active bus beam clock, including NTSC/ECS field geometry, instead of applying the PAL constant. Synthetic VBlank frame ticks, queued copper publication, title redraw waits, and the no-input `WaitPort` compatibility wait use the same profile-aware beam boundaries. Focused A500+ ECS NTSC graphics-gateway regressions compare `WaitTOF` and mid-frame `LoadView` publication with `GetNextFrameStartCycle` and reject the old PAL result.

The focused graphics/architecture and profile-aware screen/lifecycle selection now passes 434 tests, including PAL and NTSC/ECS `WaitTOF`, `LoadView`, synthetic VBlank, queued copper, and idle `WaitPort` boundaries. The broader graphics/lifecycle/copper filter now passes 451 tests, including equal-depth and asymmetric distinct dual-playfield `MakeVPort` projection plus palette-bank coverage and synthetic HAM/EHB, Interlace, SuperHires, and shared dual-playfield OpenScreen handoff coverage.

The synthetic `OpenScreenTagList` bridge now parses explicit and extended tag chains transactionally: missing terminators, unmapped/cross-boundary items, bounded-walk exhaustion, and cyclic `TAG_MORE`/`TAG_SKIP` paths return a clean null screen before legacy geometry or `SA_ErrorCode` state is applied. Empty/null lists and null `TAG_MORE` continuations remain valid, while RTG mode selection is still left to CyberGraphX.

The combined portable graphics plus OpenScreen/CloseScreen/LoadView/QueryOverscan verification now passes 425 tests after the AreaInfo and tag-chain guards. The complete `AmigaBootMemoryTests` class remains at 123 passing with the nine unrelated memory/RTG baseline failures listed in the existing ledger.

`WaitBOVP`, `ScrollVPort`, and `ChangeVPBitMap` now require an explicit host presentation boundary after guest validation. A valid viewport operation is left unclaimed when no vertical-blank or display-rebuild owner is connected; DBufInfo scheduling is also accepted as the explicit bitmap-switch owner when present.

The portable Text renderer now treats cursor, glyph-cell, underline, and bold-smear coordinate arithmetic as a guarded 32-bit guest contract. An oversized decoded advance or long text stream fails and restores the original current-X instead of wrapping into an unrelated raster address; the focused regression exercises a 65,540-character stream with the maximum signed CharSpace.

The RastPort state boundary now applies the same checked 32-bit address rule to scalar getters/setters and cursor updates. `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`, `SetABPenDrMd`, `SetWriteMask`, `SetMaxPen`, `SetOutlinePen`, `Move`, and the matching getters reject high guest pointers whose field or line-pattern phase would wrap into low memory; pure and register-level coverage confirms the low aliases remain untouched and D0 stays available for native/provider fallback.

Text metric helpers now enforce that envelope in the portable core as well: `TextLength`, `TextFit`, `TextExtent`, and `SetFont` read RastPort font/cache fields through checked addresses, and `TextFit` preflights its complete constraint `TextExtent` before reading it. A pure high-pointer regression plus the CopperStart `TextFit` gateway proves wrapped RastPort/constraint addresses remain unclaimed.

The AreaInfo collector now applies the same checked 32-bit boundary to its RastPort link and advancing vector/flag pointers. `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, and `AreaEllipse` reject a high `rp_AreaInfo` address or a vector-table advance that would wrap before reading or publishing any collector state; the pure and CopperStart regressions preserve the low alias and D0 for native/provider fallback. G08 still remains open for broader area/flood edge and clipping parity.

G08 bounded closeout: `AreaEnd` now treats an already-empty `AreaInfo` as a successful no-op, without requiring a resident bitmap or temporary raster. Non-empty streams retain the guarded decode, destination preflight, fill transaction, and collector-reset failure boundary; pure and CopperStart tests cover both the empty success and the post-fill repeat call.

G08 temporary-raster envelope closeout: attached `TmpRas` descriptors now
require an even, fully readable guest structure before `AreaEnd` or `Flood`
consumes their storage. Odd or wrapped descriptors decline before clearing
scratch or mutating the destination bitmap; the existing caller-owned,
allocator-backed, and unset-descriptor paths remain unchanged. A CopperStart
`AreaEnd` regression also preserves D0 and the recorded collector when an odd
descriptor is presented, raising the focused scaffold to 608 tests.

G07/G08 native temporary-raster alignment closeout: allocator-backed `AreaEnd`
and `Flood` scratch rasters now require even, non-null Chip addresses before
their spans are probed or cleared. Odd successful addresses are released just
like provisional false-status spans; no `TmpRas` or planar destination state is
published. Focused coverage proves `AreaEnd` declines before drawing and frees
the odd span, while explicitly attached `TmpRas` remains caller-owned through
its existing envelope validation path.

G09 bounded note: the planar `BltBitMap`/`ClipBlit` header reader now rejects odd guest `BitMap` addresses before reading word fields or plane links. Pure and CopperStart regressions preserve the destination and D0 for a malformed odd header; displayable/RTG ownership and the remaining bitmap copy/synchronization helpers stay open.

G10/G11 temporary-workspace closeout: overlapping `BltBitMap` now rejects and
releases an allocator-backed `TempA` whose even scan-line span would wrap the
32-bit guest address space. The workspace is checked for word alignment and a
representable span before the blit snapshots or mutates any planar byte;
