caller-supplied `TempA` retains its existing alignment/readability boundary.

G09 RastPort-link closeout: the shared planar `RastPort.BitMap` reader now
applies the same even-address rule used by the blit header reader. A host
memory model can expose bytes at an odd linked structure, but the portable
path declines before a raster primitive reads or writes it, preserving the
native 68k address-error/provider boundary.

G19 bounded note: the explicit V36 pixel-array temporary-RastPort validator now applies the same word-alignment rule to its guest `BitMap` header. An odd temporary header is declined before any destination plane write; the null temporary-RastPort conversion path remains unchanged.

G06/G07 bounded note: non-layered `RectFill` now has focused coverage for a touched planar byte span whose first byte is readable but whose final byte crosses the guest boundary. The region preflight declines before either selected plane is changed; layered clipping and damage remain explicit provider work.

G06/G07 address-boundary note: planar region preflight and transaction snapshots now use inclusive byte-span end checks. A row whose final byte is exactly `0xFFFFFFFF` is accepted, while any span beyond the 32-bit guest address space is rejected before mutation; sparse guest-memory coverage exercises the high-address `RectFill` path.

G19 aliasing note: `WritePixelLine8`/`WritePixelArray8` now stage the complete logical source-byte set before publishing planar destination pixels. An array overlapping the destination bitmap therefore produces the same result as the documented temporary-RastPort conversion instead of allowing an early plane write to change later source samples.

G19 envelope note: pixel-array preflight now validates the complete padded `RASSIZE` row envelope, not only logical pixels. A readable first byte with truncated padding is declined before any planar mutation, while a row ending exactly at `0xFFFFFFFF` remains valid.

G19 result-count note: V36 pixel-line/array helpers now return the requested logical pixel count even when their planar destination clips samples outside the RastPort, matching the documented API result while retaining deterministic zero-fill/read-skip clipping.

Provider-boundary closeout: the portable register adapter now declines RTG/CyberGraphX-owned ViewPorts before palette, mode, copper, frame-wait, scroll, or bitmap-association paths can claim them. `GraphicsServices` forwards declined `MakeVPort`/`MrgCop` calls only when the linked View/ViewPort is positively identified as RTG-owned; malformed standard structures retain their portable status or remain available to native Kickstart. Focused host coverage verifies RTG forwarding and malformed-state isolation.

G14 transaction closeout: `VideoControl` now stages every guest-memory write through a read-your-writes transaction and restores ColorMap bytes, in-place GET TagItems, external query destinations, allocation-owned sidecars, and the extended-node association registry when a later tag or commit write fails. Pure regressions cover unsupported later tags, rewritten GET state, malformed query outputs, and injected late-write failure. `AttachPalExtra` now publishes the public `SignalSemaphore` prefix (`NT_SIGNALSEM`, empty wait `MinList`, zero owner/nesting/queue state), WORD reference counts, and linked WORD free/shared allocation lists; portable ColorMap/pen/VideoControl calls serialize the matching allocation on a host lock. Exec task ownership, scheduler-visible contention, ROM color metric/free-entry scaling, and native palette publication remain open.

## Required test layers

Each behavioral goal adds:

1. pure portable tests using fake big-endian memory and deterministic backends;
2. register-level CopperStart gateway tests;
3. profile-specific hardware/timing tests for any custom-chip effect;
4. ROM-overlay tests proving unlisted vectors retain original bytes;
5. differential fixtures against documented Kickstart 3.1 behavior where available.

The foundation command set is:

```powershell
dotnet build .\CopperMod.Amiga.Emulator\CopperMod.Amiga.Emulator.csproj
dotnet test .\CopperMod.Amiga.Tests\CopperMod.Amiga.Tests.csproj --filter "GraphicsLibraryPortable|Architecture"
```

After any scheduler, bus, DMA, or custom-register integration goal, run the full `CopperMod.Amiga.Tests` project and the relevant cycle-accuracy filters.

G14 update: portable `ObtainBestPenA` now searches already-shared entries (leaving unallocated ColorMap slots to the allocation fallback), applies checked free-entry-scaled tolerance, and chooses a fresh pen or shares the nearest occupied entry with pure and register-level regression coverage. A newly claimed pen now publishes its viewport RGB4 callback only after guest ColorMap/PaletteExtra state commits; shared references and `PEN_NO_SETCOLOR` remain side-effect free. PaletteExtra free/shared WORD chains now preserve the native head-removal, shared-head insertion, and free-head reinsertion order, including non-sharable exclusive entries staying outside the published lists. The remaining G14 parity gates are ROM error-metric calibration, native sidecar/list corruption behavior, Exec task ownership/contention, native palette publication beyond the callback seam, and scheduler-visible OCS/ECS/AGA timing; CyberGraphX/RTG palette ownership remains outside this implementation.

G14 precision update: `ObtainBestPenA` now uses the public `PRECISION_EXACT=-1`, `PRECISION_IMAGE=0`, `PRECISION_ICON=16`, and `PRECISION_GUI=32` values as the native squared-error precision term. The acceptance test is integral and overflow-guarded: `bestDistance * pe_NFree <= precision² * pe_SharableColors`, where `pe_SharableColors` is the highest sharable index. Exact precision rejects every non-zero distance; with no free sharable entries, non-exact modes retain the nearest shared pen as the native free-entry relaxation requires. ROM-specific color-distance calibration and scheduler-visible semaphore behavior remain explicit parity gates.

G14 color-table update: `SetRGB4CM` and `SetRGB32CM` now preserve the classic high `ColorTable` nibble while replacing RGB data, and RGB4 writes clear the low-color table as native graphics.library does. This keeps reserved genlock/alpha state stable across portable palette edits and is covered by the pure ColorMap layout regression.

The same reserved-nibble rule now applies to staged `LoadRGB4` and `LoadRGB32` table commits, so bulk palette loads cannot erase legacy high-nibble state while updating the RGB planes.

Pen acquisition now consumes the guest-compatible `pe_FirstFree` head for any-entry requests and walks `pe_FirstShared` for duplicate-color reuse. This preserves the native LIFO allocation policy and shared-list tie order instead of silently preferring the lowest numeric pen.

`FindColor(..., maxPen=-1)` now applies the attached `PaletteExtra` sharable span, while an explicit non-negative `maxPen` still searches the requested full ColorMap range. This matches the documented renderable-pen distinction for screens with sprite/pointer entries beyond the planar depth ([FindColor autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/FindColor)).

G15/G17 lifecycle update: the portable `LoadView` boundary now retains the
active guest View pointer and treats a repeated request for that same pointer
as a successful no-op when the validated View/ViewPort guest chain is
unchanged, matching the native display hand-off rule. A changed View (including
`NULL` for blanking) still crosses the host publication boundary, and a failed
status-aware publication leaves the previous active pointer retryable. Pure
coverage verifies that repeated unchanged active and blank-view requests do not
rebuild or requeue the display stream, while a caller edit to the active CPR
links is republished. The first blank-view request is still published once so
an initially unknown hardware state is explicitly cleared before subsequent
blank retries become idempotent.

The `LoadView` no-op guard now consults the status adapter's publication
capability before suppressing a repeated request. An unbound host adapter
therefore still declines even `LoadView(NULL)`, preserving D0/cycle state for
native/provider fallback, while a connected host observes the native
idempotent transition.

G16/G17 active-view update: CopperStart `MrgCop` now queues the newly rebuilt
copper source immediately when the merged `View` is already active. Inactive
Views retain preparation-only behavior and are published by `LoadView`; a
failed chain rebuild still leaves the existing guest and hardware publication
untouched.

The same bounded rebuild now honors `VP_HIDE`: hidden ViewPorts remain part of
the validated guest chain but are excluded from copper projection. An
all-hidden chain returns `MCOP_NOP` without replacing the View's existing CPR
links, matching the native merge contract.

When a hidden node is the guest chain head, the rebuild temporarily exposes the
first visible node only while constructing the compatibility CPR wrapper. The
original `ViewPort` chain head is restored before success is published, so the
guest chain remains intact while the active CPR starts at the first visible
display.

G18 monitor-capability closeout: `OpenMonitor(displayId)` now applies the same
ECS display-register availability used by `ModeNotAvailable`, `BestModeIDA`,
and `CoerceMode`. An OCS host declines an ECS SuperHires mode ID, while an
explicit named PAL/NTSC monitor still opens its native monitor specification.

G07/G11 draw-mode closeout: the portable area-pattern matrix now matches the
native JAM rules. Positive one-bit patterns act as JAM1 foreground stencils,
`COMPLEMENT|JAM2` inverts the whole selected region, and a solid inverse-video
fill is a JAM1 no-op or a JAM2 BPen fill. Focused pure coverage exercises all
three boundaries.

G10/G11 ABI closeout: `BltPattern` now consumes only the documented D4 WORD
mask byte count at the register boundary. Residue in D4's upper half cannot
change the guest mask stride or force a valid stencil into native/provider
fallback; focused host coverage exercises a valid low-word stride with a
nonzero high-word residue.

G10 temporary-workspace closeout: overlapping `BltBitMap` calls with a null
`TempA` now obtain one source-stride scan line from the explicit Chip
allocator boundary and release it on every operation outcome. A caller-owned
workspace still requires the documented aligned/readable span, while an
allocator that returns a provisional address with a false status is released
before the vector declines. Focused pure coverage proves both successful
allocation/free and provisional-allocation rollback
([BltBitMap autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/BltBitMap)).

G07 clear/erase closeout: the shared `FillRectangle` writer now traverses only
the clipped drawable rectangle that it preflighted. Extreme signed-WORD
off-screen bounds therefore remain successful no-ops outside the bitmap without
turning a valid `EraseRect` call into an enormous host-side loop.

G10/G11 blit closeout: `BltBitMapRastPort` now passes the destination
RastPort's `Mask` into the planar minterm engine. Only the selected destination
planes are changed; `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` continues to ignore that field as
required by its separate stencil contract.

G10/G11 `ClipBlit` closeout: the non-layered RastPort-to-RastPort path now
reads and forwards the destination `RastPort.Mask` to the same minterm engine.
Masked destination planes therefore remain unchanged, while layered ports
still decline before any bitmap access so layers/provider ownership is intact.

G09/G10/G11 address-envelope closeout: RastPort layer, bitmap, mask, and
template reads in the portable blit family now use checked 32-bit field
addresses. A wrapped RastPort field can no longer alias low guest memory or
publish a planar write; a sparse high-address regression covers the
`BltBitMapRastPort` gateway.

G15/G17 active-view fingerprint closeout: repeated `LoadView` requests now
include each linked `RasInfo` envelope and the display-relevant `BitMap`
geometry/plane-link fields in the same-pointer signature. The signature hashes
the guest `BitMap.Planes[]` pointer fields themselves rather than reading four
bytes from linked pixel storage, so a valid one-row/two-byte display raster is
accepted without an unrelated storage read and pixel-content changes do not
masquerade as display-topology changes. Editing a plane pointer under an
already active View still rebuilds the publication, while an unchanged nested
chain remains idempotent; focused coverage exercises both paths.

G07/G11 multicolor-pattern closeout: negative `AreaPtSz` patterns now use
their decoded planes as a nonzero stencil in JAM1 and deposit `APen`; JAM2
continues to deposit the encoded multicolor value, with inverse-video applied
to the source planes before either rule.

The multicolor JAM1 boundary is explicitly regression-tested with a zero
source cell: it leaves the destination untouched rather than treating a
negative pattern as an implicit solid fill. Pattern preflight also covers
JAM1/INVERSVID reads, while the native `COMPLEMENT|JAM2` whole-region shortcut
continues to avoid an otherwise unused pattern source.

That shortcut now also bypasses alignment validation for an odd, unused
`AreaPtrn` pointer. Other pattern modes still reject odd source addresses
before any raster write.

G11 template alignment closeout: `BltTemplate` now rejects an odd `srcMod`
before decoding or writing. The source template is word-addressed on the
classic blitter boundary, while zero and negative even moduli retain their
signed BLTxMOD behavior for repeated or reverse-row templates.

G11 template pointer closeout: `BltTemplate` now also rejects an odd source
pointer before reading the first template byte. The documented source points
at an aligned UWORD; the pure path therefore preserves the native address-error
boundary and leaves malformed calls available to a CopperSharp68k/provider
implementation.

G11 template draw-mode closeout: `BltTemplate` now decodes `INVERSVID` as a
template-stencil inversion and, for JAM2, preflights and writes both `APen`
and `BPen` cells. JAM1 retains its foreground-only behavior and all selected
planes remain rollback-atomic on a late write failure.

G11 template complement closeout: the JAM2 background phase now carries the
full current draw mode into the planar writer. `COMPLEMENT` therefore toggles
both template-one and template-zero cells, while the existing `INVERSVID`
stencil inversion and rollback boundary remain unchanged.

G11 masked-pattern closeout: when `BltPattern` has no `AreaPtrn`, a non-null
mask is treated as the one-bit template. A JAM2 request is locally reduced to
JAM1 (preserving `INVERSVID`) so only mask-set cells deposit `APen`; the
external mask still controls clipping and write-mask selection.

G10/G11 mask-stride closeout: `BltPattern` now validates only the mask bytes
the clipped destination can touch on each declared row, while retaining wide
32-bit stride/address overflow checks. A legal near-`ULONG_MAX` row stride no
longer creates an unbounded host-side validation walk.

G11 blit-transaction closeout: late mask or area-pattern reads in the second
`BltPattern` pass now restore the complete destination snapshot before
declining. A guest-memory fault cannot expose an earlier patterned pixel while
the vector reports failure.

G19 pixel-array closeout: `WritePixelLine8`, `WritePixelArray8`, and
`WriteChunkyPixels` now carry the destination `RastPort.Mask` through their
planar writer. Unselected destination planes remain unchanged while the
requested pixel count and clipping behavior are preserved.

G20 scaling closeout: `ScalerDiv` and the `BitMapScale` extent path now use
the native nearest-integer, half-up ratio arithmetic. Zero source factors
remain a zero result, while fractional destination dimensions are rounded
before source sampling; pure coverage verifies the shared 4.5-to-5 extent
boundary. This follows the documented `ScalerDiv` role and the AROS
reference implementation's remainder threshold ([ScalerDiv autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ScalerDiv),
[AROS scalerdiv.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scalerdiv.c),
[AROS bitmapscale.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c)).

G19 scaler-sampling closeout: native planar `BitMapScale` now uses the
reference centered DDA row/column schedule after deriving the destination
extent. Fractional expansion therefore maps a 3-pixel source to five output
samples as `0,0,1,2,2`, rather than using a floor-only lookup that shifts the
middle sample. A focused regression proves the resulting planar bytes and
keeps the existing complete preflight/rollback boundary intact ([AROS
bitmapscale.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c)).

G06/G07 collector closeout: `AreaEllipse` now replaces a pending `AreaMove`
in-place, matching the native two-vector ellipse stream. The collector count,
vector pointer, and flag pointer therefore expose no empty polygon marker, and
a following `AreaMove` consumes exactly one new vector; pure coverage verifies
the replacement and rollback-safe guest layout ([AROS areaellipse.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaellipse.c)).

G06/G07 collector update: consecutive `AreaMove` calls replace the prior
pending start marker in place after Kickstart's initial one-vector capacity
check. A full one-vector collector therefore declines the second call, while
collectors with spare capacity keep the native `AreaInfo` count/pointer state
stable ([AROS areamove.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areamove.c)).

G08 line-pattern closeout: connected `Draw` calls now render their shared
starting vertex for JAM1/JAM2, so a pen change between segments is visible at
the vertex. Only `COMPLEMENT` performs the native post-render undo when the
pattern actually emitted that dot; the first-dot and line-pattern phase state
remain unchanged ([AROS draw.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c)).

G06 collector-capacity closeout: `AreaEllipse` reserves its two vectors before
considering pending-`AreaMove` replacement. A trailing move with only one free
slot therefore fails atomically, matching the native capacity boundary while
preserving the earlier in-place replacement when two slots are available
([AROS areaellipse.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaellipse.c)).

G03/G04 metric closeout (superseded by the 2026-08-18 alternate-constraint
selection closeout below): `TextFit` treated zero alternate width/height as a
literal zero-sized rendering box when no explicit `TextExtent` was supplied.
No glyph could fit that box, and the result extent was cleared atomically. The
explicit-extent/alternate-dimension interaction was subsequently corrected so
that A3 supplies the complete constraint when nonzero
([TextFit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).

G08 AreaInfo ABI closeout: the portable collector now publishes the native
`MOVE=0`, `DRAW=1`, `CLOSEDRAW=2`, and `ELLIPSE=3` flag values. `AreaMove` and
`AreaEllipse` close a preceding DRAW polygon before appending their new item,
retag an already closed final vertex without consuming a slot, and preserve
Kickstart's pre-close capacity checks; consecutive ELLIPSE vectors carry the
same ELLIPSE flag ([AROS AreaMove](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areamove.c),
[AROS AreaEllipse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaellipse.c),
[AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c)).

G07 scroll boundary closeout: non-layered `ScrollRaster` now leaves its
rectangle untouched when `abs(dx)` or `abs(dy)` reaches the logical rectangle
extent, matching the native no-source-pixels boundary; `ScrollRasterBF` retains
the same move boundary but clears a fully vacated rectangle through its
EraseRect-style BPen path ([ScrollRaster autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ScrollRaster),
[AROS ScrollRaster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollraster.c),
[AROS ScrollRasterBF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollrasterbf.c)).
Zero-displacement `ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` requests now retain the
same fail-closed storage probes but return before the move/fill transaction,
so valid no-ops leave both pixels and `linpatcnt` unchanged. Focused coverage
keeps this distinct from real moves and fully vacated BF clears.
G08 shape-isolation closeout: `AreaEnd` now clears and reapplies the temporary
area mask for each recorded polygon or ellipse instead of merging all shapes
into one union mask. This preserves Kickstart's sequential `BltPattern`
boundary, including one `COMPLEMENT` toggle per overlapping shape; focused
coverage proves two identical polygons restore a seeded pixel after the two
toggles ([AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c)).
G08 outline-order closeout: `AreaEnd` now reads the outline state before the
transaction and emits each polygon/ellipse outline directly after its own
fill, preserving later-shape-over-earlier-outline ordering. Focused coverage
proves a later overlapping fill replaces the earlier outline pixel
([AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c)).
G08 outline-vertex closeout: AreaEnd outline traversal now suppresses the
duplicate first/last endpoint and intermediate segment starts, so a closed
polygon's shared vertices are emitted once even in `COMPLEMENT` mode. Focused
coverage verifies the first outline vertex is not toggled back by a redundant
zero-length segment ([AROS Draw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c), [AROS PolyDraw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c)).
G08 outline-pattern closeout: polygon `AREAOUTLINE` now delegates its
segments to the portable `Move`/`Draw` state machine, preserving line-pattern
phase, `INVERSVID`, connected-vertex behavior, and the native 15-bit restart
when the outline pen is installed. AreaEnd restores the saved cursor/flags and
keeps ellipse outlines on the shared DrawEllipse path; focused coverage proves
the patterned edge and caller cursor survive the complete transaction
([AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c), [AROS Draw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c), [AROS PolyDraw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c)).
G06 line-restart closeout: `Move`, `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, and `SetDrMd` now
publish the native fresh-line `linpatcnt=15` phase instead of preserving a
stale phase (the setters previously already restarted it). `Move` updates the
cursor, phase, and `FRST_DOT` flag atomically and restores all four fields when
a guest write fails. Focused coverage checks the fresh-line phase directly,
the rollback boundary, all three setters, and the existing patterned
Draw/AreaEnd paths
([SetAPen autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node0475.html), [gfxmacros.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/gfxmacros.h), [AROS Move](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/move.c)).
G03 metric-constraint closeout: `TextFit` now honors all six fields of a
non-null constraining `TextExtent`; candidate width and height must fit its
explicit `te_Width`/`te_Height` as well as its relative rectangle. The
alternate D2/D3 dimensions remain the fallback only when A3 is null. Focused
coverage exercises a rectangle that admits a glyph but explicit dimensions
that reject it, then widens only the explicit fields to admit the same glyph
([TextFit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit), [AROS textfit.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textfit.c)).
Historical note: the earlier long-word ABI experiment is superseded by the
2026-08-15 correction below. The authoritative Kickstart frame uses signed
WORD counts for `Text`/`TextLength`/`TextExtent`, and UWORD `strLen`/width/
height plus signed WORD `strDirection` for `TextFit`; the gateway and layered
provider now consume those low fields while the portable core keeps widened
host accumulation internally. `TextLength` remains sign-extended from its
classic WORD result
([Text](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/Text.html), [TextLength](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextLength.html), [TextExtent](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextExtent.html), [TextFit](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).
G06 line-phase closeout: connected `Draw` now uses `FRST_DOT` as the sole
fresh-line marker. A 16-bit pattern phase of zero remains a connected segment
state, so `COMPLEMENT` performs the native shared-start undo after a full
period wrap; focused coverage draws a 15-pixel segment followed by a phase-
zero connected segment and verifies the endpoint is not toggled back
([AROS draw.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c)).
G06/G07 draw-mode closeout: `BltPattern` now matches the classic null-
`AreaPtrn` template path for `INVERSVID`: the external mask's selected cells
are inverted before JAM1/JAM2/COMPLEMENT pen application, while the
`COMPLEMENT|JAM2` whole-region shortcut keeps the original mask stencil.
Focused coverage exercises JAM1, JAM2's template reduction, `COMPLEMENT|INVERSVID`,
and the shortcut exception ([AROS BltPattern](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/bltpattern.c), [AROS BltTemplate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/blttemplate.c)).
G06 PolyDraw closeout: `PolyDraw` now models the native `Draw` loop for every
array pair, including the first pair. The first segment starts at the
RastPort's existing current pen rather than an inserted `Move`, preserving
the caller's first-dot and line-pattern phase; focused coverage verifies a
single-pair call draws the existing-pen-to-endpoint segment
([AROS polydraw.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c), [PolyDraw autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/PolyDraw)).
G06 ABI closeout: the host adapter now passes `PolyDraw`'s D0 count through
the low 16 bits as the original ROM does, so `0xFFFF` is not misclassified as
a negative no-op. Focused register coverage verifies the large request reaches
the guarded guest point-stream read and falls through only because its buffer
is deliberately truncated ([AROS polydraw.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c)).
Historical note: the 2026-08-15 text-vector correction supersedes this
intermediate long-word experiment. The authoritative `TextFit` frame uses
UWORD D0/D2/D3 and WORD D1; the gateway now consumes those low fields and
ignores unrelated high-word residue while preserving the classic result
fields ([TextFit autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).
G05 ABI closeout: `SetSoftStyle` now has focused register coverage with
nonzero high words in D0/D1. The adapter preserves the complete ULONG inputs,
while the portable result remains the classic byte-sized `AlgoStyle` state
combined with intrinsic font style bits ([SetSoftStyle autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/SetSoftStyle), [AROS setsoftstyle.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setsoftstyle.c)).
G04/G05 draw-mode closeout: Text JAM2 now pre-fills the complete measured
`TextExtent` envelope, so BPen covers inter-character spacing and font rows
without a glyph strike. `INVERSVID` selects APen for template-zero cells, and
`JAM2|COMPLEMENT` toggles the entire envelope exactly once instead of running
both source phases. The rectangle is preflighted through the existing planar
clipping and rollback boundary; focused coverage verifies spacing, empty rows,
and complement behavior ([AROS Text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/text.c),
[AROS TextExtent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textextent.c),
[WritePixel autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixel)).

G17/G26/G27 timed display publication closeout: the CopperStart timed display
adapter now uses its status-aware `TryLoadView` callback when the legacy void
`LoadView` callback is absent. This keeps direct timed callers on the same
publication owner as `GraphicsLibraryCore.LoadView`, while the result-bearing
`TryPublishView` path continues to preserve provider decline status. A focused
regression verifies the view pointer and CPU cycle at that boundary; the
focused `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests` suite now passes 600 tests.

G02/G04 font admission closeout: proportional guest `TextFont` nodes with a
non-null `CharLoc` now require both the first and final `tf_CharData` strike
rows implied by `tf_YSize` and `tf_Modulo` to be readable before `AddFont` or
resident-list `OpenFont` selection. Fixed-cell resident nodes retain their
opaque modulo lifecycle contract and defer detailed row/width validation to
the existing text and metric preflight. A focused malformed-font regression
guards the final-row boundary; the focused graphics scaffold now passes 599
tests.

G02/G04 proportional table closeout: the same admission path now probes every
declared `CharLoc`, `CharSpace`, and `CharKern` entry, including the extra
out-of-range default-glyph slot. A truncated table therefore remains
unselectable instead of failing only after `Text` or metric dispatch. The
fixed-cell resident contract remains unchanged; the focused graphics scaffold
now passes 600 tests.
G05/G07 layer-boundary closeout: layered `RectFill` now reaches the explicit
`IGraphicsLayerRasterBackend` claim seam with its four signed coordinates.
The portable planar core remains restricted to non-layered RastPorts; a
provider that declines the optional method preserves D0/cycles and leaves the
call available to native layers code. Focused host coverage verifies the
forwarded rectangle and the existing declined-layer behavior
([RectFill autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/RectFill)).
G05/G08 layer-boundary extension: layered `DrawEllipse` now forwards its
center/radius WORD arguments through the optional layer-raster provider while
the portable midpoint implementation remains restricted to non-layered
RastPorts. Focused host coverage verifies D0/cycle preservation and the
forwarded geometry; provider decline still leaves native layers ownership
available ([DrawEllipse autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/DrawEllipse)).
G05/G07 layer-boundary extension: layered `SetRast` now forwards its UBYTE
pen through the optional layer-raster provider. Plain RastPorts retain the
portable full-bitmap fill, while provider decline preserves the void-vector
native fallback and D0/cycles. Focused coverage verifies the pen and the
declined-layer path ([SetRast autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/SetRast)).
G05/G06 layer-boundary extension: layered `ReadPixel` and `WritePixel` now
route through optional provider methods. `ReadPixel` preserves the provider's
signed result, including `-1`, while `WritePixel` normalizes D0 only after a
successful claim; absent providers leave both vectors available to native
layers code. Focused coverage verifies coordinate forwarding, pixel results,
and D0/cycle preservation ([ReadPixel autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixel),
[WritePixel autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixel)).
G05/G07 layer-boundary extension: layered `ScrollRaster`, `ScrollRasterBF`,
`ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, and `EraseRect` now route through optional provider
methods carrying their signed displacement/rectangle arguments. Successful
claims clear D0 while preserving the guest cycle; absent or declining
providers leave the call unclaimed for native layers ownership. Focused
coverage verifies both scroll variants, the two clear vectors, and rectangle
forwarding ([ScrollRaster autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ScrollRaster),
[EraseRect autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/EraseRect)).
G05/G06/G08 layer-boundary extension: layered `PolyDraw`, `AreaMove`,
`AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`, `AreaEnd`, and `Flood` now route through optional
provider methods. The adapter preserves PolyDraw's low-16-bit count and Flood's
BOOL result while void vectors clear D0 only after a successful claim. Focused
coverage verifies point-stream, collector, ellipse, and seed coordinates plus
declined-provider ownership ([PolyDraw autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/PolyDraw),
[AreaEnd autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/AreaEnd),
[Flood autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/Flood)).
G05/G10/G11 layer-boundary extension: typed provider claims now cover layered
`ClipBlit`, `BltBitMapRastPort`, `BltMaskBitMapRastPort`, `BltPattern`, and
`BltTemplate`. The adapter preserves the signed WORD geometry, pointers, and
minterm; only the BOOL-returning bitmap-to-RastPort call publishes its provider
result. RTG source/destination endpoints are excluded before the layer claim,
keeping CyberGraphX ownership separate. Focused coverage verifies all five
forwarding paths and the existing generic callback fallback
([ClipBlit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ClipBlit),
[BltBitMapRastPort autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/BltBitMapRastPort),
[BltPattern autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/BltPattern),
[BltTemplate autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/BltTemplate)).
G05/G06/G19 layer-boundary extension: typed provider claims now cover the V36
`ReadPixelLine8`, `WritePixelLine8`, `ReadPixelArray8`, and `WritePixelArray8`
vectors plus V40 `WriteChunkyPixels`. The line/array callbacks preserve the
UWORD coordinate ABI, temporary RastPort and byte-array pointers, and their
count-returning D0 result. The chunky callback preserves signed LONG bounds,
source-array A2, and bytes-per-row D4 while retaining its void success ABI.
RTG RastPorts are rejected before the layer claim so CyberGraphX remains a
separate patch owner; provider decline leaves D0/cycles untouched for native
layers. Focused host coverage verifies all five paths and the existing
declined-layer sweep
([ReadPixelLine8 autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixelLine8),
[ReadPixelArray8 autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixelArray8),
[WritePixelLine8 autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixelLine8),
[WritePixelArray8 autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixelArray8),
[WriteChunkyPixels autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WriteChunkyPixels)).
G27 native-overlay extension: `ReadPixel` and `WritePixel` now join the
explicitly proven guest-memory-safe ROM overlay subset. The differential
overlay fixture initializes a three-plane guest bitmap, invokes both vectors
through the mapped jump table, and compares the returned registers and every
plane byte against the direct host path. Layered and RTG ownership remains
outside this overlay admission so future native layers/CyberGraphX patches
retain their boundaries.
G26/G27 lifecycle differential extension: the same mapped-jump-table fixture
now independently exercises `InitView`, `InitVPort`, `InitBitMap`, `InitArea`,
and `InitTmpRas`, comparing each complete guest envelope and void D0/cycle
result against direct CopperStart dispatch. This proves the shared View,
ViewPort, BitMap, AreaInfo, and TmpRas layouts at the native boundary without
claiming display publication, copper hardware ownership, or RTG behavior.
G19 BitMapScale ownership closeout: the portable scaler now rejects a shared
source/destination `BitMap` header even when the requested rectangles are
disjoint. The classic operation is not an in-place scaler; distinct headers
that alias plane storage remain rejected as well. Focused coverage proves the
extent fields stay unchanged on this early failure ([BitMapScale autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/BitMapScale),
[AROS bitmapscale.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c)).

G26/G27 arithmetic differential extension: the mapped native jump-table fixture
now also compares the corrected nonzero sub-unit `ScalerDiv(1,1,2)` result
against direct CopperStart dispatch, in addition to the existing ordinary
rounding case. This keeps the native-safe arithmetic proof aligned with the
portable G19 minimum-result contract.

G02 font-lifecycle closeout: `ExtendFont` now materializes a bounded effective
`TagItem` stream into backend-owned guest storage colocated with the owned
`TextFontExtension`, publishes that clone instead of retaining the caller's
pointer, and releases the combined allocation on `StripFont`. `TAG_MORE`,
`TAG_SKIP`, and ignored records are resolved while cloning, malformed/cyclic
chains still fail before allocation, and focused coverage verifies that
mutating the caller's list after publication cannot change the extension's
device-DPI tags ([AROS extendfont.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/extendfont.c)).

RemFont now preflights a canonical `TextFontExtension` and honors
`TE0F_NOREMFONT` before mutating the guest font list or `FPF_REMOVED`, matching
the AROS removal guard; malformed extension records fail closed and foreign
extensions remain removable ([AROS remfont.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/remfont.c)).

CloseFont now removes the last-accessor non-ROM font automatically while
leaving ROM fonts public and treating `TE0F_NOREMFONT` as the documented
exception; failed extension/list validation restores the accessor count for a
retry ([AROS closefont.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/closefont.c)).

AddFont now publishes the embedded Exec node's `NT_FONT` type (`ln_Type` at
the shared `TextFont` offset) before list insertion, restoring both node type
and accessor count if either the guest-list or direct availability publication
fails ([AROS addfont.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/addfont.c)).

RemFont now invokes the existing owned-extension `StripFont` path after
availability removal and restores list membership/accessors if that teardown
fails, while foreign extensions remain untouched ([AROS remfont.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/remfont.c)).

GfxFree now validates the guest association field before removing an extended
node from the registry.  An unreadable association declines without freeing
the node, so `GfxLookUp` cannot retain a stale pointer to reclaimed storage;
successful teardown removes only the association owned by that node, matching
the hash-list removal boundary in [AROS gfxfree.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfree.c).

GfxFree now also clears the guest-visible View/ViewPort backlink before the
allocation is released.  A failed backlink write leaves the node, lookup
entry, and allocation intact, so the portable path cannot free storage while
publishing a dangling association; focused coverage exercises both the
successful clear and the rollback boundary.  This completes the documented
"disassociate before freeing" contract in the
[GfxFree autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/GfxFree).

GfxNew now accepts all four public graphics extended-node types: ViewExtra,
ViewPortExtra, SpecialMonitor, and MonitorSpec.  The portable registry keeps
the View/ViewPort backwards-link association contract narrow while still
allocating and publishing the common `NT_GRAPHICS`/`SS_GRAPHICS`/subtype
metadata for monitor nodes, matching the documented allocation table in
[AROS gfxnew.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxnew.c).

OpenMonitor/CloseMonitor now share a native PAL/NTSC MonitorSpec within the
portable registry, increment and decrement its guest `ms_OpenCount`, and
release the allocation only after the last close.  Failed count writes leave
the registry and guest count unchanged, following the reference open/close
contract in [AROS openmonitor.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/openmonitor.c) and [AROS closemonitor.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/closemonitor.c).

The CopperStart graphics context now carries the active graphics.library base
into the portable core, so `GfxNew` publishes the shared `xln_Library`
back-pointer in the guest ExtendedNode layout.  `xln_Init` remains explicitly
zero until a real guest-callable dummy entry is available; no host callback
address is fabricated in guest memory.

G09 InitBitMap ABI correction: portable `InitBitMap` now declines zero-depth
and greater-than-eight-plane requests before snapshotting or publishing the
guest envelope, writes the classic `BMF_STANDARD` flag, and preserves the
caller-owned `Planes[]` links.  The OCS/ECS path therefore keeps the public
bitmap assembly contract while AGA/RTG providers retain ownership of wider
surfaces ([AROS initbitmap.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initbitmap.c)).

G01 InitRastPort ABI correction: portable initialization now uses the classic
`Mask=0xFF`, `FgPen=0xFF`, `AOlPen=0xFF`, `DrawMode=JAM2`, and `LinePtrn=0xFFFF`
defaults while leaving the documented unused pen-size fields zero.  This
matches the public autodoc and avoids manufacturing a foreground pen that the
guest routine never publishes ([InitRastPort autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/InitRastPort), [AROS initrastport.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initrastport.c)).

G01 RastPort state correction: portable initialization and the APen/BPen,
DrMd, and ABPenDrMd setters now publish the guest-visible `minterms[8]` at the
classic `RastPort` offset, including JAM1/JAM2, COMPLEMENT, and INVERSVID
truth-table variants.  Minterm writes are part of the same rollback boundary
as pen, draw-mode, and line-pattern phase updates, so a truncated or failing
guest write cannot leave derived state stale or partially published.  Focused
coverage verifies default, pen-derived, JAM1, complement, inverse-video, and
late-write rollback cases ([RastPort public layout](https://d0.se/include/graphics/rastport.h), [AROS GenMinterms](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c)).

G05 RastPort attribute transaction correction: `SetRPAttrsA` now snapshots and
restores the derived `minterms[8]` whenever an APen, BPen, or DrMd tag is
applied.  A later tag failure therefore rolls back the source pen/mode,
line-pattern restart, and derived truth table as one guest-visible update;
pure and register-boundary regressions preserve the original minterms and D0
([SetRPAttrA autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/SetRPAttrA), [RastPort public layout](https://d0.se/include/graphics/rastport.h)).

G15/G17/G26 lifecycle correction: the native ROM-overlay `InitVPort` gateway
now claims the vector only after guarded guest initialization succeeds.
Malformed or unmapped viewport pointers preserve D0/cycles and skip host
projection, matching the normal CopperStart path and leaving native/provider
ownership available; valid initialization still projects and clears D0
([InitVPort autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/InitVPort), [graphics/view.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/view.h)).

G15/G26/G27 structure-initializer overlay closeout: `InitView` and `InitVPort`
now have a paired direct-vs-mapped proof. The fixture compares the complete
guest envelopes after clear, the shared `View` origin and `SpritePriorities`
defaults, void D0/cycle behavior, and the compatibility ViewPort projection
callback. Invalid pointers remain declined before projection, so this closes
the native overlay seam without broadening ownership to malformed or provider
backed display structures.

G03/G26/G27 proportional-metric overlay closeout: the existing ROM-safe metric
vectors now have an independent direct-vs-mapped proof using a real guest
bit-packed proportional `TextFont`, `tf_CharLoc`, `tf_CharSpace`, and
`tf_CharKern` tables. `TextLength`, `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent`
produce the same proportional advances, relative bounds, fit count, guest
`TextExtent` bytes, D0, and cycles through direct CopperStart dispatch and the
mapped native jump table. Rendering, font ownership, and provider-sensitive
text remain outside this overlay admission ([AROS TextLength](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textlength.c), [AROS TextExtent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textextent.c), [AROS TextFit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textfit.c), [FontExtent autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/FontExtent)).

G04/G26/G27 `Text` overlay closeout: standard planar proportional text now has
an independent direct-vs-mapped proof covering guest bit-packed glyph decoding,
selected-plane raster bytes, cursor advance, void D0, and cycles. `GraphicsLvo.Text`
is admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos` only for non-layered, non-RTG RastPorts;
layer clipping/damage, provider-owned surfaces, and CyberGraphX remain outside
this overlay boundary ([AROS Text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/text.c), [Text autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/Text)).

G04/G06 text line-state closeout: successful `Text` now completes through the
same fresh-position state as `Move`, resetting `linpatcnt` to 15 and setting
`FRST_DOT` after the clipped cursor update. The text transaction preflights and
rolls back those fields together with the rendered raster when its final state
publication fails. Focused coverage proves both the fresh phase and rollback
boundary ([AROS Text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/text.c), [AROS Move](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/move.c)).

G06/G26/G27 `Draw` overlay closeout: a standard planar Bresenham segment now
has an independent direct-vs-mapped proof covering selected-plane line pixels,
cursor position, line-pattern phase, consumed `FRST_DOT`, void D0, and cycles.
`GraphicsLvo.Draw` is admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos` only for non-layered,
non-RTG RastPorts; connected-line state remains guest-owned and layer damage or
CyberGraphX raster ownership stays outside this boundary ([AROS Draw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c), [Draw autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/Draw)).

G07/G26/G27 `RectFill` overlay closeout: an inclusive standard-planar
rectangle now has an independent direct-vs-mapped proof covering selected-plane
fill bytes, the void D0/cycle boundary, and the existing non-layered gate.
`GraphicsLvo.RectFill` is admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos` only for standard
planar RastPorts; inverted bounds, layer clipping/damage, and CyberGraphX
surfaces remain provider/native-owned ([AROS RectFill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/rectfill.c), [RectFill autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/RectFill)).

G07/G26/G27 `SetRast` overlay closeout: the unconditional standard-planar
 raster initialization now has an independent direct-vs-mapped proof covering
 selected-plane publication, void D0/cycles, and the existing non-layered gate.
 `GraphicsLvo.SetRast` is admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos` only for standard
 planar RastPorts; layer damage, RTG surfaces, and CyberGraphX ownership remain
 outside this overlay boundary ([AROS SetRast](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setrast.c), [SetRast autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/SetRast)).

G07/G26/G27 clear-vector overlay closeout: standard-planar `ClearEOL` and
`ClearScreen` now have a paired direct-vs-mapped proof covering text-line
geometry, JAM2 background clearing, full-screen continuation, void D0/cycles,
and the existing non-layered gate. Both vectors are admitted to
`RomSafeOverlayLvos` only for standard planar RastPorts; layer damage, RTG
surfaces, and CyberGraphX remain provider/native-owned ([AROS ClearEOL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/cleareol.c), [AROS ClearScreen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/clearscreen.c)).

G06/G07 clear line-state closeout: `ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` now publish
`linpatcnt=15` after their classic `SetAPen`-style clear fill. Both vectors
snapshot the selected raster and restore it plus the original phase if the
final phase store fails; focused direct/overlay parity and rollback coverage
prove the guest-visible boundary. This is grounded in the classic-compatible
AROS implementation path rather than an explicit autodoc side-effect promise
([AROS ClearEOL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/cleareol.c), [AROS ClearScreen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/clearscreen.c), [AROS SetAPen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c)).

G06/G07 `EraseRect` line-state closeout: non-layered `EraseRect` now follows
the same classic `SetAPen`-style phase boundary, temporarily selecting
`BgPen` and routing the fill through `RectFill` before restoring `FgPen`,
derived minterms, and `linpatcnt=15`. A failing final byte store restores both
the selected raster and original RastPort state. Focused direct/overlay parity,
background-pen, and rollback coverage prove this standard-planar boundary;
layered `EraseRect` remains provider/native-owned
([AROS EraseRect](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/eraserect.c)).

G06/G07 scroll line-state closeout: real standard-planar `ScrollRaster` and
`ScrollRasterBF` operations now publish `linpatcnt=15` after their move and
vacated-area fill, matching the classic `SetABPenDrMd`/`RectFill` and
`EraseRect` paths. The clipped destination and original phase are restored if
the final phase store fails; unchanged normal-scroll no-ops retain their
existing raster/phase state. Focused direct/overlay parity and rollback tests
cover both vectors ([AROS ScrollRaster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollraster.c), [AROS ScrollRasterBF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollrasterbf.c)).

G07/G26/G27 `EraseRect` overlay closeout: standard-planar `EraseRect` now has
a paired direct-vs-mapped proof covering inclusive clipped fill bytes, pen-zero
clearing, void D0/cycles, and the existing layer-provider gate. The vector is
admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos` only for standard planar RastPorts; layered
damage, RTG surfaces, and CyberGraphX remain provider/native-owned ([AROS
EraseRect](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/eraserect.c)).

G06/G26/G27 `DrawEllipse` overlay closeout: standard-planar `DrawEllipse` now
has a paired direct-vs-mapped proof covering midpoint outline bytes, guest bit
order, cardinal points, void D0/cycles, and the existing non-layered gate. The
vector is admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos` only for valid in-bounds planar
ellipses; layer damage, RTG surfaces, and CyberGraphX remain provider/native-owned
([AROS DrawEllipse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/drawellipse.c)).

G07/G26/G27 normal `ScrollRaster` overlay closeout: standard-planar scrolling
now has a paired direct-vs-mapped proof covering source snapshot movement,
BPen-filled vacated pixels, planar bytes, void D0/cycles, and the existing
layer-provider gate. The normal vector is admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos`;
its EraseRect-style companion is recorded separately below because its
vacated-area contract differs ([AROS ScrollRaster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollraster.c)).

G07/G26/G27 `ScrollRasterBF` overlay closeout: standard-planar backfill now has
its own direct-vs-mapped proof, confirming that the moved source pixel matches
normal scrolling while the vacated edge clears to pen zero even when BPen is
nonzero. The vector is admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos`; layered damage, RTG
surfaces, and CyberGraphX remain provider/native-owned ([AROS ScrollRasterBF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollrasterbf.c)).

G08/G26/G27 area-polygon overlay closeout: standard-planar `AreaMove`,
`AreaDraw`, and `AreaEnd` now have one direct-vs-mapped proof covering the
caller-owned vector/flag stream, filled planar bytes, collector reset, void
D0/cycles, and the existing layer-provider gate. The three vectors are
admitted to `RomSafeOverlayLvos`; `AreaEllipse` remains a separate collector
unit ([AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c)).

G08/G26/G27 area-ellipse overlay closeout: standard-planar `AreaEllipse` now
has an independent direct-vs-mapped proof covering its two-vector collector
encoding, allocator-backed fill, planar bytes, collector reset, void D0/cycles,
and the existing layer-provider gate. The vector is admitted to
`RomSafeOverlayLvos` ([AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c)).

G08/G26/G27 flood overlay closeout: standard-planar `Flood` now has an
independent direct-vs-mapped proof covering seed-color connected traversal,
allocator-backed guest visited storage, planar bytes, result D0/cycles, and
the existing layer-provider gate. The vector is admitted to
`RomSafeOverlayLvos` ([AROS Flood](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/Flood)).

G07/G26/G27 PolyDraw overlay closeout: standard-planar `PolyDraw` now has an
 independent direct-vs-mapped proof covering the guest point stream,
 connected line output, final current-pen state, void D0/cycles, and the
 existing layer-provider gate. The vector is admitted to
 `RomSafeOverlayLvos` ([AROS PolyDraw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c)).

G15/G26/G27 `LoadView` overlay closeout: the validated standard display chain
now has a direct-vs-mapped proof covering active publication, repeated
signature-based no-op behavior, explicit blanking, void D0/cycles, and mapped
RTG provider forwarding. `GraphicsLvo.LoadView` is admitted to
`RomSafeOverlayLvos`; malformed standard Views remain unclaimed for native
ownership ([LoadView autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/LoadView)).

The reversible ROM overlay now snapshots each replaced slot's original
`JMP.L` target before installing the host gateway. A portable decline therefore
tail-chains into the original Kickstart routine, while a positively classified
provider call is handled by its provider callback and does not tail-chain.
Focused coverage preserves D0, cycles, and the original target for a malformed
`LoadView` call.

G17/G26/G27 `WaitTOF` overlay closeout: the scheduler-backed frame wait now has
direct-vs-mapped parity coverage for callback invocation, cycle advancement,
and the documented void D0 result. The vector is admitted alongside
`LoadView`; an unbound host still declines and tail-chains to native Kickstart.

G17/G26/G27 `VBeamPos` overlay closeout: the canonical cycle-sampled beam
callback now has direct-vs-mapped parity coverage, preserves the UWORD result
and CPU cycle, and tail-chains to the original native vector when the host has
no beam-position owner.

G17/G26/G27 `WaitBOVP` overlay closeout: a valid viewport/RasInfo chain now has
direct-vs-mapped parity through the explicit vertical-blank boundary, including
cycle advancement and void D0. Malformed or unbound waits preserve their
register/cycle state and tail-chain to native Kickstart.

G17/G26/G27 `ScrollVPort` overlay closeout: a valid viewport/RasInfo chain now
reaches the explicit display-rebuild callback through direct and mapped calls,
preserving the void D0 result and CPU cycle. Malformed or unbound scrolls
remain native-owned through the original vector.

G17/G26/G27 `ChangeVPBitMap` overlay closeout: a valid standard-planar
replacement now updates the guest RasInfo association and reaches the explicit
display-rebuild boundary through direct and mapped calls without advancing the
CPU cycle. A replacement that advertises `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` must also expose
word-aligned plane pointers and a readable complete row envelope before the
association changes; malformed or unbound swaps preserve the old association
and tail-chain to native Kickstart.

G17 displayable-swap validation closeout: `ChangeVPBitMap` now distinguishes
geometry-only bitmap envelopes used during viewport assembly from surfaces
advertising the public `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` capability. Displayable replacements
must pass the same aligned-plane and complete-row-span checks used by the
strict `LoadView` reader, while ordinary geometry-only test/assembly headers
retain their existing association behavior. The focused regression proves an
odd display plane is declined before `RasInfo.BitMap` publication and that the
same replacement succeeds after its plane envelope is repaired. Direct
CopperStart dispatch and the mapped ROM overlay now exercise that same failure
boundary: neither path requests a display rebuild, changes D0/cycles, or lets
the malformed swap cross into the RTG/provider callback.

G17/G26/G27 timed-rebuild closeout: the CopperStart `ScrollVPort` and
`ChangeVPBitMap` host seams now receive the explicit guest call cycle. A direct
host gateway therefore queues a rebuilt native copper stream against the caller
cycle even when the emulator CPU state's last observed cycle is older; the
guest `ViewPort.DspIns` projection remains visible immediately while the
custom-chip copper pointer changes only at the selected frame boundary. The
untimed callbacks remain available for CopperScreen/native hosts that own their
own current-cycle source, and CyberGraphX remains outside this planar seam.

G17/G26/G27 double-buffer overlay closeout: `AllocDBufInfo` and
`FreeDBufInfo` now have direct-vs-mapped parity for guest message-envelope
initialization, per-library ownership, allocator release, and D0 results.
Allocation or ownership failure remains unclaimed and tail-chains to native
Kickstart.

G02 font-list atomicity closeout: removing the final guest `TextFont` now
 treats the canonical empty-list sentinel publication as part of the same
 transaction as unlinking the node and setting `FPF_REMOVED`.  A late byte
 failure restores the GfxBase list links, the font's predecessor/successor,
 and its flags, so the native/provider boundary can retry without exposing a
 half-removed font.  Focused coverage injects the failure at that final
 publication and verifies both rollback and a subsequent successful remove.

G03/G04 fixed-cell metric closeout: `GraphicsFontMetrics` now preserves
whether a guest `TextFont` supplies `CharSpace` or `CharKern`.  Non-proportional
fonts without either table use their nominal movement cell for `TextLength`,
`TextExtent`, and `TextFit`; a wider individual strike no longer expands the
public fixed-cell extent.  Variable-width fonts and fixed fonts with either
per-character table retain their kerning/strike envelope.  The focused pure
metric regression covers both the 12-byte extent result and the fit count;
provider clipping and exact ROM edge weighting remain separate gates.

G04 fixed-cell rendering closeout: the portable `Text` path now applies the
same `CharSpace`/`CharKern` presence rule as the metric vectors.  A provider
kerning value is ignored whenever the font has no `CharKern` table across glyph
placement, underline-range calculation, destination preflight, `FontExtent`,
and the published current-X cursor.  A focused regression proves that a
malformed or provider-specific kerning value cannot expand the nominal
fixed-cell advance; variable-width and fixed fonts with explicit per-character
tables retain their kerning behavior.

G06/G26/G27 pixel-vector overlay closeout: standard-planar `ReadPixel` and
`WritePixel` now have an independent direct-vs-mapped proof. The regression
covers two-plane colour reconstruction, APen/JAM1 publication, the signed
`-1` outside-RastPort result, and the unchanged destination bytes after that
rejection. The existing layer-provider claim remains the only path for layered
pixel access; CyberGraphX/RTG surfaces and provider-owned backing stores stay
outside the ROM-safe overlay ([ReadPixel autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixel),
[WritePixel autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixel)).

G03/G04 signed-spacing envelope closeout: variable-width `TextExtent` and
`TextFit` now include both intermediate and final movement cells in their
horizontal envelope, so negative `CharSpace`/`TxSpacing` extends `MinX` rather
than disappearing from the measured bounds. The alternate `TextFit` width is
checked against the complete rendered envelope instead of only the signed
cursor advance. JAM2 background and underline coverage use the same two-sided
movement range, keeping rendering, metrics, and the guest `TextExtent` ABI in
lockstep. Focused coverage raises the graphics scaffold to 601 tests.

G03/G04 styled-underline closeout: the run-wide underline now expands through
the same algorithmic bold-smear and italic-padding envelope reported by
`TextExtent`. Combined soft styles therefore underline their final styled
pixels, and destination preflight validates that expanded range before any
planar write. Focused `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests` coverage now
contains 609 passing cases.

G03/G04 fixed signed-envelope closeout: fixed-cell `TextExtent` and `TextFit`
now retain both endpoints of the nominal movement cell after negative
`TxSpacing` and `FPF_REVPATH` advances. JAM2 background and run-wide underline
coverage therefore agree with the leftward renderer envelope, while fixed
strike widths remain nominal unless proportional/`CharSpace`/`CharKern`
metadata opts into variable metrics. Focused `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests`
coverage now contains 611 passing cases.

G09 bitmap-query closeout: `GetBitMapAttr(BMA_FLAGS)` now publishes only the
public `BMF_DISPLAYABLE`, `BMF_INTERLEAVED`, and `BMF_STANDARD` classification
bits. Allocator request bits such as `BMF_CLEAR` and `BMF_MINPLANES` remain
private to bitmap construction and are masked from both pure and register ABI
queries. Focused coverage verifies the filtered value and preserves the 601
test graphics scaffold.

G09 malformed-teardown closeout: registered `FreeBitMap` calls now preflight
the complete standard-planar bitmap envelope and every declared plane raster
before releasing storage. Interleaved bitmaps additionally require the exact
contiguous plane sequence published by `AllocBitMap`; corrupted, sentinel, or
wrapped plane links preserve the instance ownership token, allocator state,
guest D0, and cycles for native/provider fallback. Pure and register-level
coverage raises the focused graphics scaffold to 603 tests.

G09 allocation-contract closeout (2026-08-29): ownership now captures the
exact standard-planar header geometry, flags, and plane links that
`AllocBitMap` published. `FreeBitMap` declines an otherwise readable but
altered descriptor before it can release a shortened plane prefix or a
different compact-header span; restoring the original descriptor leaves the
same allocation retryable. This remains an OCS/ECS portable ownership rule;
CyberGraphX/RTG bitmap lifecycles remain outside this path.

G10 temporary-A closeout: overlapping standard-planar `BltBitMap` spans now
validate a caller-supplied `TempA` workspace for word alignment and readable
source-row capacity. Alias detection compares the complete byte envelopes of
all participating source and destination planes, so shifted or cross-plane
storage cannot bypass the overlap gate. A NULL workspace retains the host's
transactional source snapshot, while a malformed workspace declines without
changing destination pixels; non-overlapping copies do not probe an unused
`TempA`. Pure and register-level coverage raises the focused graphics scaffold
to 606 tests.

G16/G17 nested-display closeout: the AmigaBoot compatibility projector now
reads `ViewPort.RasInfo`, both RasInfo nodes, BitMap geometry/depth, and every
declared plane link through checked 32-bit field envelopes. RasInfo source
offset arithmetic is widened before conversion to a DMA displacement, and the
complete displayed row span must remain inside the guest address space before
the chipset address adapter is used. A high RasInfo whose BitMap field wraps
to a low alias is rejected before replacing an existing `DspIns`/View CPR
publication; focused host coverage verifies the previous list remains intact.
CyberGraphX/RTG scanout remains outside this OCS/ECS projection boundary.

G16 copper-link closeout: optional `ViewPort.ColorMap`/`ColorTable` and
`UCopList`/`CopList`/`CopIns` fields now use the same checked 32-bit field
helpers. The complete user-instruction byte envelope is admitted before any
decode or generated-list write; a malformed wrapper preserves the old
`DspIns`/CPR links, while a malformed present ColorMap uses the documented
compatibility palette fallback without reading a wrapped low alias. Focused
AmigaBoot coverage exercises both high-pointer cases. CyberGraphX remains
outside this standard OCS/ECS copper path.

G16 publication closeout: `MakeVPort` now preflights the exact `View.ViewPort`,
LOF/SHF CPR, and `ViewPort.DspIns` fields that its host builder publishes.
Host-only calls with a wrapped publication target decline before allocating or
retargeting guest links; focused coverage preserves low-memory sentinels. The
guest layouts remain shared with CopperSharp68k, while CopperScreen retains
ownership of generated raw-list storage.

G17 host-read closeout: scheduler-facing viewport waits, active-chain mode
lookup, and synthetic-screen teardown now use checked field envelopes for
their `View`/`ViewPort` reads and DspIns/CPR clears. Wrapped host pointers can
no longer alias low memory during a beam wait or close-time teardown; the
standard portable validation and native/provider fallback boundaries remain
unchanged.

G18 `DisplayInfo` layout closeout: `DTAG_DISP` now publishes the complete
Kickstart guest chunk through a 0x38-byte payload with header length five,
including the public sprite/palette and RGB-bit fields plus zeroed padding and
the two reserved ULONG terminators. Partial caller buffers remain clipped
without changing the advertised native layout; focused coverage checks both
the short 0x30-byte compatibility request and a complete chunk.

G19 BitMapScale staging closeout: the transactional planar scaler now stores
each sampled pen in a byte-sized buffer (the native path is limited to eight
planes) and computes row bases in widened arithmetic before converting to the
guarded staging index. This preserves the existing atomic source/destination
contract while avoiding an unnecessary four-byte host allocation and an
overflow-prone `WORD * WORD` index expression. The focused BitMapScale filter
passes seven pure and mapped tests, including an eight-plane pen-value case;
the full graphics scaffold remains the
verification gate for the shared direct/mapped ABI.

G20/G26/G27 sprite teardown closeout: `FreeSpriteData(NULL)` now remains a
claimed successful no-op in the native overlay, matching the V40 contract.
Non-null foreign `ExtSprite` handles still decline and tail-chain to the
provider, while owned allocations retain their normal allocator release path.

G18 monitor-lifecycle correction: portable `MonitorSpec` objects now follow
the resident monitor-list ownership used by Kickstart. Repeated
`OpenMonitor` calls share the same guest object, `CloseMonitor` only decrements
`ms_OpenCount`, and a zero count leaves the node available to `DTAG_MNTR` and a
later reopen. The portable registry still owns allocation at graphics-instance
scope rather than pretending that a resident monitor node is a per-open
allocation; semaphores, monitor callbacks, and provider/native records remain
outside this portable slice ([OpenMonitor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/openmonitor.c), [CloseMonitor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/closemonitor.c)).

Screen lifecycle ownership correction: the synthetic Intuition
`SetWindowTitles` bridge now ignores foreign non-null `Window *` handles, so a
provider/native window cannot rewrite or allocate the private compatibility
screen. The existing null-window screen-title-only path remains available for
the host shim, and focused coverage proves a foreign call leaves the published
`Screen.Title` pointer unchanged ([SetWindowTitles autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node03F8.html)).

Screen-title clearing correction: an explicit NULL/empty `screenTitle` now
clears the synthetic title-bar rows immediately after publishing the null
`Screen.Title` pointer, while preserving pixels below the bar and retaining
the NoTitleChange sentinel behavior. Focused host coverage verifies the bar is
blanked, the current title pointer is zero, and a marker in the application
area survives ([SetWindowTitles autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0598.html)).

The same ownership guard declines null-window title calls before the first
synthetic screen exists, preventing an invalid pre-open call from allocating
compatibility Screen/View storage; the normal opened-screen null-window path
remains supported.

`ShowTitle(FALSE)` semantic correction: `SHOWTITLE` is an ordering flag for
backdrop windows, not a visibility gate. The synthetic single-surface host now
keeps an existing title rasterized in either flag state and reserves visual
suppression for `SCREENQUIET`; a focused regression proves the title-bar bytes
survive the FALSE transition ([ShowTitle](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0598.html), [Intuition Screens](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Intuition_Screens)).

G05 RastPort-attribute envelope closeout: `GetRPAttrsA` now rejects any
four-byte result or `RPTAG_DrawBounds` rectangle whose guest address would
wrap past `0xFFFF_FFFF`; the eight-byte Rectangle destination must also be
word-aligned. The output snapshot therefore cannot be satisfied by a wrapping
or odd-address memory provider; declined calls preserve the existing result
bytes and remain available to the native/provider implementation. Focused
coverage exercises both wrapped scalar and odd Rectangle boundaries.

G18 monitor-envelope closeout: each portable PAL/NTSC `MonitorSpec` now
publishes a valid empty display-info Exec list *and* initializes the embedded
`SignalSemaphore` prefix with an empty wait queue, zero owner/nesting/count,
and the public node type. This keeps the guest monitor layout lockable by
future CopperSharp68k/native display-record code without inventing host
pointer fields or claiming CyberGraphX monitor ownership.

G18 monitor-envelope wrap closeout: `OpenMonitor` now rejects odd or
full-envelope-overflowing allocator addresses before clearing or publishing
the resident `MonitorSpec`; a high-address/wrapping-memory regression proves
that low aliases remain untouched and the failed public allocation is rolled
back.

G18 monitor-initialization atomicity closeout: `OpenMonitor` now stages the
complete public `MonitorSpec` prefix and commits it only after every field has
been prepared. If a guest-memory provider rejects a late byte during commit,
the original envelope bytes are restored before the public allocation is
released, so a later allocator reuse or native `MonitorList` walk cannot see a
half-built monitor node. Focused lifecycle coverage injects a late write
failure and verifies byte-for-byte preservation plus the single matching
allocator release.

G18 native-list publication atomicity closeout: when a full guest `GfxBase` is
mapped, `OpenMonitor` now snapshots the resident prefix before the optional
`MonitorList` splice and restores it if a later list-link write fails. The
existing link rollback and a focused late-tail-predecessor fault test together
prove that both the native list and the released allocation remain byte-for-
byte at their pre-open state.

G15/G17 screen-ownership closeout: synthetic `CloseScreen` now clears the
host current-view and guest `GfxBase->ActiView` publication only when the
synthetic view is still active. If a valid foreign prepared `View` was loaded
before teardown, the compatibility screen's copper wrappers and guest links
are retired without revoking that foreign view. Focused AmigaBoot coverage
exercises the cross-owner handoff (the screen/view lifecycle filter now passes
52 tests); ordinary active-synthetic blanking and fresh-open geometry remain
unchanged.

G15/G17 screen-publication closeout: `OpenScreen` now keeps the staged
`Screen` envelope private until its standard-planar or provider-owned bitmap
setup succeeds. A failed plane/RasInfo/BitMap allocation rolls back the guest
links, retires the compatibility Screen handle, and returns the classic NULL
open result instead of publishing a half-built display chain. Focused
AmigaBoot coverage exhausts chip memory while leaving pseudo-fast allocation
available for the public envelope and verifies both the null ABI result and
the cleared compatibility ownership state.

G15/G17 program-envelope closeout: synthetic `OpenScreen` now catches
compatibility program-memory exhaustion while staging the public 0x160-byte
`Screen` prefix and returns the classic NULL result. Mandatory boot-program
allocations retain their existing exception contract; only the recoverable
guest screen request is translated at the Intuition boundary. Focused
AmigaBoot coverage consumes the pseudo-fast list down to a fragment smaller
than the Screen envelope and verifies that no host allocation exception or
synthetic ownership state escapes.

The later-allocation branch is covered by a companion fixture that leaves
enough pseudo-fast memory for the Screen prefix but not the following RasInfo
node. The complete screen-session rollback clears the staged guest links and
handles, and releases an already-registered optional RTG surface through its
provider boundary before the failed open returns.

G04/G06 text-cell closeout: portable `Text` and its destination preflight now
walk the complete font-height template cell, treating rows outside a shorter
decoded glyph strike as source-zero rows. Focused coverage proves that
`JAM1|INVERSVID` paints those empty rows with APen and
`COMPLEMENT|INVERSVID` complements them, while the glyph's source-one pixel
remains untouched. The same unit fixes underline planning so an unstyled
RastPort cannot perform a hidden underline pass that toggles the final cell
row; all 640 graphics scaffold tests pass.

G15/G17 screen-error closeout: accepted synthetic `OpenScreenTagList` requests
now defer their validated `SA_ErrorCode` destination until the staged Screen,
RasInfo, BitMap, and planar backing session either succeeds or rolls back.
Successful opens publish zero; program-memory exhaustion publishes
`OSERR_NOMEM` (3), and standard planar backing exhaustion publishes
`OSERR_NOCHIPMEM` (4). Provider/native declines for unknown display IDs,
custom/public screens, unreadable legacy structures, and malformed tag chains
still preserve the caller's pre-existing error word. Focused AmigaBoot coverage
exercises both allocation classes alongside the existing 26-case
OpenScreenTagList/CloseScreen lifecycle slice, with no CyberGraphX ownership
added to this path ([OpenScreen autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/intuition.library/OpenScreen), [screens.h](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node0602.html)).

G15/G17 depth-error closeout: accepted native OCS/ECS `OpenScreenTagList`
requests with an explicit depth above six planes now return `OSERR_TOODEEP`
(7) through the caller's validated `SA_ErrorCode` pointer before Screen/View
staging. ECS SuperHires retains its documented two-plane compatibility cap and
continues to open through the existing path. Focused coverage verifies the
failure leaves the synthetic screen unallocated, while the complete
OpenScreenTagList slice remains green.

G15/G17 legacy-depth closeout: the stack-based `OpenScreen(NewScreen *)` bridge
now rejects an OCS/ECS request above six planes before synthetic allocation and
returns the classic NULL result. The compatibility rejection is cleared for a
subsequent repaired request; the existing NS_EXTENDED/RTG provider handoff and
ECS SuperHires cap remain unchanged. Focused coverage verifies both the failure
and retry path alongside the 25-case OpenScreenTagList/legacy provider slice.

G15/G17 screen-prefix closeout: the synthetic `Screen` now publishes canonical
Kickstart 3.1 prefix fields (`Title` `0x16`, `DefaultTitle` `0x1A`, `Font`
`0x28`) while retaining the nested `ViewPort`/`RastPort`/`BitMap` offsets
`0x2C`/`0x54`/`0xB8`. Legacy `NewScreen.Font` and tagged `SA_Font` are carried
through as caller-owned `TextAttr *` values; an omitted font receives a
reset-scoped guest `TextAttr` mirroring the compatibility `TextFont`, and an
unreadable pointer declines to the native/provider owner. Focused coverage
proves canonical layout, default attributes, legacy/tagged ownership, and the
malformed-pointer handoff. The combined OpenScreen/lifecycle and graphics
scaffold gate passes 676 tests; the emulator project builds with zero warnings
or errors. CyberGraphX remains outside this portable path.

Shared-layout follow-up: the canonical `Screen`/`NewScreen` prefix is now
owned by `GraphicsLayouts` beside the existing View/ViewPort/RastPort/BitMap
contracts. `AmigaBoot` and the host lifecycle tests consume those constants
instead of duplicating offsets, and a portable layout regression pins the
word-aligned title/font fields plus the nested `0x2C`/`0x54`/`0xB8` offsets for
future CopperSharp68k-native and CopperScreen-host implementations. The
focused OpenScreen/graphics scaffold gate passes 677 tests and the emulator
build remains warning-free.
