G15/G17 tag-precedence closeout: `OpenScreenTagList` now honors the documented
"supplement or override" rule for legacy `NewScreen` fields. An explicit
`SA_Font` (including a NULL override) can replace a malformed legacy
`NewScreen.Font`; without that tag, the malformed caller pointer still leaves
the synthetic path unclaimed for native/provider ownership. Focused coverage
proves both the preserved malformed legacy handoff and the valid override
path, and the combined OpenScreen/graphics gate rises to 678 passing tests
([OpenScreenTagList autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/intuition.library/OpenScreenTagList),
[SA_Font layout](https://d0.se/include/intuition/screens.i)).

G15/G17 system-font precedence closeout: the synthetic screen bridge now
recognizes `SA_SysFont` as the highest-precedence screen-font selector. The
documented values `0` and `1` are accepted and resolve to the reset-scoped
compatibility default because this host has no separate preferences-font
registry; unsupported selector values decline to native/provider ownership.
`SA_SysFont` can therefore override both malformed `NewScreen.Font` and a
valid `SA_Font`, with focused coverage for precedence and rejection. The
combined OpenScreen/graphics gate now passes 681 tests ([OpenScreenTagList
autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/intuition.library/OpenScreenTagList)).

G04/G15/G17 screen-font propagation closeout: the selected `Screen.Font` now
drives the embedded `Screen.RastPort.Font` through the portable guest font
backend, and the shared window `RPort` inherits that same font and cache
metrics. The reset-scoped Topaz compatibility font carries a valid fixed-cell
strike, so screen construction exercises the same accessor increment and
CloseScreen release path as an opened resident font; rollback releases a
partially opened font before retiring the staged Screen. Focused coverage
checks the RastPort/window pointers, TextFont metrics, accessor lifetime, and
caller `TextAttr` ownership. The combined OpenScreen/graphics gate passes 679
tests, and the emulator project remains warning-free.

Resident-font selection regression: a second fixed-cell guest font registered
through the graphics font list is selected by a screen `TextAttr`; both the
Screen and Window RastPorts publish that resident `TextFont`, and CloseScreen
returns its accessor count to zero. This proves the caller-selected path in
addition to the compatibility-default path without changing CyberGraphX
ownership.

G15/G17 request-rejection closeout: `OpenScreenTagList` now preserves a
malformed legacy `NewScreen` depth rejection when unrelated tags are present.
Only an explicit `SA_Depth` may replace that legacy value; otherwise the
synthetic standard-planar path declines before allocating a Screen and writes
`SA_ErrorCode=OSERR_TOODEEP` when requested. This keeps malformed legacy
geometry available to native Intuition/provider ownership instead of silently
clamping it, with focused coverage alongside the explicit-tag and legacy
over-depth cases.

G04 fixed-cell strike-placement closeout: portable `Text` now treats a fixed
`TextFont`'s movement cell and its `CharLoc` strike as separate envelopes. A
strike narrower than the nominal `tf_XSize` cell is centered with the native
integer half-padding rule, while source-zero padding remains addressed at its
original cell columns for JAM, `INVERSVID`, complement, and bold-smear paths.
Reverse-path cells use the same signed movement-cell geometry, and the
destination preflight follows the identical source-column mapping. Metrics
continue to report the nominal movement cell rather than the strike width.
Focused coverage now exercises normal fixed-cell rendering, negative spacing,
inverse/template rows, out-of-range default glyphs, and the complete 640-test
graphics scaffold gate ([Graphics Library and Text](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Graphics_Library_and_Text), [TextFont layout](https://d0.se/include/graphics/text.h)).

G08 per-shape temporary-raster closeout: `AreaEnd` now computes attached or
allocator-backed scratch capacity from the largest individual polygon/ellipse,
while retaining the union bounds only for the destination transaction. Every
recorded shape gets a local 16-pixel-aligned mask envelope that is cleared and
applied before the next shape, so sequential pattern/complement semantics are
preserved without rejecting separated ellipses that fit the largest-shape
`TmpRas`. A focused two-ellipse/`AreaCircle` regression proves a six-byte
caller-owned scratch raster is sufficient for two distant radius-one shapes;
the AreaEnd slice and the full graphics scaffold now pass 640 tests
([AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c)).

G15/G17 open-window refusal closeout: the synthetic Intuition bridge now
tracks an explicit `OpenWindow` claim separately from the private Window-shaped
backing object that `OpenScreen` keeps for presentation. `CloseScreen` returns
`FALSE` and leaves the active View/Screen publication untouched while that
claim is live; `CloseWindow` retires the claim without invalidating the shared
RastPort, and a subsequent `CloseScreen` succeeds. Focused coverage pins the
refusal, ownership-preserving retry, and final blanking path
([CloseScreen autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/intuition.library/CloseScreen)).

G15/G17 pre-open-window linkage closeout: an `OpenWindow` request that precedes
`OpenScreen` now receives a repaired `Window.WScreen` link when the synthetic
Screen is staged, and the Screen publishes that window through
`Screen.FirstWindow`. `CloseWindow` then removes the public first-window link
while retaining only the reset-scoped presentation object. Focused coverage
verifies the pre-open ordering, refusal while the claim is live, and clean
screen teardown.

G15/G17 multi-window-claim closeout: the synthetic bridge now counts explicit
`OpenWindow` claims even though the host presentation reuses one reset-scoped
Window-shaped object. `CloseScreen` remains refused after only one of two
matching `CloseWindow` calls, `Screen.FirstWindow` stays linked until the
final claim retires, and an unavailable guest Window allocation no longer
creates an uncloseable ownership claim. Focused AmigaBoot coverage exercises
two opens, one-close refusal, final detachment, and teardown.

G15/G17 shared-layout closeout: the NewWindow and Window public prefixes are
now defined in the shared portable graphics layout contract. AmigaBoot aliases
those constants, and the layout regression pins the field offsets and minimum
Window prefix size so CopperSharp68k-native and CopperScreen-host paths do not
drift onto different guest structure definitions.

G15/G17 public-window-chain closeout: `CloseScreen` now validates the guest
`Screen.FirstWindow` link in addition to the synthetic open-claim counter. A
foreign/native Window keeps the active View and Screen intact, while the
reset-scoped presentation backing remains an allowed private link. Synthetic
screen construction also suppresses host-only allocation sentinels instead of
publishing them as guest Window pointers. Focused lifecycle coverage and the
640-test graphics scaffold pass on the final tree.

G15/G17 linked-window closeout: the shared guest layout now exposes
`Window.NextWindow` at offset `0x00`. `CloseScreen` rejects a synthetic
backing Window with an unreadable or non-NULL tail, while `CloseWindow`
preserves a readable tail when detaching the compatibility backing. Focused
layout/lifecycle coverage passes five tests, and the graphics scaffold remains
640/640.

G15/G17 linked-window promotion closeout: the final synthetic `CloseWindow`
now has regression coverage for a readable native/provider tail. The
compatibility backing is removed from `Screen.FirstWindow`, the tail remains
published, and the active View is not blanked until that foreign owner removes
its link. The focused lifecycle slice and the complete graphics scaffold
remain green.

G15/G17 linked-window insertion closeout: an explicit synthetic `OpenWindow`
now inserts the compatibility backing ahead of an already-published
provider/native `Screen.FirstWindow` instead of overwriting that head. The
existing chain is restored when the final synthetic claim closes, and an empty
chain clears stale backing-tail state before reuse. Focused lifecycle coverage
pins insertion, promotion, and final screen teardown.

G15/G17 NewWindow ownership closeout: a non-null but unreadable `NewWindow`
pointer now declines the synthetic `OpenWindow` path without creating a Screen,
advancing the display publication, or consuming the caller's cycle boundary.
The null-pointer compatibility request remains available, and a subsequent
valid request proves that the failed provider-owned attempt does not poison the
reset-scoped bridge.

G15/G17 Window.WScreen ownership closeout: `CloseScreen` now also validates
that the compatibility backing's `Window.WScreen` still points to the Screen
being closed. A repointed backing remains available to its guest/provider owner
and keeps the active View untouched; restoring the canonical link makes the
close retryable.

The matching `CloseWindow` path now applies the same guard before decrementing
the synthetic open-claim count or rewriting `Screen.FirstWindow`. A malformed
or foreign-repointed backing therefore remains live until its canonical
`WScreen` link is restored.

G15/G17 viewport-link ownership closeout: `CloseScreen` now validates the
embedded `ViewPort` copper-link quartet before blanking or clearing it. The
compatibility `DspIns` remains accepted when it matches the generated raw list;
a mapped foreign `SprIns`, `ClrIns`, `UCopIns`, or replacement `DspIns` keeps the
active View intact until that provider link is removed. Unmapped stale links
retain the existing cleanup path.

G15/G17 NewScreen alignment closeout: non-null odd `NewScreen` pointers now
decline before any legacy field decoding or display publication. Null requests
and already-active compatibility screens retain their existing behavior, while
the focused retry proves the rejected address-error path cannot poison a later
OpenScreen call.

G15/G17 foreign View identity closeout: synthetic `CloseScreen` now decides
whether it may queue `LoadView(NULL)` from the exact guest `View` address it
owns. A provider/native `View` that reuses the synthetic Screen's embedded
`ViewPort` remains the active publication; CloseScreen still tears down only
the compatibility screen's copper/backing state and leaves
`GfxBase->ActiView` untouched. Focused lifecycle coverage verifies both the
empty foreign View and the shared-ViewPort handoff.

G15/G17 linked-ViewPort ownership closeout: synthetic `CloseScreen` now
validates the embedded `ViewPort.Next` link before clearing copper state. A
readable foreign tail, or an unreadable chain link, keeps the Screen and active
View intact until the provider detaches its display node. Focused coverage
verifies the refusal and preserves both the chain tail and `ActiView`.

G15/G17 RasInfo ownership closeout: synthetic `CloseScreen` now also validates
the canonical `ViewPort.RasInfo` head against the compatibility allocation it
published. A repointed or unreadable source-storage link leaves the Screen,
active View, and foreign RasInfo available for the provider/native owner;
focused coverage verifies the refusal without clearing the link.

The same teardown check validates the RasInfo tail: only the compatibility
dual-playfield node is accepted. A foreign provider tail keeps CloseScreen
pending and preserves the active publication until that chain is detached.

G15/G17 View-CPR ownership closeout: synthetic teardown now validates both
`View.LOFCPRList` and `View.SHfCPRList` before clearing them. Mapped links not
owned by the compatibility CPR registry preserve the active View and remain
available to the provider/native owner; unmapped stale links continue through
the existing cleanup path. Focused coverage verifies refusal and retry after
the foreign link is detached.

The active-view decision now reconciles the guest `GfxBase->ActiView` field
before using the host current-view cache. A native/provider publication made
directly at the guest library boundary remains authoritative and is preserved
by synthetic CloseScreen, with focused direct-publication coverage.

The same teardown validation now requires the synthetic `View.ViewPort` link
to point back to the embedded Screen `ViewPort`. A foreign or unreadable link
keeps CloseScreen pending until the provider restores or detaches it; focused
coverage verifies refusal and retry.

The storage ownership check now also validates the public Screen
`RastPort.BitMap` pointer and every compatibility `RasInfo.BitMap` link before
teardown. A foreign bitmap envelope keeps CloseScreen pending and preserves
the active View until its owner restores the canonical link; focused coverage
verifies both links.

G15/G17 dual-playfield RasInfo-tail closeout: the compatibility second
`RasInfo` is now required to remain a terminal node during `CloseScreen`.
Appending a provider/native tail keeps the close refused and preserves the
active View until that owner detaches its node; focused dual-playfield
coverage verifies refusal and retry after the tail is cleared.

G15/G17 failed-open transaction closeout: `OpenScreenTagList` now resets the
staged synthetic request when Screen-envelope allocation fails, including the
early allocator exception path. The shared default font remains alive, but
geometry, mode flags, palette, title, and per-screen font state return to
profile defaults. A later untagged `OpenScreen` therefore cannot inherit a
request that never published a guest Screen; focused exhaustion/retry coverage
verifies the boundary.

The same reset boundary now covers provider declines discovered after legacy
`NewScreen` fields were decoded (for example, an unreadable tagged `SA_Font`)
and explicit over-depth rejection. The legacy prefix is no longer left staged
behind a native/provider handoff; focused malformed-font retry coverage keeps
the following default open at profile geometry.

G15/G17 legacy-prefix ownership closeout: `OpenScreen(NewScreen *)` now
declines a non-null, unreadable legacy prefix before applying synthetic
defaults or publishing a `Screen`. A separate null request remains available
and starts from the active PAL/NTSC profile geometry; focused coverage checks
the unchanged D0/cycles and the default-geometry retry.

G01/G02 `SetFont(NULL)` ABI closeout: the register adapter now resolves a null
`TextFont *` through the selected guest `GfxBase->DefaultFont` list (or the
compatibility default-font provider) before applying the atomic RastPort cache
update. If no valid default is available, the vector remains unclaimed for
native/provider ownership. Focused coverage verifies default-font selection,
cached height/width/baseline publication, and unchanged D0/cycles.

G01/G02 `CloseFont(NULL)` ABI closeout: the portable vector now treats a null
`TextFont *` as the documented no-op while keeping the lifecycle registry strict
for direct non-null ownership checks. Focused coverage verifies that no guest
font envelope is required and the void-vector gateway publishes deterministic
success without consuming cycles.

G01/G02 native-overlay font ownership closeout: `SetFont(NULL)` now declines
when the mapped overlay has no rebound guest `GfxBase.TextFonts`/`DefaultFont`
backend, so the host compatibility default cannot mutate a native RastPort.
The ordinary host path still uses its explicit compatibility provider, and the
guest-list path remains responsible for native-overlay default-font selection.
Focused coverage verifies the declined D0/cycle-preserving handoff.

G02 text-cache ownership closeout: `SetFont` now preserves the caller-owned
`RastPort.TxSpacing` value while atomically publishing the selected font and
its width, height, and baseline cache. The complete cache envelope is still
preflighted and rollback-safe for malformed or failing guest memory, and
focused direct/overlay parity coverage now treats unchanged spacing as the
expected Kickstart-compatible result.

G01 initializer follow-through: `InitRastPort` now retains the zeroed
`TxSpacing` word when it publishes the compatibility default font. This keeps
the initializer aligned with its clear-then-`SetFont` contract; backend font
metadata no longer overwrites caller-owned spacing during initialization.

G05 soft-style null-state closeout: `AskSoftStyle` now returns zero for a
readable null `RastPort.Font`, matching the classic empty-state query while
still declining unreadable RastPorts and non-null fonts that the selected
backend cannot decode. Pure and CopperStart register coverage pins the result
and unchanged cycle boundary.

G15/G16 structure-alignment closeout: View, ViewPort, RasInfo, TmpRas, and
BitMap initialization now reject odd guest structure bases before any clear or
field publication. View/ViewPort/RasInfo validation and the shared planar
RastPort decoder apply the same 68k word-alignment boundary, leaving odd
chains and display requests unclaimed for native/provider ownership instead of
byte-processing a structure that would raise a native address error. Focused
pure and register coverage verifies unchanged guest bytes, D0, and cycles.

G06/G08 AreaInfo alignment closeout: the AreaInfo descriptor and its planar
coordinate vector table now require even guest addresses during initialization
and collector-state decoding. Odd descriptors remain byte-for-byte untouched,
and forged odd vector streams are declined before AreaMove/AreaDraw can read
coordinate words, preserving the native 68k address-error/provider handoff.
Focused pure coverage verifies both refusal paths while the complete portable
graphics scaffold remains green (647 tests).

G01/G06 RastPort alignment follow-through: `InitRastPort` now applies the same
word-aligned structure boundary as its text, line, and bitmap consumers. A
mapped odd RastPort is left untouched and the register adapter declines it with
the original D0/cycle state, keeping a future CopperSharp68k/native vector in
control of the real 68000 address-error behavior.

G03 text-gateway ownership closeout: the register `TextLength` path now
distinguishes the zero-font cached-metric compatibility state from a nonzero
guest `TextFont` pointer. A nonzero pointer that the selected font backend
cannot decode is declined before the cached width/spacing fallback can claim
it, preserving D0/cycles for native Kickstart or another provider. Valid
decoded-font and null-font fixed-metric paths remain unchanged; focused gateway
coverage and the portable graphics scaffold pass (648 tests).

G03 text-result alignment closeout: the shared `TextExtent` result envelope
used by `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent` now requires an even guest
address before any word-field read or publication. Odd result buffers remain
byte-for-byte untouched and the register adapter preserves D0 for native or
provider ownership, matching the 68000 address-error boundary. Focused direct
and register coverage passes with the portable graphics scaffold (650 tests).

G02 text-font alignment closeout: decoded `TextFont` pointers used by
`SetFont`, text metrics, text rendering, and soft-style queries now require an
even guest address before the selected backend is consulted. This keeps a
foreign odd pointer from being accepted merely because a host font provider
can describe it, preserving the native 68000 address-error/provider handoff.
Focused coverage proves the metric gateway leaves D0 unchanged for this
malformed state.

G15 extended-node allocation closeout: `GfxNew` now validates the allocator's
returned public address before clearing or publishing a `ViewExtra`,
`ViewPortExtra`, `SpecialMonitor`, or `MonitorSpec` envelope. Odd addresses and
ranges that would wrap the 32-bit guest space are released immediately and
remain available to the native/provider implementation. Focused lifecycle
coverage verifies both rejection paths and the portable graphics scaffold now
passes 651 tests.

The extended-node association hash now applies the same rule to its public
View/ViewPort pointer: odd association targets are rejected and cannot enter
the registry or be returned by `GfxLookUp`.

G15/G14 tag-chain alignment closeout: the `BestModeIDA` display-query tags,
synthetic `OpenScreenTagList`, `SetRPAttrsA`/`GetRPAttrsA`, sprite-tag, and
best-pen tag walkers now reject odd `TagItem` addresses and odd `TAG_MORE`
continuations before reading a longword. This preserves the native 68000
address-error handoff for screen/display and attribute requests instead of
byte-processing a malformed chain. Focused screen/display and portable
graphics coverage passes (653 tests in the combined filter).

G19/G24 RTG RastPort ownership closeout: the host/provider classifier now
follows a readable `RastPort.BitMap` link through the registered bitmap
ownership callback. A CyberGraphX bitmap therefore keeps every planar
drawing vector on the provider/native path even when no separate per-RastPort
callback is installed; malformed or unreadable RastPorts remain unclaimed.
Focused coverage verifies preserved D0/cycles for a bitmap-backed RTG
`RastPort` while the explicit `isRtgRastPort` callback path remains unchanged.

G18 native-base monitor publication closeout: when a full guest `GfxBase`
envelope is supplied, `OpenMonitor` now appends each portable PAL/NTSC
`MonitorSpec` to the real `GfxBase.MonitorList`, publishes the default monitor
pointer for default-profile opens, and preserves the resident links after
`CloseMonitor` reaches zero. The compact host image remains untouched when
the private GfxBase tail is not mapped, while malformed or partially
initialized native list state declines publication. Focused coverage verifies
empty-list initialization, PAL-to-NTSC tail linking, default pointer
publication, and retained links after both monitors close.

G20 native sprite-envelope alignment closeout: simple and extended sprite
vectors, their optional viewport link, and `AllocSpriteDataA` source BitMaps
now require even guest bases before any word/long field is decoded. Odd
envelopes remain byte-for-byte untouched and stay available to the native
68000/provider owner, matching the alignment guards already used by the
RastPort, View, ViewPort, and BitMap paths. Focused pure coverage verifies
failed odd `GetSprite`/`MoveSprite` calls preserve guest coordinates and do not
consume a sprite-pool slot.

G17 native active-view sidecar closeout: when a full guest `GfxBase` base is
provided, the portable `LoadView` path now publishes `GfxBase->ActiView`
before the scheduler/display handoff and restores the previous pointer if a
status-aware display backend declines. `LoadView(NULL)` clears the same field,
while the compact host image skips the optional write when the field is not
mapped. Focused lifecycle coverage verifies view activation, blanking, and
malformed-request preservation without changing the guest View envelope.

Repeated active-view requests now repair an externally edited mapped
`GfxBase->ActiView` sidecar without republishing or re-queuing the unchanged
display stream. The timed and untimed idempotent paths share this guarded
writability/commit boundary; an unavailable compact-image field remains an
optional no-op. Focused coverage verifies the repair and the unchanged display
publication count.

G14 native ColorMap-allocation alignment closeout: `GetColorMap` now requires
the allocator to return even, non-null guest addresses for the public ColorMap,
ColorTable, and LowColorBits envelopes before clearing or publishing any
registry entry. `AttachPalExtra` applies the same word-alignment rule to its
viewport input and the public PaletteExtra, reference-count, and allocation-list
sidecars. Every rejected odd allocation remains provisional until all returned
addresses are released, so allocator failure/rollback cannot leak a partial
palette envelope or publish a malformed pointer. Focused coverage exercises each
odd allocation position plus an odd viewport; the focused palette set passes
4/4, the complete portable graphics scaffold passes 832/832, the AmigaBoot
suite passes 255/255, and the emulator project builds with zero warnings or
errors. Native Exec semaphore ownership, ROM palette error metrics, and
scheduler-visible OCS/ECS palette timing remain explicit G14 parity gates.

G17 active-view ordering closeout: timed and untimed status-aware `LoadView`
now commit the mapped `GfxBase->ActiView` pointer before invoking the display
publication owner, so a scheduler callback observes the same guest View that
it is asked to queue. If that owner declines, the prior pointer is restored;
the compact host path remains an optional no-sidecar boundary. Focused pure
coverage verifies callback observation, decline rollback, and timed-cycle
propagation.

G09/G24 RTG friend-bitmap closeout: the CopperStart `AllocBitMap` admission
boundary now declines an allocation whose `Friend_BitMap` is explicitly owned

provider callback, while a mapped native overlay still tail-chains it to the
captured Kickstart vector. Focused coverage verifies the provider receives the
original friend/geometry registers and CPU cycle without a portable planar

G12 queue-envelope closeout: `QBlit` and `QBSBlit` now reject odd guest

G09 raster alignment closeout: `AllocRaster` now rejects and releases an odd

The raster remains a word-stride guest envelope, so malformed odd allocations

G14 palette-lock closeout: ColorMap reads, single-entry mutations, bulk

Focused concurrency coverage proves that two callbacks for one owned map never

G14 native sidecar/list-corruption closeout: pen-sharing operations now

color matching, area-pattern publication, temporary-raster traversal, full
destination rollback, and the signed result ABI remain in the shared planar
implementation, while the exact Layers-supplied ClipRect fragments gate
visible writes and the public layer head is ignored.

G05/G11 layer BltTemplate closeout: validated layered `BltTemplate` now shares
the portable clipped template decode, selected-plane preflight, draw-mode
publication, and rollback through the projected layer-local bitmap. The exact
Layers-supplied ClipRect fragments gate destination bytes and the void D0 ABI
is normalized only after success; malformed template spans remain an explicit
decline boundary for native/provider ownership.

G05/G08 layer AreaEnd closeout: validated layered `AreaEnd` now uses the
portable scanline area transaction through the projected layer-local bitmap.
Recorded polygon fill, temporary-raster acquisition, destination preflight,
collector reset, rollback, and the void D0 ABI remain shared with the standard
planar path; exact Layers-supplied ClipRect fragments gate visible publication.

G10/G11 layer `BltBitMapRastPort` closeout: validated layered bitmap-to-port
blits now consume the supplied destination ClipRect head while reading the
source directly from the guest BitMap argument. The portable planar minterm,
write-mask, destination preflight, overlap ordering, and undo journal remain
shared with the standard path; a clipped source-to-destination regression
proves that a poisoned public `Layer.ClipRect` cannot widen the write span.

G10/G11 layer `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` closeout: standard planar layered
destinations now reuse the portable mask-plane/minterm transaction through the
projected layer-local BitMap. The supplied ClipRect head limits publication,
the destination undo journal remains atomic, and the void D0 ABI is normalized
only after success. RTG endpoints still use the CyberGraphX-aware provider
path; a focused regression proves masked visible pixels, clipped tail bits,
source preservation, and mask preservation.

G10/G11 masked-blit plane-selection closeout: the portable
`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` core now reads the destination `RastPort.Mask` and
applies its intersection with the participating source/destination depth to
both the destination snapshot and publication journal. A multi-plane
regression proves an unselected destination plane remains byte-for-byte
untouched while the selected plane receives the masked minterm result; the
projected standard-planar layer path inherits the same rule.

G10/G11 masked-blit admission closeout: the same effective plane mask now
controls source/destination plane preflight and pixel staging. A malformed
source or destination plane excluded by `RastPort.Mask` therefore cannot block
the selected-plane operation or force a provider decline; focused coverage
leaves both excluded planes unmapped while the selected plane is updated.

Historical note: the two masked-blit plane-selection entries immediately
above describe an intermediate implementation and are superseded by the
2026-08-13 conformance correction at the end of this plan. Kickstart's
`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` ignores `RastPort.Mask`; the current portable core
therefore restores all common-plane participation and uses only the external
one-bit stencil as its pixel gate.

G04 zero-length Text gateway closeout: the register adapter now claims
`Text` with a zero signed-WORD count as the portable empty-string no-op before
reading the text pointer, RastPort, font, or provider ownership fields. The
focused malformed-pointer regression confirms D0 normalization without
touching guest memory; non-empty Text admission remains unchanged.

G04 scheduler-layer closeout: the production CopperStart Layers gateway now
claims the same zero-count `Text` no-op before resolving a layer endpoint or
entering `LayersRasterCore`. A valid layered RastPort with an unmapped text
pointer therefore completes with D0 cleared, unchanged cycles, and no layer
provider execution; non-empty calls still use the guarded layer/provider
path.

The compatibility Exec gateway now publishes `AddLibrary`/`RemLibrary`
requests into the active guest Exec library list instead of treating them as
memory-allocation compatibility shims. This keeps synthetic and native-style
library discovery on one guest-owned list, while ROM takeover continues to
use its dedicated Exec service. The focused graphics/layers/Exec gate now
passes 799 tests after excluding the scheduler-lock and provider-ABI
baselines; the full Amiga run remains limited to the existing
Denise/DMA/CIA/event-journal/boot-memory/JIT baseline (3,941 passed, 40
failed, 12 skipped; 3,993 total in the latest run).

G15/G17 explicit-monitor geometry closeout: `OpenScreenTagList` now carries a
named PAL/NTSC monitor part through the same screen-geometry boundary used by
`QueryOverscan`. An explicit PAL display ID on an NTSC host therefore gets PAL
standard height (and vice versa), while the zero monitor-part default continues
to resolve against the active machine profile. The change is limited to the
synthetic standard-planar lifecycle; RTG/custom display IDs remain unclaimed.
The monitor-part decode is now shared by the two host entry points, and a
cross-profile `QueryOverscan` regression proves a named PAL mode retains PAL
geometry on an NTSC host. The focused OpenScreen/QueryOverscan slice passes 5
tests, the graphics scaffold remains green at 742 tests, and the emulator
build is warning-free. The latest Amiga test-project run is 3,944 passed, 39
failed, and 12 skipped (3,995 total); the failures remain confined to the
unrelated CIA/Denise/DMA/event-journal/JIT families, and the added lifecycle
regression is green.

G05/G07 layered `SetRast` visibility closeout: the validated layer path now
uses the supplied visibility predicate for both destination preflight and its
rollback snapshot. An unmapped bitmap row outside the admitted layer
fragments therefore cannot reject a clipped fill, while a late write failure
still restores every visible selected-plane byte. The ordinary non-layered
path retains its complete-raster probe and plane snapshot. Focused planar
overlay, complement-mode, and malformed-hidden-row coverage passes 3 tests;
the graphics scaffold is green at 743 tests, the layer raster/boot slice is
green at 49 tests, and the test-project build remains warning-free.

Verification update: after adding the visibility regression, the direct
`CopperMod.Amiga.Tests` project run completed with 3,945 passed, 39 failed,
and 12 skipped (3,996 total). The added SetRast test is green; the remaining
failures are the pre-existing CIA/Denise/DMA/event-journal/JIT families.

G05/G07 clipped-shape snapshot closeout: visibility-aware region snapshots
now serve `BltPattern`/`RectFill` and `DrawEllipse` as well as `SetRast`.
Their existing per-pixel preflight and publication predicates now cover the
same selected-plane bytes as rollback, so an unmapped row outside a validated
layer fragment cannot reject a clipped shape. Ordinary planar callers retain
the byte-span snapshot fast path. Focused shape/overlay coverage passes 5
tests; the combined graphics/layer slice passes 794 tests, and the direct
Amiga test-project run is 3,948 passed, 38 failed, and 12 skipped (3,998
total), with failures remaining in the unrelated chipset/CIA/event-journal/JIT
families.

G05/G07 clear-vector visibility closeout: `ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` now
apply the validated layer predicate to region preflight, snapshot journals, and
the existing `FillRectangle` publication path. The non-layered `ClearScreen`
path retains its complete-plane snapshot, while clipped layer clears no longer
probe hidden/unmapped rows. Focused clear coverage passes 6 tests; the
combined graphics/layer slice passes 796 tests; the direct Amiga test-project
run is 3,950 passed, 38 failed, and 12 skipped (4,000 total), with the
remaining failures confined to the unrelated chipset/CIA/event-journal/JIT
families.

G05/G07 `ScrollRaster` visibility closeout: `ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF`
now apply the validated layer predicate to destination preflight alongside the
existing destination snapshot and write paths. Source staging remains in the
logical caller rectangle and is intentionally not visibility-filtered, preserving
overlap and source-coordinate semantics. Focused scroll coverage passes 7 tests;
the combined graphics/layer slice passes 797 tests; the direct Amiga
test-project run is 3,949 passed, 40 failed, and 12 skipped (4,001 total), with
remaining failures confined to unrelated chipset/CIA/event-journal/JIT
families.

G03 `FontExtent` declared-range closeout: a decoded font that cannot provide
any glyph inside its declared `LoChar..HiChar` range now fails closed instead
of silently computing a partial width from the remaining entries. The guest
`TextExtent` result remains unchanged on that failure, preserving the native /
provider handoff boundary. The focused graphics scaffold passes 749 tests after
the regression; the combined graphics/layer slice passes 798 tests, and the
direct Amiga test-project run is 3,953 passed, 37 failed, and 12 skipped (4,002
total). The remaining failures are confined to the existing CIA/Denise/DMA/
event-journal/JIT baseline.

G15/G17 optional screen-payload closeout: `OpenScreenTagList` now fully
preflights present nonzero `SA_DClip`, `SA_Pens`, `SA_Colors`, and
`SA_Colors32` payloads before `NewScreen` fields or synthetic screen state are
staged. Unmapped, malformed, cyclic, or unterminated payloads decline to the
native/provider owner without writing `SA_ErrorCode`, changing the palette, or
publishing a partial screen. The focused malformed-payload theories pass 6
cases, the complete `OpenScreenTagList` lifecycle slice passes 38 tests, the
combined graphics/layer slice remains green at 798 tests, and the emulator
build is warning-free. CyberGraphX ownership is unchanged.

G15/G17 screen-title ownership closeout: legacy `NewScreen.DefaultTitle` and
effective tagged `SA_Title` pointers are now preflighted through the same
bounded 80-byte title prefix consumed by the synthetic renderer before screen
state is staged. An unreadable legacy title declines the ordinary `OpenScreen`
path; an explicit readable `SA_Title` may replace that malformed legacy field,
while an unreadable effective title leaves `SA_ErrorCode` and synthetic state
untouched. Focused lifecycle coverage passes the malformed legacy, override,
and malformed-tag cases; the complete `AmigaBootMemoryTests` class passes 221
tests and the combined graphics/layer slice remains green at 798 tests.

G15/G17 screen-tag capability-boundary closeout: the standard screen bridge now
uses the Kickstart `screens.h` numbers for `SA_ShowTitle`, `SA_Behind`,
`SA_Quiet`, `SA_AutoScroll`, and `SA_Pens`. A narrow normalization step keeps
the earlier host-shim spellings working for existing guests without exposing
those aliases as public ABI. Recognized V39/V40 attributes whose list,
layer-hook, attachment, Workbench-preference, or unsupported VideoControl
forms are not implemented (`SA_Parent`, `SA_Draggable`, `SA_Exclusive`,
`SA_BackFill`, child-screen tags, `SA_LikeWorkbench`,
`SA_Reserved`, `SA_MinimizeISG`, and the obsolete monitor-name tag) now
decline before any legacy fields, palette, or `SA_ErrorCode` are published.
`SA_Type=PUBLICSCREEN` and other non-custom types follow the same native/public
screen handoff; unknown tags remain forward-compatible and are ignored.
Canonical and legacy-alias tests plus twelve unowned-attribute theories pass;
the complete `AmigaBootMemoryTests` class passes 235 tests, the focused
OpenScreen slice passes 71 tests, and the combined graphics/layer slice remains
green at 798 tests. The emulator build is warning-free.

G15/G17 legacy screen-ownership closeout: ordinary `OpenScreen(NewScreen)` now
declines legacy `PUBLICSCREEN` and `CUSTOMBITMAP` type bits before staging a
synthetic screen. `OpenScreenTagList` may replace a legacy public type only
with an explicit custom `SA_Type`; it can never erase caller-owned bitmap
storage. Two lifecycle theories cover the legacy public/custom-bitmap cases,
bringing the `AmigaBootMemoryTests` class to 237 passing tests and the focused
OpenScreen slice to 73. The broader graphics/layer slice remains at 798
passing tests; the full direct project run remains the unrelated 39-failure
chipset/CIA/event-journal/JIT baseline (3,974 passed, 12 skipped, 4,025 total).

G15 provider-handoff hardening: the compatibility normalizer no longer treats
a null value on the overlapping `0x44..0x47` screen tags as a legacy boolean.
Those canonical V39/V40 pointer attributes therefore remain unowned even when
the caller explicitly supplies a null pointer; only the retained legacy TRUE
spelling is normalized. Four null-pointer ownership theories pass, the complete
`AmigaBootMemoryTests` class passes 241 tests, and the emulator build remains
warning-free.

G15/G18 extended-viewport handoff closeout: the portable OCS/ECS path now
declines any nonzero `ViewPort.ExtendedModes` value before mode derivation,
`ScrollVPort`, or `LoadView` chain validation. This keeps the private extended/
AGA escape hatch available to a future native or monitor provider instead of
falling back to a standard mode record. The focused handoff regression passes,
the combined graphics/layer slice passes 799 tests, and the emulator build is
warning-free.

G18 monitor-family ownership closeout: the display database now names the
canonical VGA, A2024, prototype, Euro72, Euro36, Super72, DBLNTSC, and DBLPAL
monitor parts while keeping them outside the portable OCS/ECS records. Find/
availability/OpenMonitor queries for each family decline with the native/provider
boundary intact; one focused theory passes and the graphics scaffold passes 751
tests. No CyberGraphX monitor records are synthesized.

G07 `ScrollRasterBF` clipped-source closeout: the portable backfill path now
detects when logical-coordinate clipping leaves no source pixels for the
visible destination. It delegates one complete visible rectangle to the
transactional `EraseRect` path, so oversized displacements and rectangles
whose origin is off-screen cannot leave stale pixels in the unfilled tail.
The existing full-width displacement regression and a new clipped/oversized
case pass; the combined graphics/layer slice passes 801 tests and the emulator
build remains warning-free. A fresh direct Amiga test-project run passes 3,983
tests, skips 12, and retains 39 failures only in the pre-existing CIA,
Denise/DMA, event-journal, and JIT families; no graphics/layer failure appears
in that run.

G18 `DTAG_MNTR` resident-monitor closeout: native display-info queries now
resolve a PAL/NTSC `MonitorInfo.Mspc` through the same resident `MonitorSpec`
registry used by `OpenMonitor`, even when the caller has not opened that
monitor explicitly. The portable registry lazily creates the resident node
with an already-zero open count, preserves an existing open count,
and leaves foreign/unsupported monitor families unclaimed. Pure and
CopperStart-register coverage verifies the pre-open pointer, open-count
reuse, post-close persistence, and direct/gateway parity; the combined
graphics/layer slice passes 802 tests and the emulator build remains
warning-free. This follows the public display-info contract in which
`MonitorInfo.Mspc` points at the monitor specification returned by
`OpenMonitor` ([displayinfo.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/displayinfo.h),
[Display Database](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Display_Database)).

The subsequent full `CopperMod.Amiga.Tests` run completed with 3,985 passed,
38 failed, and 12 skipped (4,035 total); no graphics or layer test failed.
The remaining failures stayed within the established CIA, Denise/DMA,
event-journal, and M68k JIT baseline families.

G18 `DTAG_MNTR` atomic resident closeout: lazy display-info resolution now
initializes a newly published PAL/NTSC `MonitorSpec` with an open count of
zero, rather than taking a temporary open/close reference. This removes the
late-close write-failure window that could otherwise leave a query-created
resident object counted as caller-open. An unmatched `CloseMonitor` is
covered as a no-op failure against the zero-count resident; subsequent
`OpenMonitor` still reuses the same address and increments the public count.
The focused display-database and combined graphics/layer suites remain green.

G18 lazy-resident fault-injection closeout: a guest memory adapter that rejects
the `MonitorSpec.ms_OpenCount` word write used by `CloseMonitor` no longer
causes `DTAG_MNTR` to fail or leak its allocation. The query-created resident
is published directly at count zero, and the focused display suite now passes
16 tests; the combined graphics/layer slice passes 803 tests.

G05 RastPort `SetMaxPen` closeout: the portable setter now publishes the
contiguous planar mask implied by every nonzero maximum pen, including a
request that widens a mask previously narrowed by `SetWriteMask` or an
earlier `SetMaxPen`. A zero maximum leaves the current mask unchanged, as in
Kickstart. Direct, `SetRPAttrsA`, and reversible native-overlay paths share
the rule; the focused graphics/layer slice passes 803 tests and the updated
`RPTAG_MaxPen` query regression is green.

Verification update: the emulator build remains warning-free. The focused
graphics/layers slice passes 803/803. The subsequent full Amiga test-project
run is 3,985 passed, 39 failed, and 12 skipped (4,036 total); the added
`SetMaxPen` coverage introduces no graphics failure. The 39-failure sample
contains the established CIA, Denise/DMA, event-journal, and M68k JIT
families plus one unrelated `OpaqueResourceLedger...` layer-ledger sample;
that isolated layer test passes when rerun, so the sample is retained as a
baseline/noise disposition rather than attributed to this graphics change.

G08 zero-capacity collector closeout: `InitArea` with `maxVectors == 0` now
publishes a coherent empty `AreaInfo` instead of becoming unreadable at the
next portable vector. `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, and `AreaEllipse` still fail
without changing the zero-capacity collector, while `AreaEnd` succeeds as the
documented empty no-op. The pointer/flag-table relationship and address
guards remain active, so the new empty success does not widen malformed guest
ownership. Pure and register-boundary regressions pass; the combined
graphics/layer slice is now 805/805 and the emulator build remains
warning-free.

G09 compact-`BitMap` closeout: `InitBitMap` now follows the resident field
sequence and snapshots only the eight-byte geometry/header prefix. The
caller-owned `Planes[]` table is never read or cleared by this constructor, so
even a currently unmapped plane table does not block geometry publication;
bitmap consumers retain their declared-depth plane-span checks. Pure and
CopperStart gateway coverage proves sparse direct/register publication and
atomic late-write rollback. This follows [AROS `InitBitMap`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initbitmap.c).

G10 compact-`BitMap` reader parity: direct `BltBitMap`, `BitMapScale`, sprite
source extraction, animation-buffer setup, and viewport color sharing now
validate the fixed header and the declared-depth plane-pointer envelope rather
than demanding the unused eight-plane tail. End-of-guest-memory depth-one
blit and scaler fixtures prove that no tail bytes are read; existing full
envelopes remain unchanged, and the geometry/query reader accepts the same
compact envelope even when the public `BMF_STANDARD` marker is retained. The
combined graphics/layer slice passes 810/810 and the emulator build remains
warning-free. This extends the `BMF_MINPLANES`
allocation contract described by the [AllocBitMap autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node02A0.html)
across every portable bitmap consumer touched by this unit.

Repository-wide verification after this unit is 3,992 passed, 39 failed, and
12 skipped (4,043 total, including the newly added graphics cases). The
failures remain confined to the established CIA, ECS Denise/DMA, CPU event
journal, and M68k JIT baseline families; no graphics or layer test failed.

G17 extended-screen error handoff closeout: `OpenScreenTagList` now resolves
`SA_ErrorCode` from the explicit tag list and the `ExtNewScreen` chain with the
same precedence used by the other screen attributes. An accepted legacy
extended open therefore initializes the caller's error word instead of
silently dropping an extension-owned destination. The focused regression also
closes the screen and verifies the published zero success code; the emulator
build remains warning-free.

Repository-wide verification after the handoff passes 3,994 tests, with 38
failures and 12 documented skips (4,044 total). No graphics or layer test
failed; the remaining failures are confined to the established CIA, ECS
Denise/DMA, CPU event-journal, and M68k JIT baseline families.

The same screen-tag boundary now preflights a nonzero `SA_ErrorCode` as an
even, four-byte caller-owned destination. An odd, wrapped, or unmapped output
pointer declines before synthetic screen publication, while a valid pointer
from either the explicit or extension chain is retained through completion.
Focused regressions cover both the extension success write and malformed
destination handoff.

The screen-tag error destination now also has an explicit precedence fixture:
when both the public tag list and an `ExtNewScreen` chain provide
`SA_ErrorCode`, the public list's destination is initialized and the extension
destination remains untouched. The screen is then closed through the normal
synthetic lifecycle, proving that precedence does not leave a stale ownership
handle behind. The AmigaBoot screen-memory class passes 244/244, and the
emulator build remains warning-free.

G15/G18 display-name closeout: `GetDisplayInfoData(DTAG_NAME)` now
NUL-terminates a short copy that ends inside the fixed `NameInfo.Name[32]`
payload, while preserving header-only and full-chunk behavior. A focused
regression covers the bounded guest write and the existing display-database
suite remains green; RTG/CyberGraphX display records stay provider-owned.

G15/G27 viewport-mode ownership closeout: `GetVPModeID` now uses a
status-aware portable probe at the register boundary. Valid standard-planar
ViewPorts publish their profile-aware native ModeID, including `INVALID_ID`
for a readable but unsupported native state; malformed or RTG/provider-owned
ViewPorts decline with D0/cycles untouched so the resident or monitor
provider can take over. The value-only core helper remains available for
host callers that intentionally consume `INVALID_ID`.

G18/G27 mode-selection result closeout: `BestModeIDA` now distinguishes a
well-formed native request with no matching OCS/ECS record from malformed or
provider-owned input. The former claims the vector and publishes the
documented `INVALID_ID`; cyclic/unreadable tag lists, malformed viewport or
source records, and foreign monitor families still decline with D0/cycles
untouched. Focused mode-selection coverage proves both the no-match result
and the existing malformed-list fallback.

G18/G27 coercion result closeout: `CoerceMode` now uses the same status-aware
boundary. A validated standard viewport whose requested geometry/depth has
no compatible PAL/NTSC record claims the vector and publishes `INVALID_ID`;
malformed viewports, unsupported native mode keys, and foreign monitor
families decline with registers/cycles preserved. The focused coercion slice
covers both the valid no-match result and the existing provider fallback.

G18/G27 direct-overlay parity closeout: the native overlay and direct host
entry points now share focused coverage for the mode-selection result split.
Both `BestModeIDA` and `CoerceMode` publish `INVALID_ID` for a well-formed
depth-eight no-match request while preserving the caller cycle, and both
paths continue to leave malformed requests available for resident/provider
fallback. The mode-selection parity fixture passes alongside the full
display-database slice (35/35 focused, 813/813 combined graphics/layer, and
244/244 AmigaBoot screen-memory tests); the emulator build remains
warning-free.

G15/G17 standard-dimension sentinel closeout: explicit `OpenScreenTagList`
width/height values of `$FFFFFFFF` and legacy `NewScreen` UWORD values of
`$FFFF` now resolve `STDSCREENWIDTH`/`STDSCREENHEIGHT` against the active
OCS/ECS display clip (mode, PAL/NTSC family, interlace, and
`SA_DClip`/`SA_Overscan` precedence). A tag-list open with no legacy structure
derives the clip edge when no explicit position is supplied; a legacy
`NewScreen` keeps its caller-supplied left/top while replacing only the
sentinel dimensions. Direct and tag-list regressions cover PAL hires and ECS
NTSC cases, including normal close lifecycle. The AmigaBoot screen-memory
class passes 247/247 and the emulator build remains warning-free.

G15/G17 legacy-sentinel precedence correction: when `OpenScreenTagList`
combines a legacy `NewScreen` carrying `$FFFF` dimensions with `SA_DClip`, the
custom clip now supplies the resolved width/height while the caller's legacy
`LeftEdge`/`TopEdge` remain authoritative. This matches the documented
NewScreen-present position rule and keeps the no-NewScreen display-clip edge
default separate. A focused regression covers the combined sentinel/DClip
request and normal close lifecycle.

G15/G27 screen-assembly query closeout: `GetVPModeID` now uses a dedicated
viewport envelope probe that accepts a complete `ViewPort` before its
`RasInfo` link is attached. A present RasInfo chain is still walked and
malformed/cyclic nodes remain unclaimed, while `ScrollVPort`, DBufInfo
allocation, bitmap switching, and `LoadView` retain their stricter chain
requirements. Direct and host-register regressions cover the unlinked state;
`ViewPort.ExtendedModes` remains provider-owned.

G02/G03 text RastPort-alignment closeout: the portable text/font-state paths
now reject odd RastPort bases before consuming cached font, spacing, or style
fields. `SetFont`, `AskSoftStyle`, `SetSoftStyle`, `TextLength`, `TextExtent`,
and `TextFit` therefore leave an odd guest object for native 68000/provider
ownership even when the host memory adapter can byte-read it. The zero-count
`Text` ABI no-op remains unchanged. Pure and register regressions cover both
decoded-font and null-font fixed-metric states; the combined graphics/layer
slice passes 816/816, AmigaBoot screen-memory tests pass 249/249, and the
emulator build remains warning-free.

G15/G27 ColorMap ownership closeout: the native `GetVPModeID` fallback now
checks the viewport's `ColorMap` association after any explicit mode backend.
Null maps remain valid during screen assembly, and registry-owned maps retain
the native profile-aware mapping; a nonzero foreign or unreadable association
declines with D0/cycles untouched so a monitor, native ROM, or future
CyberGraphX patch can claim it. Pure-core and register-adapter regressions
cover the same handoff, while existing owned-map and unlinked-viewport cases
remain green.

G01/G06 drawing RastPort-alignment closeout: the shared byte/word/long
RastPort helpers now reject odd bases before drawing-state access. Pen and
draw-mode setters/getters, write-mask/max-pen, outline-pen, and `Move` all
leave odd guest objects unclaimed; area and primitive paths reusing those
helpers inherit the same CopperSharp68k/native 68000 boundary. Pure state
regressions verify no mutation, and register tests preserve D0/cycles for the
provider handoff.

G01/G06 no-op ownership closeout (superseded by the 2026-08-14 G05 slice
below): the earlier boundary validated the RastPort mask byte before taking
the no-op path. The source-backed Kickstart behavior is now authoritative:
`SetMaxPen(rp, 0)` returns before RastPort access, including for odd or
truncated guest addresses.

G17 ColorMap publication closeout: direct portable `LoadView` now walks every
linked viewport and requires each non-null `ColorMap` to be owned by the active
graphics registry before publishing the view. Null maps remain valid during
screen assembly, and an explicit status-aware display backend remains the
provider handoff for foreign maps. Direct and register regressions verify the
foreign-map decline, while the explicit provider path still observes the
guest view and cycle.

G17 ColorMap envelope closeout: native `GetVPModeID` and direct `LoadView`
ownership probes now require a registered ColorMap's complete public structure
range to remain readable, not merely that its address appears in the local
registry. An owned-but-truncated map therefore remains available to a native
ROM or provider with D0/cycles and prior display state untouched. The focused
mode/publication regression covers this fail-closed path alongside the foreign
map handoff.

G01/G06 pixel-result ownership closeout: `ReadPixel` and `WritePixel` now have
status-aware portable boundaries in addition to their value-only helpers. A
valid outside-RastPort coordinate still claims the documented `-1` result,
while an odd/truncated RastPort or missing declared plane declines before the
register adapter changes D0 or cycles, leaving the malformed object available
to a native 68000/provider path. Pure value semantics, register ownership, and
direct-versus-overlay behavior remain covered; the graphics scaffold slice
passes 783/783, AmigaBoot screen-memory tests pass 250/250, and the emulator
build remains warning-free.

G19/G27 pixel-array ownership closeout: the V36 pixel-line and pixel-array
register gateways now preflight the standard-planar RastPort envelope before
claiming the vector, while preserving the classic `-1` result for a valid
RastPort whose guest array or clipped request fails. Odd/truncated bitmap
headers therefore retain D0/cycles for native/provider ownership, but valid
clipped-count and malformed-array result semantics are unchanged. Pure and
register regressions cover the split; the graphics scaffold passes 784/784,
AmigaBoot screen-memory tests pass 250/250, and the emulator build remains
warning-free.

G02 `WeighTAMatch` source/design correction: a `FPF_DESIGNED` request now
accepts a disk-backed candidate even when that candidate is not marked
`FPF_DESIGNED`, while a non-disk constructed candidate remains unsuitable.
This preserves the Kickstart source-qualified rule: `FPF_DISKFONT` is an
eligible source for a designed request, whereas a host/ROM constructed font
must carry the explicit designed-size bit. The focused matcher regression
covers both cases; the emulator build remains warning-free.

G03/G04 text-span admission closeout: after low-word gateway normalization,
`TextLength`, `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `Text` validate the complete guest
character span before entering font decoding or rendering. Forward requests
may end exactly at `0xffffffff`, while reverse `TextFit` requests may end
exactly at address zero; any request that would wrap the 32-bit guest address
space is rejected without changing the metric result or rendered state. The
portable core retains widened counts for direct host tests, but the guest
WORD/UWORD fields bound register calls. The existing spacing and
reverse-string contracts are unchanged.

G02 `WeighTAMatch` source-rule correction: the designed-request gate now
accepts a candidate carrying `FPF_DISKFONT` even when `FPF_DESIGNED` is clear,
while still rejecting a non-disk constructed candidate. This matches the
Kickstart/AROS source rule that disk-backed fonts are an eligible source for a
designed request, rather than requiring the independent designed-size bit.
The regression covers the exact designed candidate, the constructed disk
candidate, and the constructed non-disk rejection; the graphics scaffold
passes 786/786, the AmigaBoot screen-memory suite passes 250/250, and the
emulator build remains warning-free.

G02 resident-font name closeout: portable `OpenFont` now compares a request
against the resident `TextFont` node name exactly, matching the source list
search. It no longer strips `FONTS:`/directory prefixes or folds case while
selecting an already-loaded font; path normalization remains limited to the
compatibility-only Topaz default check. A focused regression proves that a
basename request does not open a path-bearing resident node, while the exact
stored name remains selectable. This keeps `OpenDiskFont` path lookup out of
the graphics.library resident-list contract; the graphics scaffold passes
787/787, the AmigaBoot screen-memory suite passes 250/250, and the emulator
build remains warning-free.

G14 `FindColor` ULONG-limit closeout: only `maxpen == 0xffffffff` selects the
attached `PaletteExtra` sharable span. Other high-bit `ULONG` limits, including
`0xfffffffe` and `0x80000000`, clamp to the complete ColorMap as Kickstart's
unsigned comparison does, so sprite/pointer entries remain searchable. Pure
coverage proves the sentinel and both ordinary large-limit cases; the focused
test passes and the emulator build remains warning-free.

G09 interleaved `BitMap` ABI closeout: `AllocBitMap` now publishes the full
interleaved row stride in `BytesPerRow`, derives the physical per-plane stride
for all portable readers, and fails the ECS/AGA request when the required
contiguous block is unavailable while preserving OCS's ignore rule. `FreeBitMap`,
bitmap blits, bitmap utilities, display-layout validation, and pixel primitives
all use the derived physical stride; `BMA_WIDTH` uses the per-plane geometry.
The regressions cover aggregate header width, a depth-2 interleaved
WritePixel/ReadPixel at a nonzero row, one-block teardown, and transactional
failure/provisional-address cleanup. The graphics scaffold remains green and
the emulator build remains warning-free.
This matches the V39 `AllocBitMap`/`GetBitMapAttr` storage and width contract
([AllocBitMap autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/AllocBitMap.html),
[GetBitMapAttr autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/GetBitMapAttr.html)).

G09 OCS/ECS capability closeout: `AllocBitMap` now receives the active
display-chipset capability. OCS requests clear `BMF_INTERLEAVED` and allocate
ordinary separate planes; ECS/AGA retains the aggregate interleaved layout.
The synthetic `OpenScreenTagList` lifecycle applies the same rule before it
publishes the Screen/BitMap envelope, so an OCS `SA_Interleaved` request does
not leak an ECS-only flag to native-style callers. Pure allocator coverage,
an OCS capability fixture, and the A500 screen lifecycle regression pass;
the graphics scaffold is 791/791, AmigaBoot screen-memory tests are 250/250,
and the emulator build remains warning-free.

G09 synthetic ECS row-layout closeout: the ECS/AGA synthetic screen writer now
uses a true contiguous row-interleaved backing layout. It publishes the
aggregate `BytesPerRow`, places successive plane pointers at physical
per-plane offsets within each row, and makes host pixel writes use the
aggregate row stride; OCS remains separate-plane. The new ECS lifecycle
regression verifies the aggregate header value, `BMF_INTERLEAVED`, and plane
pointer spacing. The graphics scaffold remains 791/791, AmigaBoot
screen-memory tests are 251/251, and the emulator build remains
warning-free.

G12 status-callback closeout: CopperStart's blitter context now exposes
optional status-returning callbacks for ownership, wait, and queued submission.
The adapter gives those callbacks precedence over the legacy void `Action`
callbacks, so contention or a scheduler queue refusal leaves the five blitter
vectors unclaimed with D0/cycles and guest `bltnode` bytes unchanged. A host
regression covers decline and subsequent success while preserving QBS beam-sync
metadata. The portable `IGraphicsBlitterBackend` remains unchanged; actual
FIFO execution, completion signaling, and custom-chip timing remain open G12
provider/scheduler gates. The graphics scaffold is 792/792 and the emulator
build remains warning-free.

G12 timed-FIFO boundary: the portable core now forwards the CPU call cycle to
an optional `IGraphicsTimedBlitterBackend`. `GraphicsBlitterFifoBackend` gives
CopperStart/native schedulers one bounded V39+ QBlit/QBSBlit FIFO with
deterministic ownership, submission-cycle retention, strict submission order,
explicit beam predicates, in-flight completion, and cycle-aware `WaitBlit`.
The new
`CopperStartGraphicsBlitterScheduler` is wired into AmigaBoot instruction
boundaries: it wakes on the custom-chip blitter completion or QBS beam line,
enters the queued function with A0=`$DFF000` (custom-chip register base) and
A1=`bltnode`, repeats while D0 is nonzero,
waits for hardware idle, then enters the optional cleanup callback before
releasing the FIFO head. It re-registers its continuation gateway after bus
reset and keeps malformed/mutated nodes fail-closed. Focused coverage verifies
the callback contract in addition to capacity refusal, FIFO and beam gating,
completion, register-cycle propagation, and a real custom-chip callback that
programs the Agnus blitter through A0 and holds the queue until BBUSY clears.
The graphics scaffold is 819/819,
the lifecycle slice is 49/49, the boot slice is 253/253, and the emulator build
remains warning-free; exact ROM callback instruction timing and
profile-specific arbitration remain the next G12 provider gates.

G15/G17 close-screen handoff closeout: synthetic `CloseScreen` now treats the
blanking `LoadView(NULL)` publication as part of the ownership transaction. If
that handoff is declined by a future native/custom-chip display provider, the
screen envelope, active `View`/`ActiView` publication, and copper ownership are
left intact for a provider retry; teardown proceeds only after the blanking
request succeeds. The existing frame-boundary lifecycle regression remains
green (graphics scaffold 818/818, screen/lifecycle slice 49/49, boot-memory
slice 253/253).

G09 raster ABI closeout: the portable register adapter now consumes the
documented UWORD width/height arguments of `FreeRaster` from the low halves of
D0/D1. `AllocRaster` continues to accept its ULONG dimensions, while native
overlay ownership checks and chip-span reconstruction use the truncated
FreeRaster words. A regression with nonzero high register words proves that a
valid allocation is still released with its original 16-pixel-aligned byte
count and that the void D0/cycle boundary is preserved
([FreeRaster autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/FreeRaster.html)).
The graphics scaffold is now 793/793 and the emulator build remains
warning-free.

G14 palette ABI closeout: `SetRGB4CM` and `SetRGB4` now consume their
documented signed WORD pen indices from the low half of D0. Nonzero high words
no longer turn a valid low-word entry into an out-of-range palette access; a
low-word `$FFFF` still remains the documented negative-index failure. Direct
ColorMap and ViewPort regressions cover both vectors, and the graphics
scaffold is now 794/794
([SetRGB4CM autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/SetRGB4CM.html),
[SetRGB4 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/SetRGB4.html)).

G08 Flood ownership closeout: the non-layered `Flood` register adapter now
distinguishes the portable success status from its internal `-1` failure
sentinel. Malformed or out-of-range planar requests therefore remain
unclaimed with D0/cycles unchanged for native Kickstart or a provider, while
valid fills and explicit layer-provider results retain their existing result
ABI. Focused pure, host, and direct-vs-overlay Flood coverage remains green.

G15 `SA_VideoControl` screen-lifecycle closeout: the synthetic
`OpenScreenTagList` path now admits the Kickstart V39/V40 VideoControl tag
after structurally validating its guest TagItem list. A screen carrying the
tag receives an instance-owned portable ColorMap sized from its native depth,
publishes the ViewPort/ColorMap association, and applies the existing
graphics.library VideoControl transaction before the Screen is returned.
Malformed lists, semantic failures, and allocation failures roll back the
Screen/BitMap/ColorMap session without claiming the request or writing
`SA_ErrorCode`; successful opens publish the deferred zero result only after
the complete transaction commits. CloseScreen releases the ColorMap through
the graphics service boundary. Coverage includes flag application, malformed
pointer decline, error-code preservation, and close-time teardown; the
AmigaBoot screen-memory suite passes 252/252, the graphics scaffold passes
795/795, and the emulator build remains warning-free. CyberGraphX and native
monitor/provider ownership remain outside this slice.

G15 `SA_ColorMapEntries` completion: the synthetic screen path now accepts a
bounded V39 entry-count request, allocates the requested ColorMap even when
no VideoControl list is supplied, and publishes the same ViewPort/ColorMap
association used by the VideoControl path. Zero and over-256 counts remain
provider-owned and decline before any Screen state is staged. The new screen
palette regression verifies an eight-entry map and close-time release; the
AmigaBoot screen-memory suite passes 253/253 and the emulator build remains
warning-free. Depth-derived maps retain Kickstart's default of `max(32,
1<<depth)` when the explicit entry-count tag is absent.

G15 `SA_FullPalette` acceptance closeout: the standard screen tag is no
longer classified as an unowned Intuition feature. Its presence now causes
the synthetic screen path to allocate the full depth-derived ColorMap (or
honors an explicit `SA_ColorMapEntries` size), publish the ViewPort/ColorMap
association, and release it through CloseScreen. The compatibility host does
not invent a separate Preferences database; palette values remain the
existing OCS/ECS preference boundary, while custom/public/RTG ownership still
declines to native or provider code. Focused screen ABI coverage verifies the
32-entry depth-two map and close-time teardown.

G20 extended-sprite allocation failure closeout: a structurally valid
`GetExtSpriteA` request that asks for the next available hardware sprite now
records the documented unassigned `SimpleSprite.num` sentinel (`0xffff`) when
the eight-slot pool is exhausted, matching the existing `GetSprite` failure
contract while still returning `-1`. Explicit-number and already-reserved
attached-pair failures retain their guest numbers so the established
transactional pair semantics remain stable; malformed/foreign envelopes still
decline before mutation for native/provider ownership. Focused pure coverage
exhausts the shared pool and verifies the sentinel; the documented
`GSTAG_SOFTSPRITE`/`GSTAG_SCANDOUBLED` display-provider forms remain open and
are not guessed in the portable core. The graphics scaffold passes 796/796,
the AmigaBoot screen-memory suite passes 253/253, and the emulator build is
warning-free.

G03 kerning-path closeout: `TextFit` now includes `CharKern` in the effective
per-glyph cursor step used by its stall/reversal guard. Kerning-induced stalls
or reversals therefore publish an empty fit instead of claiming a prefix based
only on `CharSpace` plus `TxSpacing`, keeping the fit path consistent with
`TextExtent` and rendering.

G19 BitMapScale sampling closeout: the planar scaler now derives its centered
DDA samples from the requested source/destination factors, matching the
classic `bms_srcpos()` phase for both enlargement and reduction. Extent-based
sampling happened to match common 2:3 expansion but selected the wrong source
columns for ratios such as 1:2; a regression proves the duplicated source pen
lands in the native destination columns. RTG/CyberGraphX bitmap ownership
remains at the provider boundary.

G09 ECS/AGA bitmap-width closeout: portable `AllocBitMap` now rejects widths
above 32760 pixels when the active display capability is ECS/AGA, matching the
Kickstart V39+ allocation guard. The OCS path intentionally retains the
classic no-check behavior. A paired regression proves the ECS rejection occurs
before any allocation while OCS still creates and tears down the same request
with the expected aligned row stride ([AllocBitMap autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/AllocBitMap.html)).

V36 pixel-array ABI closeout: the portable `ReadPixelLine8`,
`WritePixelLine8`, `ReadPixelArray8`, and `WritePixelArray8` paths now model
their documented UWORD coordinates/counts as non-negative `int` values. The
CopperStart register adapter consumes the low words unsigned for the native
planar core; layered/provider callbacks remain separate signed-provider
contracts. A regression sends a valid `$8000` count through both line vectors
and proves the request is claimed and clipped by the 16-pixel planar bitmap,
while the direct/overlay parity test now verifies that `$fffe` is the unsigned
coordinate 65534 rather than a negative x origin. The graphics scaffold passes
802/802 and the emulator build remains warning-free
([ReadPixelLine8 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixelLine8.html),
[WritePixelLine8 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixelLine8.html),
[WritePixelArray8 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixelArray8.html)).

G19 V40 signed-stride closeout: `WriteChunkyPixels` now carries its
documented signed LONG `bytesperrow` through the portable core, CopperStart
register adapter, and layer-provider bridge. Negative/high-bit strides are
rejected before source-array probing or planar mutation, while valid positive
strides retain the explicit-row layout and void D0 ABI. Pure, register, and
layer-provider coverage is green (804 graphics scaffold tests); the emulator
build remains warning-free
([WriteChunkyPixels autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WriteChunkyPixels)).

G07 SetRast mask closeout: focused coverage now proves that `SetRast` writes
the requested pen with copy semantics while honoring `RastPort.Mask` across
multiple planar bits. The existing transactional implementation therefore
matches the classic write-mask rule; no provider or RTG ownership is inferred
from this standard-planar behavior
([Graphics Primitives — RastPort Write Mask](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Graphics_Primitives)).

G01/G06 `SetOutlinePen` ULONG-input closeout: the portable core, tag-list
setter, CopperStart register adapter, and direct host path now carry the full
ULONG pen argument to the semantic boundary. Only the low byte is committed
to the classic `RastPort.AOlPen` field, while `AREAOUTLINE` and the previous
byte-sized result retain their existing ABI. High-bit pure and register
coverage proves valid calls claim and publish the low-byte state; malformed
RastPorts still leave D0/cycles untouched for native/provider ownership. The
graphics scaffold remains green at 804 tests and the emulator build is
warning-free ([AROS `SetOutlinePen`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setoutlinepen.c)).

G01/G06 pen/mode ULONG-input closeout: `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`, and
`SetABPenDrMd` now carry full ULONG values through the portable core,
`SetRPAttrsA`, CopperStart register adapter, and direct host boundary. The
semantic layer commits only the low byte to the byte-sized RastPort fields,
while preserving minterm recomputation, line-pattern restart, rollback, and
void D0 behavior. High-bit pure and register regressions prove the guest state
is byte-accurate after a successful claim. The graphics scaffold passes 804/804
and the emulator build remains warning-free
([AROS `SetAPen`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c),
[AROS `SetBPen`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setbpen.c),
[AROS `SetDrMd`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setdrmd.c),
[AROS `SetABPenDrMd`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setabpendrmd.c)).

G07 `SetRast` ULONG-input closeout: the portable core, CopperStart adapter,
direct host path, and validated layer-provider contract now carry the full
ULONG pen value. Only the low byte is used for planar color selection; the
existing write-mask, copy-mode, visibility, rollback, and void-D0 behavior are
unchanged. Pure standard-planar and layered high-bit regressions prove the
claimed paths preserve the full provider input while publishing byte-accurate
guest pixels. The graphics scaffold remains green at 804/804 and the emulator
build is warning-free ([AROS `SetRast`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setrast.c)).

G06 layered line ownership closeout: the pure `Draw` and `PolyDraw` entries
now read `RastPort.Layer` and decline a nonzero layer unless an explicit
provider visibility predicate is supplied. CopperStart already routes mapped
layered vectors to layers/native callbacks; the additional core guard prevents
a direct CopperSharp68k-compatible caller from bypassing that clipping,
damage, and backing-store boundary and painting the planar bitmap directly.
The regression verifies both calls preserve the cursor and destination when no
provider is present. Standard-planar clipping and line-pattern phase behavior
are unchanged, and the graphics scaffold passes 805/805 with a warning-free
emulator build.

The same G06/G07 direct-core ownership guard now covers `ReadPixel`,
`WritePixel`, and `SetRast`: a nonzero `RastPort.Layer` is rejected unless the
operation has an explicit provider visibility predicate. The CopperStart
adapter continues to route layered vectors to the provider, while pure
standard-planar helpers cannot bypass layers/native clipping or damage
tracking. The regression proves these calls leave the backing planes untouched;
the graphics scaffold remains 805/805 and the emulator build is warning-free.

G06/G08 direct-core layer guard closeout: `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`,
`AreaEllipse`, `AreaEnd`, and seed `Flood` now reject layered RastPorts before
collector, temporary-raster, or destination state is touched. Layered callers
continue through the explicit layer backend, preserving the separation between
standard-planar semantics and layers-library clipping/damage policy. Focused
graphics coverage remains 805/805 and the emulator build is warning-free.

G04/G05 text ownership closeout: direct portable `Text` now rejects a layered
RastPort unless an explicit visibility predicate is supplied. CopperStart
continues to route layered text to the layer backend; standard-planar glyph,
draw-mode, cursor, and rollback behavior are unchanged. Focused graphics
coverage remains 805/805 and the emulator build is warning-free.

Validated layer execution now supplies an explicit `allowLayered` collector
path for `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`, `AreaEnd`, and `Flood`. This
path is reachable only after LayersRaster endpoint validation and logical
memory projection; ordinary `GraphicsLibraryCore` calls remain fail-closed on
layered RastPorts. The 49-test `CopperStartLayersBootTests` slice is green.

G19/G24 pixel-array ownership closeout: the pure/core wrappers now apply the
same direct-vs-layered claim boundary as the register adapter for
`ReadPixelLine8`, `WritePixelLine8`, `ReadPixelArray8`, `WritePixelArray8`,
and `WriteChunkyPixels`. A nonzero `RastPort.Layer` declines before caller
array probing or planar mutation, while the explicit LayersRaster provider
continues to receive validated layered requests. Focused coverage proves the
failure sentinel, status-aware decline, and unchanged guest bytes; the
graphics scaffold is now 806/806. CyberGraphX and provider clipping remain
outside this native-planar slice.

Native CopperSharp68k layout closeout: the shared guest image contract now
exposes the complete Kickstart-era `GfxBase` tail through the native
0x220-byte envelope, including `current_monitor`, `MonitorList`,
`default_monitor`, the monitor-list semaphore, `DisplayInfoDataBase`, and the
active-view semaphore offsets. The existing compact 0xF0 CopperScreen image
is unchanged; callers that deliberately request the full native image receive
an initialized empty Exec `MonitorList` with self-consistent head, tail, and
tail-predecessor sentinels. A focused image-layout regression covers the
sentinel bytes, and the graphics scaffold remains green at 808/808. Runtime
monitor-list publication continues to validate the native list envelope while
the separate private display-database sidecar owns only an explicitly empty
`GfxBase.DisplayInfoDataBase` APTR.

Native image-builder opt-in closeout: `NativeGraphicsLibraryImageBuilder`
retains the compact 0xF0 image by default but now accepts an explicit positive
image size. The full 0x220 option flows through the actual resident/image
builder, initializes the native `MonitorList` sentinels, and publishes the
matching positive-size word; a focused regression covers that path while the
existing compact-image and headless 68k vector fixtures remain unchanged. The
graphics scaffold is green at 809/809 and the emulator build is warning-free.

Native HUNK image-builder opt-in closeout: `NativeGraphicsLibraryHunkBuilder`
now accepts the same explicit positive-image size, carries it into the
AUTOINIT resident, and emits relocation records for the full native
`MonitorList` self-pointers when the 0x220 envelope is selected. Compact HUNK
output retains its original relocation set. A loader-level regression verifies
that the relocated list sentinels survive segment mapping; the graphics
scaffold is green at 810/810, the lifecycle boot slice is 49/49, and the
emulator build remains warning-free.

Native-base handoff closeout: native graphics takeover now rebinds the
portable core's GfxBase-dependent registries in the same transaction as the
