guest font-list rebind. `GfxNew` extended nodes publish the discovered native
library back-pointer, `OpenMonitor` splices into the native `MonitorList`, and
the `LoadView` active-view sidecar uses the native base instead of retaining the
compatibility image address. Overlay disposal restores the original base for
all three registries. A focused regression covers the extended-node and
monitor-list split-base case; the graphics scaffold is now 811/811.

Native display-database handoff closeout: the full native-base takeover now
publishes a private, self-describing guest sidecar for
`GfxBase.DisplayInfoDataBase` when the APTR is empty. Its magic/version/size/
count header and contiguous native ModeID table provide a stable
CopperScreen/CopperSharp68k bridge layout without claiming undocumented ROM
database internals. Existing Kickstart/provider pointers are preserved;
allocation and APTR writes are transactional, and disposal clears/frees only
sidecars still owned by the bridge. Focused ownership/idempotence/rollback
coverage is green; the graphics scaffold is now 813/813, the lifecycle slice
is 49/49, the boot slice is 253/253, and the emulator build remains warning-
free.

Timed blitter FIFO closeout: the portable core now forwards the guest CPU cycle
to an optional `IGraphicsTimedBlitterBackend`. `GraphicsBlitterFifoBackend`
provides a bounded scheduler-owned queue with deterministic ownership,
submission-cycle retention, strict FIFO head selection, explicit QBS beam
predicates, in-flight completion, and cycle-aware `WaitBlit`. The
`CopperStartGraphicsBlitterScheduler` is wired into AmigaBoot instruction
boundaries, enters the function and optional cleanup with A0=`$DFF000`
(custom-chip register base) and A1=`bltnode`, repeats while D0 is nonzero,
waits for hardware idle, enters optional cleanup, and releases the FIFO head
through its dedicated continuation gateway. It re-registers after bus reset and
drops malformed or guest-mutated nodes without host faults. Focused coverage
verifies the callback/cleanup contract in addition to queue capacity, order,
beam gating, completion, and register-cycle propagation. The graphics scaffold
is now 819/819, the lifecycle slice is 49/49, the boot slice is 253/253, and
the emulator build remains warning-free. A focused callback regression now
programs the real custom-chip blitter through A0 and verifies BBUSY-gated
completion; exact ROM callback instruction timing and profile-specific
arbitration remain the next G12 provider gates.

G15/G17 `CalcIVG` closeout: the CopperStart/native display boundary now
implements the Kickstart 3.1 arithmetic from the archived Commodore source.
Each compatibility `DspIns` stream records its generated display-instruction
prefix separately from appended `UCopIns`; `CalcIVG` charges four monitor color
clocks per display instruction, rounds up by the selected PAL/NTSC monitor
timing, preserves the legacy two-line OCS/ECS floor, and applies interlace or
scan-double scaling. Unbuilt, foreign, RTG, malformed, or provider-owned
viewports still return the documented zero/unclaimed result. Focused PAL and
interlace regressions are green, the emulator build remains warning-free, and
the graphics scaffold count is unchanged apart from the new lifecycle tests.

G20 provider-form closeout: `GetExtSpriteA` and `ChangeExtSpriteA` now parse
and structurally validate `GSTAG_SOFTSPRITE`/`GSTAG_SCANDOUBLED` requests before
crossing a typed `IGraphicsSpriteBackend` callback. Ordinary hardware forms
remain in the portable OCS/ECS transaction; a provider can claim a software or
scan-doubled form with its own sprite number/result, while a native-overlay
decline leaves the original Kickstart vector unclaimed. Host compatibility
mode preserves the prior `-1`/false-shaped fallback when no provider is
connected. CopperStart context coverage proves the decoded tag flags, handles,
and result ABI reach the provider without fabricating scheduler or display-DMA
state; exact profile-specific scan-doubling and active-View publication remain
provider-owned. The focused graphics scaffold is green at 821/821 and the
emulator build remains warning-free.
G19 native `BitMapScale` alignment closeout: the portable scaler now rejects
odd non-null source or destination plane pointers before publishing either
destination extent word. Source row addressing keeps the guest `WORD * WORD`
stride product wide until the final 32-bit guest-address check, preventing
large valid rows from wrapping into a low alias. Null source planes remain
legal for the classic source form; destination planes remain strict. Focused
graphics coverage is green at 822/822 and the emulator build remains
warning-free.

G10 large-stride blit closeout: portable `BltBitMap` source/destination pixel
staging now keeps `row * BytesPerRow + byte-in-row` arithmetic wide until the
final 32-bit guest-address check. Signed-WORD blit coordinates can reach rows
above 32767 in a full-UWORD bitmap, so the old host-`int` product could wrap
and either decline a valid copy or address an unrelated low byte. The sparse
high-address regression covers the late row and destination minterm write;
the graphics scaffold is green at 823/823, the lifecycle slice at 255/255,
and the emulator build remains warning-free.

G19 endpoint-range closeout: V36 pixel-array width/height derivation now
rejects endpoint spans above `uint.MaxValue` before narrowing. A full signed
32-bit endpoint span can no longer truncate to zero and claim a no-op, while
the maximum UWORD register rectangle remains a claimed `-1` failure after
bounded array-envelope checks. Direct and register regressions verify that
the source array and planar destination remain unchanged; the graphics
scaffold is green at 824/824.

G10 native blit alignment closeout: standard planar `BltBitMap` validation
now rejects odd ordinary source-plane and destination-plane pointers before
TempA selection, source staging, or destination mutation. Null and
`$FFFFFFFF` remain legal source-plane constants; ordinary planar streams
retain the 68000 word-address rule. The shifted-overlap regression now uses
two even bases with a two-byte alias, preserving the TempA proof while the
graphics scaffold is green at 825/825.

G09 native header-alignment closeout: `AllocBitMap` now rejects an odd public
`BitMap` header immediately after allocation, releases the provisional public
span, and leaves guest memory and the register frame untouched. The header's
WORD/LONG fields therefore remain consumable by a native 68000 even when a
host allocator is deliberately byte-addressable. Direct and CopperStart
register coverage prove the release/decline boundary; aligned headers with
odd chip planes still publish a usable non-displayable standard bitmap. The
graphics scaffold is green at 826/826.

Latest verification: the G08 allocator-backed temporary-raster alignment
closeout and the G10/G11 overlapping `TempA` guest-span closeout are green in
the focused regressions. The graphics scaffold is now 839/839, the
`AmigaBootMemoryTests` slice is 255/255, and `CopperMod.Amiga.Emulator` builds
with zero warnings and zero errors. The broad G02-G27 parity and native
CopperSharp68k cutover gates remain intentionally open.

G14 precision-arithmetic closeout: `ObtainBestPenA` now accepts any
non-negative `OBP_Precision` value, not only the four named header presets,
while preserving `PRECISION_EXACT` as the special zero-distance mode. The
precision square is evaluated in a 64-bit intermediate before the
free-entry-scaled comparison, so custom tolerances follow the reference
`best_distance * pe_NFree <= precision^2 * pe_SharableColors` expression
without host overflow. Focused coverage proves precision 8 shares an exact
threshold match and precision 7 allocates the remaining free pen; the
graphics scaffold remains 840/840 after this slice. Exact Kickstart color
distance calibration, Exec semaphore ownership/contention, and scheduler-
visible palette publication remain open G14 parity gates.

G14 palette-reference closeout: the host shadow for `PaletteExtra.pe_RefCnt`
now uses WORD entries and permits the full native `UWORD` range instead of
stopping at 255. Guest synchronization already publishes two-byte entries;
the new regression acquires one shared pen 256 times and verifies the guest
WORD count and shared-list cardinality. The graphics scaffold is now 841/841,
the `AmigaBootMemoryTests` slice remains 255/255, the emulator build remains
warning-free, and `git diff --check` reports no whitespace errors. Exec
semaphore ownership/contention, ROM color-distance calibration, and
scheduler-visible palette publication remain open G14 parity gates.

G06 Draw-mode closeout: standard-planar `Draw` now preserves `COMPLEMENT`
when `JAM2` emits the BPen for source-zero line-pattern samples, matching the
native whole-line inversion rule. Pure-core, CopperStart register, and
connected-line regressions pass; the graphics scaffold is now 842/842, the
`AmigaBootMemoryTests` slice remains 255/255, the emulator build has zero
warnings and zero errors, and `git diff --check` reports no whitespace
errors. Provider clipping/layer damage and the remaining broader G06/G07
edge-parity gates remain open.

G14 semaphore-ownership closeout: palette operations now project the current
Exec task identity into the public `PaletteExtra` `SignalSemaphore` while the
host allocation lock is held. A same-task re-entry increments and restores
`ss_NestCount`; a foreign owner or corrupt owner/nesting pair declines without
changing ColorMap or semaphore state so native Exec can perform the blocking
path. Host-only callers without a task identity retain the compatibility lock
behavior. Direct and CopperStart register regressions cover acquisition,
re-entry, contention, D0/cycle preservation, and unchanged palette bytes; the
graphics scaffold is now 843/843, `AmigaBootMemoryTests` remains 255/255, and
the emulator build has zero warnings and zero errors. Native queue wake-up,
full Exec semaphore blocking, ROM color-distance calibration, and scheduler-
visible palette publication remain open G14 gates.

G15/G17 single-screen ownership closeout: the synthetic Intuition bridge now
declines a second legacy `OpenScreen` or tagged `OpenScreenTagList` request
while its private Screen session is live instead of returning the existing
Screen pointer or applying replacement geometry to its active ViewPort. The
decline preserves the live Screen dimensions, guest `GfxBase->ActiView`, and
tagged `SA_ErrorCode` destination for native/provider ownership; after the
normal `CloseScreen` frame-boundary teardown, a fresh open still allocates a
new guest topology. Focused AmigaBoot coverage passes 256/256, the graphics
scaffold remains 843/843, and the emulator build has zero warnings and zero
errors. Multi-screen Intuition/public-screen list ownership remains outside
the private compatibility session.

G15/G18 display-database header closeout: native `GetDisplayInfoData` records
now publish `QueryHeader.Length` as the local payload size in 8-byte
double-longword units, excluding the 16-byte header, matching the
`graphics/displayinfo.h` contract used by callers to advance across a query
chunk. Direct and ROM-overlay coverage checks DisplayInfo, DimensionInfo,
MonitorInfo, and NameInfo lengths; the broader display-database
property/timing and monitor-list parity gates remain open.

G15/G18 capability-flow closeout: `ModeNotAvailable` now carries the active
OCS/ECS capability through its mode-resolution step instead of relying on a
hard-coded supported-chipset argument. Display records remain enumerable on an
OCS-only host, while SuperHires reports `DI_AVAIL_NO_CHIPS` consistently through
both direct core dispatch and the mapped register gateway; CyberGraphX/foreign
monitor ownership remains unclaimed.

G15/G17 ScreenToFront handoff closeout: the synthetic Intuition bridge now
recognizes its own live Screen as an explicit activation request. After
`LoadView(NULL)` or another temporary display publication clears the active
view, `ScreenToFront` re-enters the same scheduler-aware `LoadView` owner used
by OpenScreen/RethinkDisplay, restoring `GfxBase->ActiView` and the generated
copper source while leaving foreign screens on the provider viewport-selection
seam. Focused boot coverage proves the standard-planar Screen/View is
republished after a blanking handoff; multi-screen Intuition/public-screen
ownership remains outside the private compatibility session.

G06 `ONE_DOT` line-mode closeout: the portable `Draw` and its complete
destination preflight now model RastPort `ONE_DOT` as the blitter
`ONEDOT`/`SING` rule—at most one published dot per horizontal raster row—rather
than suppressing samples only on the selected major axis. The traversal still
advances line-pattern phase over every Bresenham sample, so shallow patterned
lines preserve native continuity while emitting one dot per row. Focused pure
coverage exercises a shallow line, verifies the first sample on each row,
phase advancement, and persistent `ONE_DOT` state; the broader provider
clipping and remaining line parity gates remain open ([blitter `ONEDOT`
definition](https://d0.se/include/hardware/blit.h)).

G03/G04 empty-metric closeout: `TextExtent` now preserves the native split for
zero-length strings. Fixed-cell fonts publish an empty horizontal rectangle
(`MinX=0`, `MaxX=-1`), while proportional or kerning-backed fonts retain their
zero-width movement cell (`MinX=0`, `MaxX=0`) and apply algorithmic bold/italic
expansion before publication. Focused coverage proves the styled proportional
case without changing the existing fixed-cell envelope; full metric edge and
provider/native parity remain open ([AROS `TextExtent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textextent.c)).

G03 zero-count TextLength closeout: a decoded-font `TextLength` request with
`count == 0` now returns zero after validating the selected `TextFont`, without
consuming the cached `RastPort.TxWidth` word. The compatibility NULL-font path
continues to use the cached fixed-cell fields, while a malformed non-null font
remains unclaimed. A fault-injected regression proves that a stale/unreadable
cache cannot steal an otherwise valid empty query; the graphics scaffold is
now green at 848/848, the `AmigaBootMemoryTests` slice at 257/257, and the
emulator build remains warning-free.

G01/G06 private pen-state closeout: portable `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`,
and `SetABPenDrMd` now model the private `RPF_NO_PENS` bit (`RastPort.Flags`
bit 14 / `0x4000`). Successful setters clear only that bit, preserve unrelated
Flags state, and publish the change in the same transaction as minterm
recomputation and line-pattern restart. Late Flags-byte failure restores the
old pen, pattern count, minterms, and complete Flags word; `SetRPAttrsA`
includes both Flags bytes in its tag-list rollback snapshot. Focused pure
coverage proves all four setters and the injected late-write rollback. The
graphics scaffold is now green at 851/851, `AmigaBootMemoryTests` remains
257/257, and the emulator build is warning-free. The broader G01/G06 drawing,
provider, and native parity gates remain open ([AROS private flag](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h), [`SetAPen`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c), [`SetBPen`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setbpen.c), [`SetABPenDrMd`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setabpendrmd.c)).

G03 `TextFit` height-gate closeout: the alternate-width/height form now
publishes a successful empty extent immediately when `constrainingBitHeight`
is smaller than the selected `TextFont.tf_YSize`, before it walks the guest
string or asks the font provider for glyphs. This matches the native
short-circuit and keeps malformed glyph storage from converting a valid
zero-fit into a claimed failure. Explicit `TextExtent` constraints retain
their existing authoritative path. Focused coverage proves the output is
cleared for a missing glyph, the graphics scaffold is now green at 852/852,
the `AmigaBootMemoryTests` slice remains 257/257, and the emulator build has
zero warnings and zero errors ([AROS `TextFit`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textfit.c)).

G03 zero-count `TextFit` closeout: an empty string now publishes the empty
`TextExtent` before reading `TxSpacing` or `AlgoStyle` and ignores the
alternate width/height fields, matching the native `strLen && ...` admission
guard. Fault-injected coverage proves a truncated spacing word cannot steal a
valid zero-count query. The graphics scaffold is now green at 853/853, the
`AmigaBootMemoryTests` slice remains 257/257, and the emulator build has zero
warnings and zero errors; the broader text/provider and native parity gates
remain open ([AROS `TextFit`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textfit.c)).

G03 metric-provider envelope closeout (2026-08-12): decoded metric movement
now retains the guest field widths at the portable boundary. Advances supplied
by a `tf_CharSpace` table must fit the signed WORD contract; fonts without that
table may use the unsigned `tf_XSize` cell, including the negative reverse-path
form. `TextLength`, `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent` reject a host-only
advance outside those envelopes before publishing a result, so a provider
cannot smuggle an arbitrary 32-bit movement into the CopperSharp68k-compatible
metric ABI. Focused coverage exercises a signed-CharSpace overflow across all
three RastPort metric vectors and the standalone `FontExtent` path; broader
metric/provider and native weighting parity remain open ([AROS
`TextLength`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textlength.c), [AROS
`TextExtent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textextent.c)).

G02/G03 signed-size closeout (2026-08-12): `WeighTAMatch` now sign-extends
both guest `ta_YSize` words before calculating the size penalty, preserving
the Kickstart/AROS behavior for high-bit font sizes instead of treating the
fields as host unsigned integers. Focused coverage proves the `$FFFF` versus
`$0001` signed-difference edge and the existing direct/register matcher contract; exact native
weight calibration and broader font failure parity remain open ([AROS
`weightamatch.c`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/weightamatch.c)).

G03/G04 `SetFont` state closeout (2026-08-12): the portable font switch now
updates only the selected guest `TextFont` pointer and cached `TxWidth`,
`TxHeight`, and `TxBaseline` words.  It preserves the caller-owned
`TxSpacing` word and clears the caller's prior `RastPort.AlgoStyle` effect,
matching the public Kickstart SetFont contract.  Focused coverage proves the
soft-style reset alongside spacing and late-write rollback; tag-list rollback
also restores the style byte when a later font tag fails. Broader
text/provider and native parity remain open ([SetFont autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/SetFont.html),
[AROS `setfont.c`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setfont.c)).

G04/G06/G07 validated-layer visibility closeout (2026-08-12): the
LayersRaster projection now passes its computed clip-fragment visibility
predicate into the supported portable Text, Draw, PolyDraw, RectFill, SetRast,
EraseRect, ScrollRaster, BltPattern, DrawEllipse, ClearEOL, and ClearScreen
operations.  Hidden fragments are therefore skipped during both destination
preflight and publication instead of relying only on the virtual bitmap
adapter's write suppression; the predicate restores the selected layer-domain
origin before matching the public clip-fragment coordinates.  Focused Text/Draw malformed-late-row coverage
and the 49-test validated Layers boot slice remain green; damage/backing-store,
temporary-raster, and complete provider fallback semantics remain open.

G05/G11 validated-layer template visibility closeout (2026-08-12): the
portable `BltTemplate` path now accepts the same explicit visibility predicate
as the other projected drawing operations.  Validated Layers therefore skips
hidden clip fragments during selected-plane preflight, destination snapshot,
and publication while retaining complete template-source decoding and the
void D0 ABI; direct nonzero-layer and RTG ownership remain provider/native
boundaries.  Focused two-row malformed-late-destination coverage passes with
the template's second row outside the visible fragment.

G05/G08 validated-layer Flood visibility closeout (2026-08-12): the portable
connected-region path now accepts the exact Layers visibility predicate for
destination preflight, snapshot, and publication.  Source connectivity still
reads the projected layer bitmap, while hidden destination fragments no
longer force complete-raster probes or rollback storage.  Focused coverage
uses a mapped seed/boundary pair and a malformed hidden tail row; the layer
Flood call succeeds without touching that hidden destination envelope.

G05/G08 validated-layer AreaEnd visibility closeout (2026-08-12): the
projected AreaEnd path now carries the exact ClipRect predicate through shape
destination preflight, patterned fill, optional polygon/ellipse outlines, and
the rollback snapshot. Hidden fragments therefore remain provider-owned while
the collector reset and temporary-raster ownership stay in the shared
transaction. Existing area/copper parity and the 49-test Layers boot slice
remain green; damage/backing-store and full provider fallback remain open.

G15/G17 viewport-palette ownership closeout (2026-08-12): synthetic
`CloseScreen` now validates the embedded `ViewPort.ColorMap` pointer against
the compatibility-owned palette before releasing it or clearing the viewport.
A provider-replaced or unreadable ColorMap keeps the close request unclaimed,
preserves the active view and foreign link, and allows teardown after the
provider restores the original map. Focused host coverage proves both refusal
and successful retry; native/public-screen and CyberGraphX palette ownership
remain outside this compatibility session.

G15/G17 embedded-bitmap ownership closeout (2026-08-12): synthetic
`CloseScreen` now also compares the public `Screen.BitMap` geometry, flags,
depth, and declared plane pointers with the compatibility backing bitmap before
releasing storage or clearing links. A provider-repointed plane therefore keeps
the active view and foreign pointer intact until it is restored. Focused host
coverage proves the refusal/retry transaction; custom bitmap and CyberGraphX
scanout ownership remain provider-owned.

G15/G17 ChangeVPBitMap row-geometry closeout (2026-08-12): the portable swap
boundary now retains `BitMap.Rows` in its validated layout and requires a live
viewport replacement to match stride, depth, and established row count before
publishing `RasInfo.BitMap`. A zero-row current header remains an assembling
viewport exception, while a non-zero current envelope rejects a height mismatch
without changing the guest association. Focused coverage proves refusal and
retry with the corrected row count; complete display-database/profile
conformance remains open.

G18 internal display-vector ownership closeout (2026-08-12): the portable
display database now recognizes `DTAG_VEC` (`0x80004000`) as the V39/V40
monitor-driver-only query chunk and declines it before resolving a mode or
touching guest memory. The public `DTAG_DISP`/`DTAG_DIMS`/`DTAG_MNTR`/
`DTAG_NAME` records and zero-result behavior for genuinely unknown public tags
are unchanged. Direct and register-level regressions prove that D0 and the
remaining call frame stay intact for a future resident monitor/provider to
claim the internal `VecInfo` path; full native monitor-vector publication
remains open.

G19 pixel-array padding closeout (2026-08-12): the V36 byte-per-pen helpers
now widen the 16-pixel row-padding arithmetic before rounding. A rectangle
whose logical width would round past the 32-bit guest stride contract is
declined before array or planar access, so a maximal endpoint span cannot wrap
to a small stride and accidentally enter the conversion path. The focused
pure regression preserves the source sentinel and the existing clipped-count
and malformed-array behavior; remaining bitmap utility parity remains open.

G17 viewport-aware bitmap-swap closeout (2026-08-12):
`CopperStartGraphicsDisplayAdapter.ChangeViewPortBitMap` now reports and uses
the viewport-specific rebuild callbacks before the generic display rebuild
fallback, for both untimed and timed `ChangeVPBitMap` paths. The timed bridge
keeps the supplied cycle while carrying the viewport identity to the host.
Focused adapter coverage proves the narrow callback wins and the generic path
is not spuriously invoked; broader frame ownership, DBufInfo delivery, and
native multi-viewport parity remain open.

G06/G07 zero-mask `DrawEllipse` closeout (2026-08-12): the portable ellipse
writer now succeeds as a no-op when no RastPort planes are selected, even if
the requested non-layered outline lies outside the bitmap. Focused coverage
preserves the destination sentinel and confirms nonzero-mask ellipses retain
the documented no-clipping failure boundary; layer damage/clipping remains
provider-owned.

G08 zero-mask `AreaEnd` closeout (2026-08-12): a decoded non-empty area stream
now consumes and resets its `AreaInfo` collector successfully when
`RastPort.Mask` is zero, without probing out-of-raster shape bounds, pattern
storage, or temporary-raster capacity that cannot produce destination writes.
Focused coverage uses an ellipse outside the bitmap and a plane span ending
at the guest boundary; nonzero-mask AreaEnd keeps its strict no-clipping and
transactional rollback behavior, while layer damage remains provider-owned.

G07 `INVERSVID|JAM1` `RectFill` closeout (2026-08-12): the null-pattern
rectangle path now recognizes the empty inverse-video source and completes
without probing or mutating selected planes. The rule is limited to the
implicit all-one source with no external stencil; JAM2, explicit stencils,
and non-empty area patterns retain their ordinary pattern/destination
preflight. Focused coverage uses a plane span crossing the guest boundary and
confirms the successful no-write result; broader draw-mode and provider
parity gates remain open ([AROS `RectFill`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/rectfill.c)).

G08 `INVERSVID|JAM1` `AreaEnd` closeout (2026-08-12): decoded non-empty area
streams now consume and reset their `AreaInfo` collector without allocating or
probing temporary/destination storage when the null pattern selects no fill
cells. Focused coverage uses a valid ellipse and a plane span crossing the
guest boundary; JAM2 and explicit-pattern fills retain strict shape bounds,
pattern validation, and rollback, while layer damage remains provider-owned.

G07 SetRast zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-12): a validated
`RastPort.Mask == 0` now completes `SetRast` as a bounded success without
walking the complete logical bitmap. Focused coverage uses maximum 16-bit
width/height geometry with an unmapped plane span; nonzero-mask SetRast keeps
its complete destination preflight and transactional rollback, while layered
visibility remains provider-owned.

G07 ScrollRaster zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-12): validated
`ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` requests with `RastPort.Mask == 0` now
complete without staging source pixels or probing source planes. Focused
coverage uses maximum guest geometry and a signed-WORD rectangle that would
otherwise require an impractical staging walk; nonzero-mask scroll behavior,
vacated-area backfill, and rollback remain unchanged.

G07 clear-vector zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-12): the shared
`FillRectangle` writer now completes `ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` destination
writes as bounded successes when `RastPort.Mask == 0`, after their public
RastPort/BitMap validation. Focused coverage uses maximum 16-bit bitmap
geometry with an unmapped plane span and confirms that line-pattern state is
still published; nonzero-mask clears retain clipped preflight, snapshot, and
rollback behavior.

G06/G19 pixel-array zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): validated
`WritePixelLine8`, `WritePixelArray8`, and `WriteChunkyPixels` requests with
`RastPort.Mask == 0` now return their documented zero-count success without
staging a potentially enormous padded source array or probing selected-plane
storage. Direct and CopperStart gateway coverage uses maximum guest geometry,
an unmapped plane span, and an unreadable source envelope while preserving
D0/cycles; nonzero-mask conversion retains its complete preflight and
transactional destination path.

G19 `ReadPixelArray8` aliasing closeout (2026-08-13): the portable reader now
stages the complete logical planar sample set before publishing chunky output.
An output array that overlaps a source plane therefore cannot mutate later
samples during the same call. Direct and CopperStart coverage verifies the
same clipped count and bytes; the null/non-null temporary-RastPort ownership
boundary remains unchanged.

G04/G06 text zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): validated `Text`
requests with `RastPort.Mask == 0` now consume the character stream and
publish the clipped cursor/line state without traversing glyph cells,
background, underline, or planar destination pixels. Focused coverage uses a
maximum-size inline glyph and confirms the bounded success; nonzero-mask text
retains complete glyph-strike/destination preflight and rollback semantics.

G11 `BltTemplate` zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): validated
zero-mask template calls now return the documented void success without
allocating/staging a maximum-size template rectangle or probing planar
destination storage. Direct and register-level coverage preserves D0/cycles;
nonzero-mask template conversion retains complete source/destination
preflight and rollback semantics.

G11 `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-13):
validated masked bitmap-to-RastPort calls now defer external stencil probing
until an effective destination plane is selected. Direct and CopperStart
register coverage uses maximum guest geometry with an unmapped stencil and
plane span, preserving void/D0 success and cycles; nonzero effective masks
retain complete stencil, source, destination, and rollback preflight.

G08 zero-mask `Flood` boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): validated flood
requests now return their BOOL success after the public seed envelope when
`RastPort.Mask == 0`, without inspecting optional `TmpRas`/area-pattern
storage, probing the complete bitmap, or allocating connected-region scratch.
Direct and CopperStart register coverage uses maximum guest geometry and an
unmapped plane; nonzero-mask flood retains complete source, pattern,
temporary-raster, snapshot, and rollback preflight.

G07/G11 zero-mask `BltPattern` boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): validated
pattern rectangles now return their void success after the public rectangle
and RastPort/BitMap envelope when `RastPort.Mask == 0`, without probing an
external stencil or area-pattern source. Direct and CopperStart register
coverage uses maximum guest geometry and unmapped sources; selected-plane
pattern paths retain complete stencil, pattern, destination, and rollback
preflight.

G06 zero-mask `Draw`/`PolyDraw` boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): validated
connected line operations now publish cursor, `FRST_DOT`, and line-pattern
phase state without traversing Bresenham samples when no destination plane is
selected. Direct and CopperStart register coverage consumes a maximal point
stream with signed-WORD endpoint extremes; selected-plane traversal and
transactional rollback remain unchanged.

G11 `BltClear` span-guard closeout (2026-08-13): validated clear requests now
 reject total row spans larger than the portable transactional staging limit
 before entering byte preflight. Direct and CopperStart register coverage uses
 maximum even row geometry, preserves D0 on gateway decline, and prevents a
 multi-billion-byte host walk; ordinary clears retain complete preflight and
 rollback semantics.

G06 `SetRast` span-guard closeout (2026-08-13): validated nonzero-mask
`SetRast` requests now reject a complete selected-plane span larger than the
portable transactional staging limit before probing or snapshotting it.
Region snapshots apply the same selected-plane bound. Maximum even row
geometry is covered with an unavailable plane; zero-mask and provider-clipped
paths retain their bounded no-op/visibility-aware behavior.

G08 temporary-raster probe closeout (2026-08-13): shared contiguous/row-span
consumer probes reject a guest byte span above the portable `Int32.MaxValue`
limit before entering byte-by-byte validation. The `InitTmpRas` constructor
itself only validates and snapshots its descriptor, matching the resident
field writes; a maximum ULONG or unmapped backing pointer is published there,
while AreaEnd/Flood/Text retain the bounded consumer checks. Ordinary
caller-owned temporary rasters and allocator-backed area/flood scratch retain
their existing validation and rollback paths.

G05/G07 region-preflight closeout (2026-08-13): shared planar region probes
and snapshots now bound both ordinary byte spans and visibility-aware pixel
walks before entering their loops. `ClearScreen` coverage exercises a
maximum-height, eight-plane display envelope whose remaining full-width span
is rejected without a multi-billion-byte walk; ordinary clipped and
provider-visible regions retain their transactional behavior.

G07 `SetRast` pixel-walk closeout (2026-08-13): the complete-raster fill now
rejects a non-layered bitmap whose logical width × height exceeds the portable
transactional staging limit, even when each individual plane's byte span still
fits in `Int32`. This keeps the later per-pixel publication loop from entering
a multi-billion-sample host walk. Direct and CopperStart register coverage
preserves D0/cycles on the bounded decline; zero-mask and provider-visible
paths retain their existing no-op/visibility-aware behavior.

G04 text-work closeout (2026-08-13): nonzero-mask `Text` now bounds the
aggregate host work implied by glyph strikes, styled cell rendering, bold
smear, JAM2 background fill, and underline before destination preflight. The
font-strike validator applies the same limit to decoded glyph bytes before
row-by-row probing. A maximal inline glyph therefore declines before entering
the nested cell loops, while zero-mask text still decodes the stream and
publishes cursor/line state. Direct and CopperStart coverage preserves the
void-vector D0/cycle fallback boundary.

G03/G04 text-metric count closeout (2026-08-13): validated `TextLength`,
`TextExtent`, and non-empty `TextFit` requests now reject a character count
above the portable `Int32.MaxValue` work contract before entering their guest
stream/glyph loops. Coverage uses a still-addressable ULONG span, a sentinel
TextExtent, and direct plus CopperStart invocations to prove no host walk,
no partial extent publication, and preserved D0/cycles. `TextFit`'s existing
alternate-height no-fit shortcut remains ahead of the budget gate.

G05/G07 region pixel-walk closeout (2026-08-13): ordinary planar region
preflight and rollback snapshots now reject logical touched-pixel counts above
the portable `Int32.MaxValue` work contract, in addition to their selected
byte-span guard. Direct and CopperStart `ClearScreen` coverage uses a
65536-by-65535 bitmap whose one-plane bytes still fit but whose publication
walk does not; the call declines before the unavailable plane is probed and
preserves D0/cycles. Layer visibility and zero-mask paths remain explicitly
bounded by their existing provider/no-op rules.

G05/G07 visibility-snapshot closeout (2026-08-13): the direct visibility-aware
`SetRast` rollback helper now rejects a full logical bitmap walk above the
portable `Int32.MaxValue` budget before calling the provider predicate or
probing a plane. A focused layered-core regression covers maximum geometry
with an unavailable plane; explicit provider ownership and zero-mask no-op
behavior remain unchanged.

The shared region/snapshot guards also recognize masks that select no declared
bitmap planes as effective zero-mask no-ops, so those calls do not acquire a
pixel budget or walk a host predicate unnecessarily.

G15/G17 CyberGraphX RasInfo-chain ownership closeout (2026-08-13): the
portable host classifier now scans the bounded linked `RasInfo` chain of a
viewport, rather than inspecting only its first node, before claiming OCS/ECS
display lifecycle vectors. A provider-owned bitmap in a secondary
dual-playfield/interleaved node therefore keeps `ChangeVPBitMap`, viewport
timing, copper, and mode-query paths on the CyberGraphX/provider boundary;
malformed or cyclic chains remain unclaimed for native/provider handling.
Focused classifier coverage proves secondary-node detection alongside the
existing wrapped-address rejection; full provider display-DMA parity remains
outside this graphics.library replacement.

G04/G06/G07/G08/G11 effective-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): a
RastPort write mask is now intersected with the linked BitMap's declared
plane depth before text, lines, fills, area/flood, ellipse, scroll, template,
and complete-raster operations choose their work path. Masks containing only
bits above `bm_Depth` therefore publish the same bounded successful no-op as
an explicit zero mask, without staging glyph cells or walking destination
pixels. Direct and CopperStart regressions cover maximal `SetRast` and Text
requests with an unavailable declared plane; selected-plane behavior is
unchanged.

G06 effective-mask pixel-write boundary (2026-08-13): the shared per-pixel
writer now normalizes `RastPort.Mask` against the linked `BitMap` depth itself,
so direct `WritePixel` calls cannot bypass the effective-zero-mask contract
used by the higher-level drawing paths. A mask containing only bits above
`bm_Depth` completes without probing or mutating the declared plane. Direct
and CopperStart coverage preserves the pixel byte, D0, and cycles.

G04 zero-mask text stream bound (2026-08-13): `Text` now rejects a character
stream above the portable `Int32.MaxValue` host-work limit before entering its
cursor-only decode loop. This closes the remaining zero/effective-zero-mask
path that could otherwise walk an oversized guest string despite having no
destination pixels to stage. Focused coverage proves the font backend is not
queried, the cursor remains unchanged, and the direct bounded decline remains
available for CopperStart/native provider fallback.

G07/G11 patterned-rectangle pixel-walk bound (2026-08-13): `BltPattern` now
rejects a maximal signed-word request when the linked bitmap envelope is also
above the portable `Int32.MaxValue` sample budget, before invoking external
stencil, area-pattern, visibility, or planar preflight work. `RectFill` inherits
the same guard through its patterned path, while small clipped bitmaps retain
their extreme-coordinate success behavior. Focused coverage proves the
visibility predicate is not entered and preserves the inverse-video/JAM1
null-pattern no-op.

G06/G19 effective-mask chunky-writer closeout (2026-08-13): the V36
`WritePixelLine8`/`WritePixelArray8` and V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` paths now
intersect `RastPort.Mask` with the linked bitmap depth before the no-op gate.
High-only masks therefore return the documented zero-count success without
staging a maximal chunky source or probing an unavailable planar destination.
Direct and CopperStart register regressions cover the same maximal geometry,
unreadable source envelope, and unmapped plane used by the literal zero-mask
gate; selected-plane conversion and clipped-count semantics remain unchanged.
CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remains outside this portable OCS/ECS claim.

G10 V36 constant source-plane closeout (2026-08-13): `BltBitMap` now has an
executable regression for the documented source-plane sentinels (`0` means an
all-zero plane and `$FFFFFFFF` means an all-one plane). The destination remains
ordinary word-aligned guest storage, the participating-plane count is
preserved, and the portable preflight skips guest probing for the two source
constants. This is a pure OCS/ECS blit rule; layered and RTG ownership remain
outside the portable path.

G09 `ScalerDiv` word-return closeout (2026-08-13): the portable helper now
returns the widened rounded quotient through the documented `UWORD` ABI rather
than saturating it at `$FFFF`. A valid 14-bit-factor product above the word
range therefore exposes the native low-word result; zero factors and zero
denominators still return zero. The focused graphics/lifecycle gate remains
green at 944 passing tests, including direct and CopperStart `ScalerDiv`
coverage; no CyberGraphX ownership is introduced.

G11 masked-blit ownership closeout (2026-08-13): `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` now
matches the Kickstart contract that ignores the destination `RastPort.Mask`
field. The external one-bit `bltMask` remains mandatory and gates pixels,
while all planes common to source and destination participate in the minterm.
The previous portable path incorrectly intersected those planes with the
RastPort mask, which could leave a plane untouched or make a zero mask look
like a successful no-op. Direct and CopperStart coverage now verifies both
plane publication with `RastPort.Mask == 1` and fail-closed behavior when the
external mask envelope is unavailable. The focused graphics/lifecycle gate is
green at 944 passing tests; Layers and CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remain
outside this unit.

G09/G15 NULL structure-initializer closeout (2026-08-13): all seven portable
structure initializers now reject a zero guest base before any range probe or
clear (`RastPort`, `View`, `ViewPort`, `RasInfo`, `BitMap`, `AreaInfo`, and
`TmpRas`). This preserves the native 68000 NULL-pointer/address-error boundary
even when a host memory adapter exposes byte zero. Direct core coverage and a
CopperStart register matrix prove that rejected calls leave guest bytes, D0,
and cycles unchanged, while successful initialization and existing malformed,
word-alignment, full-envelope, default-origin, sprite-priority, and rollback
paths remain unchanged. The focused graphics/lifecycle gate is green at 945
passing tests; CyberGraphX, layers, and display-DMA ownership remain outside
this slice.

G09/G19 `GetBitMapAttr(BMA_FLAGS)` displayability closeout (2026-08-13): the
portable bitmap-attribute query now derives `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` from the same
word-aligned row-stride and plane-start predicate used by `AllocBitMap`,
rather than echoing a stale guest flag. Null, odd, or unreadable declared
planes clear only the displayability capability; public standard/interleaved
classification and geometry remain queryable. Direct and CopperStart tests
cover both misaligned fail-closed and aligned results, and the behavior is
limited to native planar OCS/ECS ownership. The focused graphics/lifecycle
gate is green at 946 passing tests; emulator build and full provider/native
cutover gates remain open.

G09/G19 native-overlay parity closeout (2026-08-13): the existing direct-vs-
ROM-overlay differential now invokes `GetBitMapAttr(BMA_FLAGS)` for both an
aligned three-plane bitmap and a bitmap with one odd plane. The two execution
paths agree on both the displayable result and the fail-closed result. The
focused graphics/lifecycle gate remains green at 946 passing tests; emulator
build remains warning-free.

G16/G17 NULL viewport-copper teardown closeout (2026-08-13):
`FreeVPortCopLists` now rejects a zero `ViewPort` address explicitly before the
generic range snapshot. This preserves the native NULL/address-error boundary
even when host memory exposes address zero, and prevents a malformed call from
clearing low memory or invoking the CopperStart/native teardown owner. Direct
and register-level regressions verify guest copper links, D0, cycles, and owner
callback state remain unchanged. The focused graphics/lifecycle gate is green
at 947 passing tests; the emulator build is warning-free.

G12/G26/G27 status-aware blitter overlay closeout (2026-08-13):
`OwnBlitter`, `DisownBlitter`, and `WaitBlit` are now admitted to
`RomSafeOverlayLvos` after a direct-versus-mapped native jump-table fixture
proved identical D0/cycle results and one invocation of each explicit
status-aware ownership callback. The overlay gateway still tail-chains when
the scheduler/custom-chip backend declines, so a native Kickstart owner is
not swallowed. `QBlit` and `QBSBlit` now have the same conditional overlay
boundary; their queued node execution, completion, cleanup, and beam-
arbitration effects remain provider-owned. CyberGraphX and display-DMA
ownership remain separate.

G12/G26/G27 queued-blitter overlay closeout (2026-08-13):
`QBlit` and `QBSBlit` now join the native-safe overlay after a direct-versus-
mapped fixture proved the packed guest `bltnode` validation, D0/cycle result,
and QBS signed beam-sync metadata through explicit status-aware queue
callbacks. A queue refusal tail-chains to the captured Kickstart vector with
the guest state unchanged. The overlay still does not execute guest callback
addresses; FIFO scheduling, completion, cleanup, and custom-chip arbitration
remain in the CopperStart/native provider boundary.

G24/G26/G27 super-bitmap overlay closeout (2026-08-13):
`SyncSBitMap` and `CopySBitMap` now join the native-safe overlay because their
portable path is a bounded boolean provider boundary with no scheduler
continuation. Direct-versus-mapped coverage proves the layer address, void
D0/cycle result, and callback ownership; a declined provider restores the
captured Kickstart vector unchanged. `LockLayerRom`, `AttemptLockLayerRom`,
and `UnlockLayerRom` now use the same typed Layers gateway boundary: a live
owner's `Completed` or `BlockCurrentTask` result is preserved, while a foreign
or provider-less layer tail-chains with D0/cycles unchanged. CyberGraphX
remains separate.

G20/G26/G27 GELS overlay closeout (2026-08-13):
`DoCollision` and `DrawGList` now join the native-safe overlay when the
complete typed GELS backend bundle is installed. The direct/mapped fixture
initializes the guest `GelsInfo` envelope, verifies callback arguments and
void D0/cycle parity, and confirms an unbound host tail-chains to Kickstart.
Guest callback addresses and hardware sprite/DMA publication remain outside
the overlay; the explicit GELS provider owns those effects.

G24/G26/G27 scheduler-aware layer-lock overlay closeout (2026-08-13):
the final three public vectors are admitted conditionally. Direct and mapped
fixtures compare `LockLayerRom`, `AttemptLockLayerRom`, and `UnlockLayerRom`
through an `IGraphicsLayerGatewayBackend`, including propagation of
`M68kHostGatewayResult.BlockCurrentTask`. With no lock provider, the mapped
handler restores the captured native vector and preserves the guest D0/cycle
state. The continuation remains owned by Layers/CopperStart, and no
CyberGraphX implementation is introduced.

G05/G17/G26/G27 scheduler-aware Layers raster overlay closeout (2026-08-13):
the native overlay now consults `IGraphicsLayerGatewayBackend` for layered
RastPort vectors before the ordinary portable adapter, matching
`InvokeGateway` for direct host dispatch. Provider claims preserve the exact
guest register/cycle frame and any scheduler result; a foreign or declined
layer endpoint tail-chains to the captured Kickstart vector. Focused direct-
versus-mapped `Draw` coverage exercises both a successful provider claim and
a decline with native program-counter/D0/cycle preservation. The raster
boundary remains Layers-owned; CyberGraphX is unchanged.

G14/G26/G27 `VTAG_IMMEDIATE` transaction closeout (2026-08-13):
`VideoControl` now treats `VTAG_IMMEDIATE` as a deferred four-byte result
request. Its word-aligned output pointer is range-preflighted before any
ColorMap mutation,
the result is published only after the complete tag transaction succeeds, and
the portable owner reports `1` when a setter or other copper-affecting change
requires the caller's normal viewport remake. Pure immediate requests and
read-only V40 query batches report `0`; malformed output pointers retain the
pre-call ColorMap state and leave the operation available for native/provider
fallback. Direct register coverage now exercises setter, query, pure-immediate,
and unmapped-output cases. The focused graphics/layers gate is green at 961
passing tests and the emulator build is warning-free. Actual copper-list
patching remains provider/native-owned; the later batch-list closeout records
portable `VTAG_BATCH_ITEMS_ADD` append/replay coverage. CyberGraphX is
unchanged.

G14/G26/G27 `VTAG_NEXTBUF_CM` traversal closeout (2026-08-13):
`VideoControl` now follows the documented command-buffer splice into a
bounded second `TagItem` stream, including clean null termination. The
collector validates every buffer envelope before any ColorMap mutation, so a
truncated continuation cannot publish an earlier setter; direct register and
mapped native-overlay coverage prove scalar/GET behavior, D0/cycle parity,
and preserved resident tail-chain ownership. The mapped overlay still keeps
pointer-bearing batch mutation on the provider/native side. The focused
graphics/layers gate is green at 967 passing tests and the emulator build
remains warning-free.

G14/G26 malformed-head closeout (2026-08-13): the VideoControl collector now
has direct register coverage for an odd guest `TagItem` head. It declines
before reading or staging any ColorMap state, preserves D0/cycles, and keeps
the mapped native overlay on the captured resident vector. This makes the
word-alignment boundary explicit alongside the malformed continuation case.
G14/G26/G27 batch-list append/replay closeout (2026-08-13): the portable
`VTAG_BATCH_ITEMS_ADD` path now appends a bounded, alignment-checked guest
command list and replays the enabled list transactionally at `MakeVPort`
before host copper publication.  `VTAG_BATCH_ITEMS_SET` accepts a null list as
the assembling/no-op clear form; non-null lists and viewport/extended-node
attachment pointers are even and structurally readable before publication.
Malformed existing or added chains fail before the batch head is published.
The mapped native overlay continues to decline
pointer-bearing batch setters/`ADD`, preserving provider/CopperSharp68k
ownership of caller-owned list mutation; CyberGraphX remains separate.

G14 VideoControl pointer-boundary closeout (2026-08-13): batch-list SET now
accepts the documented null clear/no-op form, while odd or truncated batch
lists and odd viewport attachment pointers fail before any ColorMap head or
backlink is published. Direct coverage now proves atomic rejection and null
clearing; the mapped overlay retains its provider tail-chain for pointer-
bearing batch mutations.

G17 direct presentation-boundary closeout (2026-08-13): the untimed
`ChangeVPBitMap` host entry now consults the same status-aware display/rebuild
capability used by the scheduler-aware register path. When a host adapter is
present but unbound, the call declines before changing `RasInfo.BitMap` or
invoking the display callback, preserving native Kickstart/provider ownership.
The host-facing direct and timed paths also apply the bounded `ScrollVPort`
viewport envelope, rejecting malformed RasInfo tails and nonzero
`ExtendedModes` before the association changes. Focused regressions prove the
old association and callback count remain unchanged on both declines;
CyberGraphX remains outside this planar boundary.

G17 malformed-capability ordering closeout (2026-08-13): the direct and timed
host `ChangeVPBitMap` paths now validate the complete bounded viewport/RasInfo
envelope before querying a status-aware presentation owner. A malformed native
request therefore cannot trigger a provider capability probe or callback before
tail-chaining; valid unbound requests still decline at the explicit presentation
boundary.

G17 double-buffer capability ordering closeout (2026-08-13): `AllocDBufInfo`
now validates the complete bounded viewport/RasInfo envelope before querying
the display's double-buffer capability. A malformed native allocation request
therefore cannot trigger a provider capability probe or allocate a public
envelope before tail-chaining; valid viewports retain the explicit capability
boundary and allocator rollback semantics.

G17 complete-swap capability ordering closeout (2026-08-13): `ChangeVPBitMap`
now exposes a shared non-mutating preflight for the viewport/RasInfo chain,
DBufInfo ownership/envelope, replacement bitmap, and attached bitmap layout.
Both direct and timed host entries complete that preflight before querying a
status-aware presentation owner, so malformed replacement storage cannot
trigger a provider capability probe or callback. The subsequent association
write remains transactional and retains the existing scheduler/message
boundary for valid swaps.

G03 text-origin envelope closeout (2026-08-13): `TextExtent` and `TextFit`
now retain the current pen origin in their horizontal accumulation when the
first proportional glyph has positive kerning. The strike and movement cell
may begin to the right of the pen, but the published `TextExtent` remains
anchored at zero as required by the classic metric contract. Direct coverage
proves both the unconstrained extent and an explicit-origin `TextFit` result;
the focused graphics/lifecycle gate is green at 975 passing tests.

G06 WritePixel minterm closeout (2026-08-13): the portable single-pixel path
now treats the implicit pixel as a selected source cell and applies the same
JAM/INVERSVID/COMPLEMENT selection used by line and template operations.
Plain JAM1/JAM2 writes deposit APen, inverse JAM1 is transparent, inverse
JAM2 deposits BPen, and inverse COMPLEMENT has no selected cell to toggle.
The low-level planar writer receives only the resolved pen and complement
operation, keeping its mask, multi-plane preflight, and rollback boundary
independent of the public minterm decision. Focused coverage exercises all
eight classic mode combinations; the graphics/lifecycle gate is green at 976
passing tests ([WritePixel autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node048D.html)).

G05/G06 RastPort setter transaction closeout (2026-08-13): the shared
`SetAPen`/`SetBPen`/`SetDrMd` write path now preflights the requested byte, all
eight derived minterms, the line-pattern phase, and the Flags word before the
first publication. A mapped or truncated guest RastPort therefore cannot
expose a new pen/mode and fail only while writing its derived state. The
existing rollback still covers a provider that faults an otherwise mapped
write; direct and register-gateway regressions verify the complete RastPort
snapshot and preserved D0 on that decline. CyberGraphX remains outside the
portable setter boundary.

G07 SetRast address-envelope closeout (2026-08-13): the transactional
`SetRast` plane snapshot now treats a byte span as the inclusive offsets
`0..byteCount-1`. A valid selected plane whose final byte is exactly guest
`$FFFFFFFF` is accepted instead of being rejected by a one-byte-too-strict
overflow check. Direct and CopperStart register-gateway coverage prove both
planes are initialized and the void-vector D0/cycle contract is preserved;
wrapping spans beyond the 32-bit guest envelope remain rejected.

G16/G17 beam-sample ownership closeout (2026-08-13): the status-aware
`TryVBeamPos` core path now declines a display backend that exposes only the
legacy untimed beam accessor. A CopperStart/native timing gateway therefore
cannot claim a fabricated zero sample when no cycle-accurate callback exists;
the explicit direct compatibility helper remains available for callers that
opt into the legacy interface. Focused coverage proves the decline while the
existing configured-callback direct and mapped parity tests continue to
publish the callback result with unchanged cycles and D0 semantics.

G15/G18 ScreenToFront frame closeout (2026-08-13): the synthetic Intuition
`ScreenToFront` bridge now accepts an optional state-aware activation callback.
When present, the callback receives a private copy of the caller's CPU frame,
re-enters the same scheduler-aware `LoadView` boundary, and returns any cycle
advance only after a successful publication; caller registers remain
untouched. Older hosts retain the cycle-only callback. Direct coverage proves
cycle propagation and register preservation, while the CopperStart boot
gateway covers the mapped synthetic-screen handoff.

G15/G18 ScreenToFront ownership closeout (2026-08-13): when a host supplies
the state-aware activation seam, a decline now remains an ownership decline;
the Intuition bridge does not fall through to the legacy viewport selector and
cannot claim a foreign/provider-owned screen after its explicit owner rejects
it. Direct lifecycle coverage proves the decline preserves cycles and guest
registers.

G06 PolyDraw empty-stream closeout (2026-08-13): the register gateway now
matches the classic low-UWORD count contract before inspecting the RastPort or
point table. A zero low word is a successful void no-op even when both guest
endpoints are unreadable or provider-owned; nonzero counts retain the complete
point-stream, line-destination, and layer-provider validation. Direct and
mapped CopperStart overlay coverage proves the D0/cycle result and leaves the
CyberGraphX/provider boundary intact.

G02/G04 CloseFont null-handle closeout (2026-08-13): `CloseFont(NULL)` now
claims the documented idempotent no-op before the native-overlay font-list
ownership guard. An overlay without a rebound guest TextFonts backend can
therefore safely clear D0 for the null form, while non-null handles still
tail-chain unless the explicit lifecycle backend owns them. Direct and mapped
coverage prove unchanged cycles and native return-frame state, and the
existing non-null decline path remains intact.

G02/G04 StripFont null-handle closeout (2026-08-13): `StripFont(NULL)` now
claims the documented idempotent no-op before the native-overlay font-list
ownership guard. The mapped overlay can leave null extension teardown to no
owner without swallowing non-null native/provider handles; direct and mapped
coverage prove unchanged cycles, D0 normalization, and return-frame state.

G02/G04 portable StripFont closeout (2026-08-13): the shared portable font
operation now applies the same `StripFont(NULL)` no-op before consulting the
lifecycle backend. Direct-core coverage keeps a future CopperSharp68k body
aligned with the CopperStart register gateway; non-null extension teardown
still requires the selected lifecycle owner.

G06 RectFill inverted-bounds closeout (2026-08-13): the portable `RectFill`
body now treats `xMax < xMin` or `yMax < yMin` as the Kickstart void no-op,
rather than turning ordinary empty geometry into a native/provider fallback.
Pure and direct-vs-mapped native-overlay tests preserve D0, cycles, and the
existing planar pixels; malformed RastPorts and layered/provider ownership
still decline through their existing boundaries.

G07 ScrollRaster inverted-bounds closeout (2026-08-13): `ScrollRaster` and
`ScrollRasterBF` now treat reversed affected bounds as a successful empty void
operation, matching the classic early-return path. Pure and direct-vs-mapped
native-overlay tests preserve D0, cycles, bitmap pixels, and line state; the
malformed-row-stride gateway fixture proves the no-op does not probe the
bitmap, while non-inverted clipping and BPen backfill remain unchanged.

G07 EraseRect inverted-bounds closeout (2026-08-13): non-layered `EraseRect`
now delegates its reversed-bound case to the same successful empty operation
as `RectFill`, before probing bitmap, pen, or minterm state. Pure and
direct-vs-mapped native-overlay coverage preserves D0, cycles, pixels, and
line state; layered erase remains owned by the explicit layer provider.

G06/G07 empty-geometry ownership correction (2026-08-13): the fast no-op
checks for `RectFill`, `BltPattern`, `ScrollRaster`, `ScrollRasterBF`, and
`EraseRect` now run only after the portable layer field has been validated.
Direct/core calls on layered RastPorts therefore remain unclaimed without an
explicit visibility predicate, while standard non-layered and provider-backed
empty rectangles retain their successful void result.

G15/G18 ScreenToFront idempotence closeout (2026-08-13): the synthetic
Intuition activation seam now returns success without queueing a duplicate
copper publication when the host current-View cache and mapped guest
`GfxBase->ActiView` both identify the owned synthetic View as active. A mapped
foreign `ActiView` deliberately bypasses that no-op and schedules the normal
frame-boundary reclaim, preserving native/provider takeover. Boot-level tests
cover the stable no-requeue case, the replacement case, caller A1 preservation,
and the pending-copper cycle; the focused `ScreenToFront` gate passes 5/5.

G15/G18 boot LoadView idempotence closeout (2026-08-13): the boot-side
`LoadView` path now fingerprints the bounded guest View/ViewPort/RasInfo/BitMap
topology after each successful publication, matching the portable core's
idempotent rule. An unchanged active View repairs only `GfxBase->ActiView` and
does not enqueue a duplicate frame-boundary copper request; an edited public
ViewPort envelope invalidates the fingerprint and queues a fresh handoff.
`ScreenToFront` explicitly clears the fingerprint before a synthetic takeover
when its guest active-view sidecar was replaced, so provider/native ownership
is not swallowed by the LoadView no-op. The focused boot lifecycle gate covers
both branches, and the portable graphics/lifecycle gate remains green at
937/937 tests. CyberGraphX is unchanged.

G15/G18 boot `LoadView(NULL)` idempotence closeout (2026-08-13): the boot
blanking path now recognizes an already-blank stream when the mapped guest
`GfxBase->ActiView` sidecar still agrees. Repeated NULL requests repair only
that sidecar and avoid another queued frame-boundary handoff; a directly
replaced nonzero sidecar continues through the reclaim path. The mapped
`AmigaBootMemoryTests.LoadViewNullDoesNotRequeueAnAlreadyBlankStreamButReclaimsAReplacedActiveView`
regression covers the blank, repeated, and replaced states. The focused
LoadView/ScreenToFront gate passes 42/42, the portable scaffold passes 937/937,
and the OpenScreen lifecycle filter passes 93/93. CyberGraphX remains outside
this standard-planar boundary.

G15/G18 `CloseScreen` fingerprint teardown closeout (2026-08-13): successful
synthetic close now invalidates the boot-side published View topology
fingerprint after retiring the compatibility envelope, including the case
where a foreign active View remains published. The mapped
`AmigaBootMemoryTests.CloseScreenBlanksSyntheticViewAndAllowsFreshOpenScreenGeometry`
regression asserts the cache is cleared before a fresh geometry allocation.
That close gate passes 1/1; the focused LoadView/ScreenToFront gate remains
42/42, the portable scaffold remains 937/937, and the OpenScreen lifecycle
filter remains 93/93.

G01/G04/G06/G07 NULL RastPort ownership closeout (2026-08-13): the common
portable RastPort byte/word/long accessors now reject `rastPort == 0` before
probing the host memory adapter. This closes the host-byte-addressable NULL
object gap across text, state, pixel, line, fill, area, template, and scroll
vectors while retaining the existing odd-address, malformed-envelope, and
provider-decline behavior. `AmigaBootMemoryTests`-style direct/native handoff
semantics are mirrored by the focused
`GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests.AddressZeroRastPortRemainsNativeOwnedAcrossDirectAndRomOverlayDrawing`
regression, which proves unchanged D0/cycles for direct and mapped `Draw` and
`Text`, `ReadPixel`, and `WritePixel`. The portable scaffold gate passes
938/938; CyberGraphX and layer ownership remain separate.

G01/G06 RastPort setter probe-order closeout (2026-08-13): the shared
`SetByteAndRestartPattern` transaction now reads its prior requested-byte and
line-phase values through the guarded RastPort helpers instead of raw host
address arithmetic. Odd and NULL `SetAPen`/`SetBPen`/`SetDrMd` calls therefore
decline before the first host probe; aligned calls retain their complete
minterm, line-pattern, Flags, and rollback publication. The focused
`GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests.DrawingStateSettersRejectOddAndNullRastPortsBeforeHostProbe`
regression proves zero host reads for both rejected forms, and the portable
scaffold gate passes 939/939.

G01/G06 PolyDraw point-table ownership closeout (2026-08-13): non-empty
`PolyDraw` now requires a non-null, word-aligned guest point table before
decoding the first coordinate pair. A host mapping at address zero or an odd
guest address no longer lets the portable path claim a native 68k address
error/foreign-pointer request. Direct-core and direct-vs-ROM-overlay
regressions preserve the original D0/cycle state and leave the RastPort and
planar destination untouched; the low-UWORD zero-count no-op remains
unchanged.

G01/G06 V36 temporary RastPort status closeout (2026-08-13): the
`ReadPixelLine8`/`WritePixelLine8` and array-vector status adapters now validate
an explicitly supplied temporary RastPort only after positive geometry and the
complete padded caller-array envelope have passed the same checks as the
portable conversion body. Odd or malformed native workspace links therefore
decline before the host vector claims the request, while empty geometry,
zero-mask writes, invalid source arrays, and the classic `-1` result remain
owned by the compatibility vector. Direct-core coverage exercises all four
status adapters; the mapped direct-vs-ROM-overlay gate proves unchanged D0,
cycles, planar bytes, and native tail-chain behavior for an odd temporary
RastPort.

G06 PolyDraw aggregate-work closeout (2026-08-13): connected `PolyDraw` now
 bounds the sum of all signed-WORD Bresenham samples across its complete
 UWORD point stream before destination probing or RastPort publication. A
 maximal alternating endpoint stream therefore declines before a
 multi-billion-sample host traversal, preserving the cursor, line phase,
 planar bytes, and register state; the effective-zero-mask state-only path and
 ordinary connected-line phase remain unchanged. The focused scaffold gate is
 green at 943/943 tests, including direct core, CopperStart register, and
 mapped ROM-overlay decline coverage. Full provider clipping/damage and native
 custom-chip timing
 remain open under G05/G06/G17/G24/G26/G27.

G08 Flood aggregate-work closeout (2026-08-13): standard-planar `Flood` now
computes its guest logical-cell envelope immediately after the effective
RastPort mask and rejects any request requiring more than three bounded
logical passes within the portable `Int32.MaxValue` host-work contract. The
decline precedes TmpRas, seed/pattern, plane, snapshot, scratch-allocation,
and destination traversal reads, preserving native/provider ownership and the
status-bearing D0 ABI. The focused scaffold gate is green at 946/946 tests,
including pure-core, CopperStart register, and mapped ROM-overlay fixtures;
full layer clipping/damage and native custom-chip timing remain open under
G05/G08/G17/G24/G26/G27.

G19 BitMapScale aggregate-work closeout (2026-08-13): standard-planar
`BitMapScale` now rejects a destination rectangle whose three logical
sample/probe, rollback-snapshot, and publication passes exceed the portable
`Int32.MaxValue` host-work contract. The guard runs before DDA arrays or the
byte-per-pixel staging buffer are allocated, preserving `bsa_DestWidth`,
`bsa_DestHeight`, destination planes, and the void-vector D0/cycle frame.
Pure and CopperStart register coverage use a sparse near-maximum UWORD
rectangle; the native-overlay fixture confirms caller-owned endpoints remain
unclaimed for the captured resident/provider owner. Full bitmap utility parity,
layer clipping/damage, and native custom-chip timing remain open under
G09/G10/G11/G19/G24/G26/G27.

G06/G19 pixel-array aggregate-work closeout (2026-08-13): the V36
`ReadPixelLine8`/`WritePixelLine8`/`ReadPixelArray8`/`WritePixelArray8`
family and V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` now bound logical-pixel and complete padded
array-row work before staging, planar snapshots, or publication. A
representable oversized request declines before the multi-billion-entry host
walk, while an array envelope that cannot fit the guest/portable contract
retains the claimed classic `-1` result. Pure-core and CopperStart register
coverage, plus the mapped overlay fixture, preserve D0/cycles and leave the
native/provider owner available for the bounded decline. Full bitmap utility
parity, layer damage/clipping, and native custom-chip timing remain open under
G09/G10/G11/G19/G24/G26/G27.

G08 AreaEnd aggregate-work closeout (2026-08-13): standard-planar `AreaEnd`
now sums the logical-cell envelopes of its decoded polygons and ellipses and
requires four bounded mask/rasterize/snapshot/fill passes to fit the portable
`Int32.MaxValue` host-work contract. The guard runs before managed-mask or
guest-`TmpRas` acquisition, destination-plane probing, and collector reset, so
a representable multi-billion-cell shape declines with its `AreaInfo`, D0,
cycles, and planar bytes unchanged. Direct-core, CopperStart register, and
native-overlay fixtures cover the boundary; empty/zero-mask/inverse-JAM1 and
malformed stream semantics remain distinct. Full layer clipping/damage and
native custom-chip timing remain open under G05/G08/G17/G24/G26/G27.

G10 BltBitMap/masked-blit aggregate-work closeout (2026-08-13):
standard-planar `BltBitMap` now bounds the clipped rectangle as four logical
passes for source/destination staging, rollback snapshot, and publication;
`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` uses five passes including external-mask staging. Each
guard runs before overlap/TempA or external-mask checks, scratch growth, or
plane-pointer reads. A full signed-WORD rectangle therefore declines before

Scope clarification for this closeout: the new address-class predicate is
consumed by display-surface publication (`AllocBitMap`, `BMA_FLAGS`,

bitmap utilities continue to use their own portable mapping and provider
boundaries; they do not claim native display-DMA ownership merely because a
bitmap is word-aligned.

and the prior active-view sidecar for both malformed chains. `git diff --check`

codec/API drift, so the new regression awaits a clean rebuild.

the existing Layers codec/API drift (seven/fifty errors respectively), so the
new test awaits a clean rebuild. Exact ROM timing, layer damage, and

fixed cell, checks the centered strike, and verifies signed current-X
