## Validation supersession (2026-08-14)

The interim build-blocker notes above are superseded. The repository's explicit
DOS `freeMemory` callback is now supplied by the existing console test fixture,
and the mapped Text/Flood fixtures encode the real guest ABI (decodable
TextFont metadata; Flood mode in D2). The emulator and test projects build with
zero warnings/errors. The focused complement-ownership set passes 7/7, and the
complete `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests` class passes 1033/1033.

## G19 V36 pixel-line requested-count closeout (2026-08-14)

The line-specific result correction supersedes the earlier blanket
“clipped-count” note: `ReadPixelLine8` and `WritePixelLine8` now return the
requested UWORD width for valid calls, even when bitmap clipping leaves some
or all pixels outside the destination. The portable implementation keeps
array/plane preflight, deterministic zeroed read samples, and transactional
write rollback; the effective-zero-mask bounded no-op returns the requested
line width without staging the guest array. Rectangle `ReadPixelArray8`/
`WritePixelArray8` and `WriteChunkyPixels` retain clipped counts. Direct,
CopperStart, and native-overlay tests cover partial and fully clipped lines;
the complete graphics scaffold passes 1033/1033 after the correction.

## G09 V39 interleaved-allocation failure closeout (2026-08-14)

`AllocBitMap` now treats `BMF_INTERLEAVED` as a required contiguous-storage
form on ECS/AGA: when the aggregate chip block is unavailable, the portable
path releases any nonzero provisional address, rolls back the public bitmap
header, and returns NULL instead of silently rewriting the request into
separate planes. OCS keeps the V39 rule that the flag is ignored and ordinary
per-plane storage is allocated. Direct pure coverage proves both outcomes and
the provisional-address rollback; the mapped Kickstart overlay proves the same
decline chains to the captured native vector with D0/cycles unchanged. The
focused bitmap set passes 41/41, the full graphics scaffold passes 1034/1034,
the screen/lifecycle gate passes 277/277, and both emulator and test projects
build with zero warnings/errors. This follows the V39
[`AllocBitMap` autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/AllocBitMap.html).

## G02/G04 `SetFont` soft-style reset correction (2026-08-14)

The portable `SetFont` transaction now follows the Kickstart contract that
selecting a new `TextFont` clears the previous `RastPort.AlgoStyle` effect.
The selected font pointer, zeroed style byte, and cached height/width/baseline
publish atomically; caller-owned `TxSpacing` remains unchanged. A late guest
write restores the prior font, style, and metric words. Direct, CopperStart
register, and mapped ROM-overlay coverage verify reset, D0/cycle parity, and
rollback behavior. The source basis is the
[`SetFont` autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0479.html).
The focused SetFont set passes 10/10, the full portable scaffold passes
1034/1034, the screen/lifecycle gate passes 277/277, and the emulator and
test projects build with zero warnings/errors.

## G20 AddVSprite system-flag admission closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable `AddVSprite` path now masks the VSprite status portion of
`Flags` to the user-owned low byte when insertion succeeds. This prevents a
previous `GELGONE`, `VSOVERFLOW`, `BACKSAVED`, or `BOBUPDATE` state from
escaping into a new list membership, while preserving caller-selected
`VSPRITE`/`SAVEBACK`/`OVERLAY`/`MUSTDRAW` bits. The status write is included in
the same rollback envelope as the four reciprocal links. Direct and mapped
overlay tests pass, and the existing GELS regression set remains green. The
source basis is the
[`graphics/gels.h` flag split](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node00C3.html)
and
[`AddVSprite` contract](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html).
Validation: focused GELS 9/9, full portable scaffold 1035/1035,
screen/lifecycle 277/277, and warning/error-free emulator and test-project
builds.

## G20 generic extended-node association closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable extended-node registry now applies the generic `GfxAssociate`
contract to all four Kickstart node types. Nodes without public backwards
links (`SpecialMonitor` and `MonitorSpec`) use the registry's opaque lookup
table; reassociation removes an old alias and `GfxFree` removes every lookup
entry before deallocation. Direct and mapped coverage is required for this
unit, while native Alert behavior for foreign nodes and CyberGraphX ownership
remain provider/native gates.

## G21 InitGels sentinel-state closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable GELS initializer now matches the classic sentinel setup: head and
tail `OldY/OldX` values are published alongside `Y/X`, and `head.ClearPath`
points to `tail`. The direct initializer regression covers all fields and the
failure injection test covers rollback after the larger publication envelope.
This remains a guest-layout operation; native CopperSharp68k code can consume
the same 0x3C-byte VSprite structures without a host-only extension.

## G22 AddBob/RemIBob flag-domain closeout (2026-08-14)

The Bob admission/removal unit now follows the `graphics/gels.h` split between
VSprite render/background flags and Bob mode/system flags. `AddBob` clears
stale Bob system state, preserves the user byte, and sets `BWAITING`; the
portable draw boundary sets VSprite `BACKSAVED` and Bob `BDRAWN`, while
`RemIBob` clears those system fields after background restoration. Focused Bob
and animation coverage passes 5/5 and the complete portable scaffold passes
1037/1037; native/provider rendering remains behind the existing GELS backend.

## G23 Compact collision-table admission (2026-08-14)

`DoCollision` no longer requires all sixteen collision-handler longwords to be
resident before walking a valid GELS list. The portable path probes entry zero
as the minimum table envelope and lets each selected higher mask bit perform
its own guarded callback read. A sparse-memory direct regression covers a
one-entry routine-zero collision table; the existing full-table direct and
mapped coverage remains unchanged. Provider/native callback execution stays
behind `IGraphicsGelsBackend`.

The sentinel integrity follow-up also validates `head.Prev == NULL` before
backend dispatch. A direct malformed-list regression proves no collision
callback is observed when a stale head predecessor is present.

G08 `InitArea` descriptor-only closeout (2026-08-14): the portable initializer
now validates only the even, fully addressable `AreaInfo` descriptor and
checked vector/flag arithmetic before atomically publishing the six public
fields. Positive, zero, odd, and currently unmapped buffers are not
dereferenced by this constructor; `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`, and
`AreaEnd` retain their consumer-owned capacity/readability checks. Focused
direct and register coverage proves sparse publication and strict consumer
decline. Source: [AROS `InitArea`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initarea.c).

G08 `InitTmpRas` descriptor-only closeout (2026-08-14): the portable
initializer now accepts `(buffer == NULL, byteCount == 0)` and all other
backing pointer/size pairs after validating the `TmpRas` descriptor itself,
matching the native routine's descriptor-only publication. It does not read or
probe the backing span; AreaEnd/Flood/Text remain responsible for requiring
usable temporary storage and keep their bounded consumer probes. Direct and
register-gateway regressions preserve the void result, cycle counter, and
atomic descriptor rollback for late writes. Source: [AROS
`InitTmpRas`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/inittmpras.c).

G08 zero-capacity `AreaEnd` closure (2026-08-14): the shared AreaInfo reader
now admits the exact all-null storage/cursor tuple emitted by
`InitArea(areaInfo, NULL, 0)` when `Count == MaxCount == 0`. `AreaEnd` reaches
its native empty no-op without requiring a bitmap, temporary raster, or dummy
vector buffer; non-empty and partially-null collectors remain strict. Direct
and mapped CopperStart regressions cover the empty close and void D0 result.

G08 `InitArea` exact-end address closeout (2026-08-14): the constructor now
allows an exclusive vector/flag buffer end at `2^32`, so a valid high-address
collector may place its final flag byte at `$FFFFFFFF`. Ends beyond the guest
address space still decline, and the even-buffer plus complete readable-span
guards remain unchanged. A sparse direct regression verifies the published
vector/flag pointers; the focused initializer, full portable scaffold,
screen/lifecycle gate, and warning-free emulator/test builds remain the
required validation set. The focused AreaInfo set passes 9/9; bounded groups
cover the complete portable scaffold at 1042/1042, the screen/lifecycle gate
passes 277/277, and both project-reference builds complete with zero
warnings/errors. A single monolithic host run still aborts after 1039 passing
facts, so the grouped result is the authoritative full-suite evidence for
this turn.

## G07 `ScrollRasterBF` two-dimensional backfill union (2026-08-16)

The ScrollRasterBF audit found that the apparent signed-coordinate overflow
in its derived strip endpoints is unreachable: every overflow condition also
implies full logical displacement, which already takes the complete clipped
EraseRect path. The reachable defect was the two-dimensional backfill union.
When both deltas were nonzero, the horizontal and vertical EraseRect strips
overlapped at one corner; under COMPLEMENT draw mode the second fill toggled
that corner back. The portable path now narrows the vertical strip to the
source-preserving X span, so each vacated cell is backfilled exactly once.

all moved/interior/right-edge/bottom-edge pixels plus D0 and cycles. Layer
damage, CyberGraphX/RTG, and custom-chip timing remain provider/native gates.

## Graphics gate audit (2026-08-16)

by this audit.

## G09 OCS interleaved rollback ownership closeout (2026-08-16)

The portable `AllocBitMap` transaction now derives its rollback flags from the
published bitmap header. OCS still ignores a requested `BMF_INTERLEAVED` bit
and publishes separate chip-plane pointers, while ECS/AGA retains the
contiguous interleaved contract. If a late plane-pointer publication fails,
rollback therefore releases each OCS plane independently and uses the actual
public envelope shape; it cannot reinterpret the request as one aggregate

## G14 `GetRGB32` zero-count table ownership closeout (2026-08-16)

`GetRGB32` now validates the color range before examining the output pointer

zero-count form has no guest output envelope; non-empty requests retain the
existing even-pointer, readable-table, and transactional rollback checks. The
direct and CopperStart register paths therefore agree without claiming a
provider/native address-error form for a request that performs no memory I/O.

## G18 default screen ColorMap publication (2026-08-16)

The synthetic standard-planar `OpenScreen` path now allocates and attaches an
owned `ColorMap` for every successful screen, including requests that omit

`ColorMap.ViewPort` in the same construction transaction as the bitmap,

allocation. This prevents a later un-cleared `AllocMem` caller from inheriting
stale map fields when the allocator reuses the block, while leaving foreign
or provider-repointed maps untouched. Allocation failure, rethink failure,
and teardown rollback retain the existing provider/native handoff.

## G12 timed blitter FIFO schedule-peek admission

The portable FIFO schedule peek now performs the minimum scheduler admission:
it rejects an in-flight operation and a node whose `SubmittedCycle` is still
in the future, and evaluates a supplied beam predicate without bypassing a
blocked QBS head. A null predicate remains an explicit CopperStart owner
escape hatch so its profile-aware line/frame predicate can run before
`TryDequeueReady`.

`TimedBlitterFifoSchedulePeekHonorsDueCycleBeamPredicateAndInFlightBoundary`
passes the due-cycle, beam-gate, FIFO-order, and in-flight cases. Isolated
emulator/test-project builds and the complete portable scaffold remain the
required verification gates for this scheduler unit. CyberGraphX/RTG,
custom-chip callback timing, and display ownership remain provider/native
work.

## G24/G26 `GfxNew` extended-node publication rollback

`GraphicsExtendedNodeOperations.New` now snapshots the complete allocated
guest envelope before clearing and publishing its graphics node metadata. A
failed clear or late `NT_GRAPHICS`/`SS_GRAPHICS`/subtype/`xln_Lib` write restores
the original bytes, releases the provisional public span, and leaves the
extended-node registry untouched. This keeps `GfxLookUp`/`GfxFree` from
observing a partially initialized object and preserves the shared layout for a
future CopperSharp68k resident path.

`GfxNewRestoresExistingEnvelopeWhenMetadataPublicationFails` passes the
fault-injected clear boundary; the focused GfxNew set passes 4/4. Native
monitor internals, layer backing stores, and CyberGraphX/RTG remain separate
provider/native work.

`GraphicsRegionOperations.NewRegion` now snapshots the complete allocated

allocation, and returns without registering the Region. The shared guest
Region layout remains suitable for a future CopperSharp68k owner; foreign
Regions, layer clipping, and provider-backed storage remain unclaimed.

`NewRegionRestoresExistingHeaderWhenPublicationFails` passes the injected
late-write boundary; the focused NewRegion set passes 2/2. The isolated builds
and complete portable scaffold are the required gates for this unit.

without removing the registry association or releasing the public allocation;

association registry, and allocator therefore cross the guest teardown
boundary atomically while foreign/provider-owned nodes remain unclaimed.

Validation: `GfxFreeRestoresTheGuestBacklinkWhenItsLateClearFails` passes the

the operation to the explicit Layers/native callback. It does not interpret
private Layer, SuperBitMap, or ClipRect storage, and a missing provider leaves
the vector unclaimed for the resident owner. This preserves the separate
CyberGraphX/RTG patch boundary rather than introducing a second backing-store
implementation in graphics.library.

callback-backed gateway cases, and the 1,446/1,446 graphics scaffold run.

## G26 native `InitRastPort` body extension

`NativeGraphicsRasterBodies.BuildCode` now includes `InitRastPort`. The body

## G05/G06/G26 native guarded `PolyDraw` body extension

`NativeGraphicsRasterBodies.BuildCode` now emits a guarded `PolyDraw` body for
the low-UWORD empty form and exactly one connected orthogonal segment. The
body validates the point base, endpoint geometry, one-plane bitmap, JAM1 mode
zero, selected mask, fresh-dot state, and all-ones line pattern, then branches
through the native `Draw` body so cursor and line-phase publication remain
shared. Longer chains, sloped endpoints, malformed state, and richer modes
restore the incoming D0 and use the shared RTS fallback.

Verification: the accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture covers one-segment pixels and
cursor/phase publication, the empty no-read success, and preserved D0/raster/
cursor state for longer and sloped fallback calls. Connected-chain
transactionality, clipping, provider handoff, and exact ROM timing remain
open G05/G06/G26/G27 work.

## G07/G26 native guarded `ClearEOL` body extension

`NativeGraphicsRasterBodies.BuildCode` now emits a guarded fixed one-row
`ClearEOL` body. The admitted form requires a NULL guest Font, cached
`TxHeight=1`/`TxBaseline=0`, a nonnegative cursor, one standard plane, an even
bounded row stride, JAM1 mode zero, and mask bit zero selected. It computes the
current row and MSB-first pixel phase, clears through the row edge, and
publishes `LinePatternCount=15` without mutating public pen/cache fields.
Font-derived heights, JAM2/BPen, multi-plane and malformed forms restore D0
and branch to the shared RTS fallback.

Verification: the accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture covers one-row clearing,
right-edge empty reset, line-phase publication, and cached-height/JAM2/
multi-plane fallback preservation. Full clear-screen geometry, transactional
rollback, provider clipping, and exact ROM timing remain open G07/G26/G27 work.

## G03/G05/G07/G26 native guarded `Text` body extension (2026-08-19)

`NativeGraphicsRasterBodies.BuildCode` now emits a guarded fixed-cell `Text`
body. The body first requires a non-NULL, even, non-wrapping TextFont public
prefix. The admitted slice is selected/non-layered RastPort state, an eight-bit
fixed cell with `Modulo`-strided glyph rows, one standard bitplane, JAM1/JAM2
or non-inverse `COMPLEMENT` modes 2/3 or `INVERSVID` modes 4/5, mask bit 0,
no spacing, and no style/proportional tables. The body preflights
the entire source stream, paints source-one glyph bits in Amiga MSB-first
order, advances the cursor by eight pixels per character, and publishes the
line-pattern/first-dot state. Both foreground-pen bit states are published for
JAM1 source-one cells, JAM2 additionally publishes source-zero cells from the
background pen, `COMPLEMENT|JAM1` toggles source-one cells, and
`COMPLEMENT|JAM2` toggles the complete fixed-cell template with BCHG without
reading either pen. Every richer text or surface form branches to the shared
RTS fallback.

Verification: the accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture covers two fixed glyphs over
eight rows, cursor/flag publication, foreground set/clear behavior, JAM2
foreground/background composition, both `INVERSVID` phases, both non-inverse
`COMPLEMENT` forms (including complete JAM2 cells), whole-source preflight, and
combined inverse/complement fallback with preserved D0, bitmap, and cursor
state. The dedicated
`NativeGraphicsTextRenderingAndFitGuardSelectedTextFontEnvelopeOnAccurateM68000`
fixture verifies odd and wrapping-font declines before any text or cursor
publication. The dedicated
`NativeGraphicsTextPublishesFixedCellGlyphAndCursorOnAccurateM68000` fixture
also proves a valid one-row glyph, MSB-first plane bytes, cursor advance,
line-pattern reset, and `FRST_DOT` publication. Proportional/kerning/style/
clipping/layer/provider semantics and exact ROM timing remain open.

Current validation: the valid-glyph and broader native fixtures pass 1/1 each,
and the graphics scaffold passes 1469/1469. Project-local emulator and test
builds pass with 0 warnings and 0 errors when dependency builds are disabled;
a normal dependency build is blocked by the unrelated missing
`DosFileSystemContextAttributeCore` worktree symbol.

## G15/G17 native preallocated blank CPR/raw construction (2026-08-23)

The first native construction unit now uses an explicit caller-owned resource
envelope rather than guessing an allocator ABI. `MakeVPort` admits an even,
bounded View/ViewPort whose non-NULL `vp_RasInfo` marks the resource-bearing
form, whose `vp_DspIns` points to a bounded CopList, and whose View LOF/SHF
links point to bounded CPR wrappers. Both CPR starts and the CopList `CopPtr`
must name the same bounded raw buffer; both wrapper capacities must be
nonzero. The body writes only the canonical `$FFFF/$FFFE` copper terminator,
publishes both wrapper starts/max-counts, and clears the CopList's public
`Next/System/Count` fields before returning `MVP_OK`.

The body restores D0 and leaves all guest/output state untouched for split
LOF/SHF buffers, odd/wrapped/unlinked structures, absent resources, or empty
capacity. No allocator call, DIW/DDF/bitplane synthesis, display-DMA handoff,
or CyberGraphX claim is made. CopperScreen's existing CPR/raw allocator and
display builder remain the host path; a future native allocator ABI can adopt
the same public layout after this preallocated seam is extended.

Validation: `NativeGraphicsMakeVPortWiresPreallocatedBlankCopperResourcesOnAccurateM68000`,
focused MakeVPort/MrgCop/resource family `65/65`, graphics scaffold `1595/1595`,
and signed native-image audit `892,152` bytes / `45,041` branches / `3,276`
relays / `7` chains / `3,276` fragment boundaries, displacement
`-32,744..32,752`. The broad project baseline remains `4976 passed / 54 failed /
12 skipped`, with failures outside this graphics scaffold. The latest broad
rerun after the preallocated unit is `4978 passed / 53 failed / 12 skipped`

bus-timing, and JIT suites.

The completed implementation unit is the interior full-height
`ClearRectRegion` split above. It admits only a canonical native one-node
Region where `clear.minX > header.minX`, `clear.maxX < header.maxX`,
`clear.minY <= header.minY`, and `clear.maxY >= header.maxY`; it allocates and
validates two replacement nodes before any public write, publishes the ordered
left/right chain, then frees the former node. The replacements are
`[header.minX..clear.minX-1, header.minY..header.maxY]` followed by
`[clear.maxX+1..header.maxX, header.minY..header.maxY]`.  On either allocation
or validation failure, free only provisional nodes and leave the original
Region unchanged. Noncanonical/multi-node Regions and all remaining corner
and hole forms stay on the portable path. The upper-left corner is now native
when `clear.minX <= header.minX`, `clear.minY <= header.minY`,
`clear.maxX < header.maxX`, and `clear.maxY < header.maxY`. It publishes the
upper-right band `[clear.maxX+1..header.maxX,
header.minY..clear.maxY]` before the full-width lower band
`[header.minX..header.maxX, clear.maxY+1..header.maxY]`. AccurateM68000
coverage verifies both relative rectangles, predecessor/successor links,
atomic old-node retirement, and the shared allocation-failure rollback.
The symmetric lower-left form is also native when the clear reaches the left
and bottom edges but begins below the top and ends inside the right edge. It
publishes `[header.minX..header.maxX, header.minY..clear.minY-1]` followed by
`[clear.maxX+1..header.maxX, clear.minY..header.maxY]`; a shorter clear uses
the distinct three-node edge-interior topology.
The upper-right form is native when the clear reaches the top and right edges,
begins inside the left edge, and ends above the bottom. It publishes the
upper-left band before the full-width lower band. The shared transaction's
post-allocation selector is covered by the accumulated AccurateM68000 corner
fixture.

The strictly interior hole is native when all four clear edges are inside
the canonical Region. It allocates and validates upper, middle-left,
middle-right, and lower nodes before initializing and publishing the chain,
then retires the former node. The original three-node expectation lost pixels
to the right of the hole. The new differential fixture exercises sorted links,
signed endpoints, Exec volatile-register clobbering, and rollback at all four
allocations while retaining the old public head. Lower interior clears that
reach the bottom and leave two lower side
bands are also native through the shared allocator; its post-allocation
selector emits the sorted upper/left/right chain. Right-interior clears reuse
the hole's upper/middle-left/lower geometry. Upper-interior clears now use the
same allocator and emit upper-left, upper-right, then lower-full-width bands;
the focused fixture checks their exact relative bounds, links, and old-node

all relative bounds, and old-node retirement.

### G25d — Native `OrRectRegion` disjoint list-growth contract (completed)

The first growth arm must reproduce the portable boolean builder's canonical
result, not merely preserve the union's pixels. Its result rectangles are
coordinate-compressed, vertically banded, and sorted by absolute `minY` then
`minX`; every published `RegionRectangle` is re-encoded relative to the new
Region bounds. Native staging must therefore allocate and validate every new
16-byte public node before changing the old header or chain, initialize all
next/previous links and relative bounds before publishing the new head, then
release the previous owned nodes through Exec only after publication. A failed,
odd, or wrapping allocation must release all provisional nodes and leave the
old Region byte-for-byte available to the portable fallback. The emitted case
is a marker-owned one-node Region plus a disjoint Rectangle, with either
canonical ordering. AccurateM68000 coverage proves input-first ordering,
fresh-node publication/old-node retirement, second-allocation rollback, and
immediate release of odd or wrapping first replacement results.
L-shaped overlap follows only after its two- or three-band canonical result
and rollback have dedicated AccurateM68000 coverage.
